content.title: H03 — Permit to work and SIMOPS coordination — Training
content.description: Complete H03 guided course. Answer six lesson knowledge checks and 20 final questions. A wrong answer requires reading the explanation and explicitly acknowledging the correct answer. Original and remediated scores remain separate. Completion contributes to the company training requirement; practical competence and work authorization remain separate.

explanations.H03_check1: Opening containment changes the activity and possible exposure. The same equipment name does not make the original authorization cover a different method. The appropriate authority must review the change; this course does not prescribe the isolation or opening procedure.
explanations.H03_check2: A permit does not physically establish a safeguard. Missing verification must be resolved by the right people, and an unapproved substitute could introduce another exposure. The crew should communicate the gap rather than fill it with assumptions.
explanations.H03_check3: Physical and operational interactions determine the need for coordination. Administrative separation does not remove a shared hazard, route or control. The same logic applies to a new activity introduced after the first briefing.
explanations.H03_check4: The unresolved change affects the basis for work. A later administrative correction does not protect the crew now. The right operating and permit authorities must resolve the condition through the applicable site process.
explanations.H03_check5: Changing people does not correct a safeguard or authorize a changed condition. A controlled handover preserves the hold and makes responsibility clear. The exact documentation follows the site system, not a universal assumption made by this course.
explanations.H03_check6: Your task's completion does not cancel another crew's dependency. The operating and permit authorities must establish a controlled handback and restoration. The learner does not gain isolation-release authority from finishing this course.
explanations.H03_q1: A permit is bounded by scope and conditions. Similar equipment or a general maintenance purpose does not expand it. Revisit Lesson 1.
explanations.H03_q2: Equipment identity is part of the authorization and safeguarding boundary. Do not substitute an item or change identification to make the paperwork fit. Revisit Lesson 1.
explanations.H03_q3: The changed method can create a new exposure. The original equipment name does not make the new activity authorized. Revisit Lessons 1 and 4.
explanations.H03_q4: A signature does not physically establish the isolation or supply missing verification. The correct technical authority must resolve it. Revisit Lesson 2.
explanations.H03_q5: Testing is a technical task requiring its own competence, suitable equipment and procedure. This course does not confer that authority. Revisit Lesson 2.
explanations.H03_q6: The physical or operational interaction matters, including shared safeguards, routes, systems and resources across employers. Revisit Lesson 3.
explanations.H03_q7: Separate permits do not assess the combined exposure. The coordinator and appropriate authorities must resolve the overlap before affected work. Revisit Lesson 3.
explanations.H03_q8: A link helps only when people understand the dependency and control changes or release decisions. A reference alone is not a safeguard. Revisit Lesson 3.
explanations.H03_q9: The change can invalidate assumptions about energy or atmosphere. The responsible people must establish its actual effect rather than ask the crew to guess. Revisit Lesson 4.
explanations.H03_q10: A future paperwork correction cannot authorize or safeguard current changed work. Maintain the affected hold and escalate unresolved instructions. Revisit Lesson 4.
explanations.H03_q11: A universal duration would ignore site and task requirements. Understand the actual validity conditions rather than inventing one. Revisit Lesson 4.
explanations.H03_q12: Restart depends on resolved conditions and the right authority, not a deadline or administrative appearance alone. Revisit Lesson 4.
explanations.H03_q13: Handover must transfer the facts needed to control work and make responsibilities clear. The folder can support but cannot replace understanding. Revisit Lesson 5.
explanations.H03_q14: Changing people does not fix a safeguard or authorize changed work. The incoming people need to receive and understand the hold. Revisit Lesson 5.
explanations.H03_q15: Comprehension is the aim. Attendance and experience are not proof that specific changed conditions are understood. Revisit Lessons 2 and 5.
explanations.H03_q16: Bound the completion claim to what actually occurred. Outstanding integrity or closeout checks remain prerequisites. Revisit Lesson 6.
explanations.H03_q17: Your task completion cannot remove another crews protection. Shared safeguards and linked work need coordinated authorized restoration. Revisit Lesson 6.
explanations.H03_q18: Records must describe actual events and checks. Fictional examples and backdating create false assurance. Revisit Lesson 6.
explanations.H03_q19: A knowledge result is bounded evidence of learning, not field performance, a permit or proof of company implementation. Revisit Start here and the closing boundary.
explanations.H03_q20: Later implementation and observed results test whether a correction is used and persists. Administrative closure alone cannot establish that. Revisit Lesson 6.

lessons.title: Start here: Permit to work and SIMOPS coordination
lessons.body:
# H03 - Your assigned course

Work through each section in order. There are six lesson checks and 20 final assessment questions: 26 questions in total. Submit your answer to each question. If it is incorrect, a popup explains the correct answer and why. You must acknowledge that correction before continuing. The course retains your first answer, the acknowledged correction, and both scores.

Completion requires all sections and questions to be accomplished, either correctly on the first answer or through acknowledged remediation. Your original score is never replaced with the remediated score. Completing the course contributes to the company training requirement as part of its existing metric, not the entire safety assessment.

All scenarios are fictional. This course does not authorize permit issuing, isolation, gas testing, equipment operation, or return to service. Continue to the first lesson when ready.

lessons.title: Lesson 1 - Define exactly what is being authorized
lessons.body:
## A permit is a bounded agreement

A useful scope identifies the job, equipment, location, boundaries and period of authorized work. “Maintenance in the process area” is too broad to tell another crew which equipment will be disturbed. A better description identifies the specific item and task, the work limits and the related operating system using the site's identification method.

The work description must match the method actually proposed. Inspecting a valve externally is different from opening a pressure-containing connection. Cold work does not automatically cover a later decision to grind or weld. A permit for one piece of equipment cannot be transferred to a similar-looking item because the original identification is inconvenient to find.

The job risk assessment explains hazards and safeguards for the task. The permit records authorization and conditions within the site's system. Neither replaces the other. Technical isolation and testing records establish their own bounded facts. A permit can refer to them, but its signature does not perform the isolation or the test.

Before work, the issuer or operating authority and the person accepting responsibility for the crew must establish a shared understanding of scope. Job titles vary by company. What matters is that the site's authorized roles are identified and the acceptance is real. Being a contractor supervisor does not automatically make someone a permit issuer.

## Worked example: the wrong pump

Noah's permit refers to pump P-204A. The crew stands at P-204B because it is easier to access and someone says both pumps are on the same skid. Noah pauses the affected work. The operating authority must resolve the identity and scope and verify the correct safeguards before the crew touches the equipment. The crew does not relabel the equipment or assume the existing isolation covers both pumps.

The correct response starts with identification, not with guessing whether two similar pumps have common energy sources. A visual resemblance is not a verified equipment boundary.

lessons.title: Lesson 2 - Check conditions at the worksite
lessons.body:
## A completed form is not a physical safeguard

Before work begins, the responsible people must confirm that the permit conditions apply to the actual job and that the required safeguards are established. Depending on the task, those safeguards may include isolation, access control, testing, ventilation, fire precautions, monitoring, rescue arrangements, equipment fitness or particular competent personnel. The applicable site and technical procedures determine which are required and how they are verified.

Read a condition as a commitment that has to be satisfied, not as a box to copy from yesterday. If the permit requires an isolation certificate, check the correct reference and status through the authorized process. Do not infer isolation from a stopped machine, a quiet line or an informal statement. If atmosphere testing is required, the designated competent tester must perform and interpret it under the approved procedure. A learner must not invent limits, reuse an unrelated result or perform testing outside their authorization.

The work party should understand the safeguards it relies on and the limits on its actions. A briefing should identify the job, boundaries, required precautions, nearby work, emergency arrangements, stop conditions and reporting route. Ask people to explain the relevant restrictions in their own words. Attendance alone is weaker evidence than comprehension.

## Worked example: a signature with a missing attachment

Anika receives a signed permit that refers to isolation record ISO-17. At the job briefing, the referenced record cannot be found or confirmed by the authorized isolation authority. A coworker suggests starting because the permit is signed. Anika maintains the hold and asks the issuer and isolation authority to resolve the missing verification. She does not create a replacement isolation record from memory.

The signature may show that someone intended to authorize work. It does not give the crew reliable knowledge of the correct isolation state when the required reference is unresolved.

## Required conditions can become invalid

Some controls must remain effective throughout the job. A barrier may be displaced, monitoring may stop, an assigned attendant may leave, or ventilation may fail. A valid starting condition does not excuse a later loss of protection. Know the activity's specified stop triggers and act when they occur. Inform the permit holder and site coordinator; authorized personnel manage equipment and process conditions using their procedures.

lessons.title: Lesson 3 - Find the interactions between jobs
lessons.body:
## Look beyond your own permit

SIMOPS coordination asks how one activity could change another activity's risks or controls. Two jobs can interact even when their equipment numbers differ. Shared air space, drains, access routes, power, lifting areas, emergency routes, isolation boundaries or operating systems can connect them.

Compare the activities in time as well as location. A nearby job scheduled for later may begin early. A startup can affect maintenance that is still awaiting handback. A delivery can obstruct access needed for an emergency. A crane movement may affect work below or close a route used by another contractor.

Ask four practical questions: What can our work introduce into another work area? What can other work introduce into ours? Which safeguards or resources do we share? Who has authority to resolve the overlap? Answers should identify specific interactions, not simply state that everyone has a permit.

## The coordinator resolves the combined situation

The site's designated coordinator or area authority needs visibility of the relevant activities and their status. Each permit holder must communicate planned changes and restrictions. The coordination decision may separate work in time, move an activity, change an approved method, establish additional controls, or prohibit an overlap. The appropriate authorities must review and authorize any revised arrangement. A worker is not expected to design technical compensating measures to keep two incompatible jobs running.

Linking permits helps people find dependencies, but a reference number alone is not coordination. People must understand which activity depends on which condition and who can release it. “Hot work stops before hydrocarbon transfer starts” is a dependency that must be communicated, monitored and reflected in the site's authorization process, not merely written in a note nobody sees.

## Worked example: two permits, one conflict

A grinding crew is preparing work near a maintenance area. The maintenance crew plans an activity that could release flammable material. Each permit was prepared before the other job appeared. The crews hold the affected activities and notify the area coordinator. The coordinator and relevant operating and permit authorities review the interaction and select an approved sequence or revised plan. Neither crew treats its earlier signature as priority over the other.

The concern is the combined exposure. The course does not set a separation distance or atmospheric limit because that decision depends on the actual plant, task and governing procedures.

lessons.title: Lesson 4 - Suspend and revalidate when the basis changes
lessons.body:
## Know what the authorization depends on

A permit's validity depends on its stated scope, conditions and site rules. Changes in work method, equipment identity, operating state, atmosphere, weather, staffing, access or neighboring activities may affect that basis. Site rules determine the required suspension, cancellation, extension, reissue or revalidation steps. Do not invent a universal rule that every permit lasts one shift or that every shift change requires the same paperwork everywhere.

The safe decision is to pause the affected activity when a required condition fails or a relevant change is unresolved, then notify the permit holder and responsible authority. An operator brings plant or equipment to an appropriate condition using the approved procedure. A stop request is not permission for an untrained observer to manipulate equipment, enter a hazard area or improvise an isolation.

“We will update the permit later” does not authorize changed work now. A handwritten correction made by someone without authority does not establish an approved change. If the relevant people disagree, maintain the affected hold and escalate through the site's designated route. Deadlines and production pressure are information for planning, not evidence that a missing safeguard is satisfied.

## Worked example: a new operating state

The maintenance permit was accepted while an adjacent system was out of service. During the job, operations proposes starting that system. The permit holder cannot confirm whether the startup affects the isolation boundary or the work atmosphere. The affected maintenance and startup interface remains held for review. The operating and permit authorities establish the actual effects and necessary authorizations before either team relies on the revised condition.

This is not an instruction to stop unrelated plant indiscriminately. The responsible authority determines the safe scope of the hold, including connected work. Workers report the uncertainty promptly and stay within their roles.

## Restart is a new decision based on verified conditions

Before resuming, confirm that the change has been assessed, required corrections are complete, safeguards have been verified by the appropriate people, required authorizations are current, affected people understand the revised arrangement, and the designated authority has released the hold. If a required answer is still unknown, the decision is not complete.

lessons.title: Lesson 5 - Transfer responsibility without losing the controls
lessons.body:
## Handover is an exchange of responsibility and information

Shift changes and changes of permit holder can break the chain of understanding. The incoming person needs the actual work status, equipment condition, outstanding restrictions, linked activities, required safeguards, open actions and authority arrangements. The outgoing person should describe incomplete work explicitly. “Everything is in the folder” does not confirm the incoming crew understands a suspended permit or a shared isolation.

The site procedure determines whether a particular handover requires signatures, revalidation, reissue or another controlled step. Whatever the method, responsibility must not become ambiguous. Establish who now holds the permit, who controls the work party, and who coordinates interfaces. If those roles are unclear, the affected work is not ready to resume.

Confirm the handover was received. Ask the incoming holder to explain the important restrictions and dependencies. They should know, for example, that an adjacent crew must remain clear or that a particular operating change is still prohibited. Do not use the outgoing shift's completion of this course as evidence that the incoming crew knows the job's actual conditions.

## Worked example: an open hold at shift change

Lee's crew has suspended work because a nearby operating change is awaiting assessment. At handover, Lee identifies the affected equipment and activity, the reason for suspension, the safeguards that remain in place, the assessment still needed, the linked operation and the responsible area authority. The incoming permit holder repeats that the job is held and knows whom to contact. Work does not resume simply because the day shift has left.

If the outgoing person cannot confirm a condition, that uncertainty belongs in the handover. Recording “not verified” with an owner and a restriction is safer than representing an assumption as a completed check.

## Contractors must coordinate the same facts

A Vendor's internal shift handover does not automatically update the Partner's permit system or another contractor's plan. Communicate through the site's actual interface. If the responsible coordinator changes, make sure the permit holders know who now controls that interface. Translation or other communication support may be needed; a signature in an unfamiliar language is not a reliable comprehension check.

lessons.title: Lesson 6 - Close the work and hand plant back deliberately
lessons.body:
## Finished work is not the same as plant ready for service

A crew may have completed its own task while the equipment is still incomplete, another permit is active, temporary protections remain, or operating checks are outstanding. The work party should report the actual condition, remaining defects, tools or materials, temporary changes and any incomplete work through the site's closeout process.

The permit holder and operating authority must use the applicable handback and acceptance procedure. Required inspections and technical tests must be completed by appropriately qualified people. The status of linked permits and shared safeguards must be checked before restoration. A contractor does not remove a shared isolation or restore plant simply because its own task is finished.

Distinguish task completion, permit closure, release of safeguards and return to service. These can be separate decisions with different authorities. A signed completion box cannot substitute for an outstanding integrity test. Closing a permit in software does not physically remove a tool, restore a guard or confirm another crew has withdrawn.

## Worked example: another crew still relies on the isolation

Two crews have work associated with the same system. Crew A finishes and asks to return equipment to service. Crew B is still working under a linked authorization and relies on the shared protective arrangement. The operating authority must resolve the linked work and safeguards before any restoration. Crew A reports its own completion accurately and does not clear Crew B's restriction.

## Preserve a record that supports the next decision

Record the work actually performed, permit identity and version, relevant changes, suspensions and revalidations, handovers, verification results and closeout decisions. Attribute checks to the people who actually made them. Do not backdate a permit or copy a fictional teaching case into an operational record. Protect personal and confidential information through the authorized reporting routes.

Afterward, review recurring interface problems. A useful improvement asks whether the next comparable job identified the interaction before exposure, whether the coordinator had accurate information, and whether required holds survived shift change. Counting signatures or declaring every action closed does not establish that coordination worked.

lessons.title: Apply the course - two complete worked decisions
lessons.body:
## Scenario 1: grinding and a process opening

At fictional North Pad, Omar holds permit M-31 for work on identified process equipment. The plan includes opening a process connection under the site's approved preparation and isolation procedures. A different contractor arrives with permit G-12 for grinding nearby. The permits were prepared separately. The area coordinator has not reviewed the overlap, and the crews cannot confirm whether the planned process work could affect the grinding area. You are a member of Omar's work party, not the issuer, gas tester or isolation authority.

Before reading the solution, write three things: the unresolved interaction, the message you would give, and the facts required before a restart decision.

### Worked solution

The unresolved interaction is a possible release affecting nearby ignition-producing work, with no coordinated assessment of the combined activities. Two permits do not resolve that uncertainty. The affected activities remain held while the area coordinator and relevant authorities review the interface.

A suitable message is: “Hold the affected process-opening and grinding activities. Permits M-31 and G-12 have not been reviewed together, and we cannot confirm that their safeguards remain adequate when both proceed. Area coordinator, please confirm the interface review and who may release the hold.” Communicate from a safe location using the site method. Do not enter another crew's work area or perform an unassigned test.

Before release, the responsible people must establish the hazards and interaction, select an approved sequence or revised method, verify the required safeguards and tests through qualified people, update or revalidate the relevant authorizations, and brief both work parties. The designated authority then decides whether the affected work may resume. No separation distance, gas limit or isolation method is supplied by this fictional case.

If someone says “G-12 was signed first,” repeat that signature timing does not decide whether the overlap is safe. Use the designated escalation route if the concern remains unresolved. Record facts, not blame.

## Scenario 2: unfinished work at handback

At fictional South Station, a maintenance crew reports its task complete on equipment C-8. A temporary opening still needs final closure and its specified verification. Another contractor has a linked authorization and still relies on the protective arrangement. A production supervisor wants C-8 available before the shift ends. You are the outgoing permit holder; you are not authorized to release the shared isolation or accept plant back into operation.

Write what “complete” can accurately mean here, what remains held, and what you would hand over if the shift ends.

### Worked solution

Report the part of the task actually completed, while explicitly identifying the incomplete closure and verification. Do not state that C-8 is ready for service. The protective arrangement remains controlled by its authorized people, and the linked contractor's dependency remains unresolved. A schedule target does not satisfy either requirement.

A suitable report is: “Our repair activity is complete, but the temporary opening has not had its required final closure and verification. The linked contractor still relies on the protective arrangement. C-8 is not being offered as ready for service. The operating authority must coordinate the linked work and required checks before handback and restoration.”

At shift change, transfer the equipment and permit identities, actual completion state, remaining opening and verification, linked authorization, safeguards still in place, restrictions, action owners and the person with acceptance authority. Obtain acknowledgment from the incoming holder and coordinator. Do not let “end of shift” become an unrecorded transfer of responsibility.

The correct outcome is an accurate, bounded completion report and an unresolved hold with clear ownership until the real prerequisites are met. This scenario does not teach the technical closure, testing or isolation-release procedure.

lessons.title: Final assessment - attempt before reading the explanations
lessons.body:
## Final assessment

Answer the following 20 questions individually. Your first answer is recorded. Incorrect answers require an explicit acknowledgment of the correct answer and explanation before you can continue. The final result shows both the original and remediated scores across all 26 course questions.

lessons.title: Finish H03 -
lessons.body:
## Research and scope

This original VNDRLY course teaches the agreed H03 scope: define work boundaries, coordinate simultaneous activities, verify permit conditions, stop and revalidate changes, and control handback. It uses fictional worked cases rather than reproduced company manuals. The agreed source register identifies the Chevron permit/JSA example and Enbridge GTM Construction Safety Manual as H03 research references. External examples do not confer authority at another company.

Further reading: https://www.hse.gov.uk/comah/sragtech/techmeaspermit.htm
The HSE page provides additional permit-system context. The worked cases, learning sequence and assessment here are original VNDRLY teaching material; the course does not claim regulator or external provider approval.

questions.prompt: The permit authorizes external inspection. The crew now wants to open a process connection to investigate a leak. Is the original permit enough?

options.label: Yes, because the equipment name is unchanged.
No. Hold the changed activity and have scope, hazards, safeguards and authorizations reviewed through the site procedure.
Yes, if the crew promises to be quick.

questions.prompt: A required safeguard cannot be verified, but the permit is signed. Which statement is correct?

options.label: The signature automatically resolves the missing safeguard.
The crew may decide its own substitute technical method.
The affected work stays held while the appropriate authority verifies and resolves the condition.

questions.prompt: Which pair of activities needs interface review?

options.label: Only jobs performed by the same employer.
Any activities that can affect each other's exposure or safeguards, even with different permits and employers.
Only activities using the same permit number.

questions.prompt: A new activity may affect the permit's safeguards. A supervisor says to continue and fix the paperwork at lunch. What should happen?

options.label: Keep the affected work held and obtain the required review and authorization before proceeding.
Continue because a supervisor has spoken.
Let the newest worker choose which condition matters.

questions.prompt: The outgoing crew leaves an unresolved permit hold. What does shift change do to the hold?

options.label: It expires automatically.
It remains until the authorized process resolves it; the incoming crew must receive and understand it.
It becomes optional if the incoming crew is experienced.

questions.prompt: Your crew's work is finished, but another crew still depends on a linked safeguard. What is appropriate?

options.label: Remove the safeguard because your permit can close.
Tell the other crew afterward.
Report your completion and let the responsible authority resolve linked work and safeguards before restoration.

questions.prompt: 1. What does a permit authorize?

options.label: Any maintenance the crew decides to perform
Specified work within its stated conditions and the site authorization system
All work on similar equipment

questions.prompt: 2. The permit identifies P-204A, but the crew is at P-204B. What should happen?

options.label: Hold the affected work and resolve identity, scope and safeguards through the responsible authority
Assume the same skid means the same protection
Relabel the pump to match the permit

questions.prompt: 3. A job changes from external inspection to opening a process connection. What is required?

options.label: Only a verbal promise to be careful
No change if the equipment name matches
Review the changed scope, hazards, safeguards and required authorization before that activity

questions.prompt: 4. A permit is signed, but a required isolation reference cannot be confirmed. What is correct?

options.label: The signature proves the isolation
Keep the affected work held until authorized verification resolves the gap
Create a replacement record from memory

questions.prompt: 5. Who should perform and interpret required atmospheric testing?

options.label: The site-designated competent and authorized person using the applicable procedure
Any course participant
Whoever has a convenient instrument

questions.prompt: 6. Which statement best describes SIMOPS?

options.label: Only tasks sharing a permit number
Only work by one employer
Activities that overlap or share interfaces and can affect one another

questions.prompt: 7. Two crews each hold a permit, but a possible ignition/release interaction was not reviewed. What should they do?

options.label: Let the earlier permit take priority
Hold the affected activities and obtain a coordinated interface review
Start both jobs and compare results

questions.prompt: 8. What makes linked permits useful?

options.label: Their dependencies are understood, communicated and controlled by responsible people
Their numbers are written in a folder nobody uses
They eliminate the need to coordinate

questions.prompt: 9. An adjacent operating system will change state and its effects on your work are unknown. What is appropriate?

options.label: Continue because the first briefing is finished
Ask an untrained worker to infer the isolation boundary
Maintain the affected hold and have operating and permit authorities assess the change

questions.prompt: 10. A supervisor says to change the permit at lunch and start now. What should happen?

options.label: Start because the instruction is verbal
Obtain the required review and authorization before changed work proceeds
Remove the condition from the permit

questions.prompt: 11. Does this course establish a universal permit duration?

options.label: No; validity and revalidation follow the applicable site system and conditions
Yes, every permit lasts exactly one shift
Yes, every permit lasts until someone signs it

questions.prompt: 12. Which conditions support restart after a relevant change?

options.label: A deadline and an unsigned note
Only a new signature
Verified corrections and safeguards, current authorizations, understood briefing and designated release

questions.prompt: 13. What does an incoming permit holder need?

options.label: Only the folder location
Actual status, restrictions, linked work, safeguards, open actions and authority arrangements
Only the equipment name

questions.prompt: 14. An unresolved hold exists at shift change. What is true?

options.label: It remains until the authorized process resolves it and must be handed over
It expires when the outgoing person leaves
It becomes optional for an experienced crew

questions.prompt: 15. What best checks understanding of changed instructions?

options.label: An attendance mark alone
Assuming experienced people know
Affected people explain the restrictions and required actions in their own words

questions.prompt: 16. Your repair is complete, but required closure verification is unfinished. What can you accurately report?

options.label: The plant is ready for service
The repair portion is complete, with the remaining closure and verification explicitly outstanding
All requirements are complete because the deadline arrived

questions.prompt: 17. Another crew still relies on a shared safeguard. What may your crew do?

options.label: Report its completion and let the responsible authority coordinate dependencies before restoration
Remove the safeguard without telling them
Treat its own permit closure as their release

questions.prompt: 18. Which record is acceptable?

options.label: A copied fictional scenario presented as a real intervention
A backdated authorization
An accurate account of work, changes, checks and decisions attributed to the people who actually made them

questions.prompt: 19. What does passing this written course establish?

options.label: Authority to issue permits and release isolations
The course written standard was met; practical competence and work authorization remain separate
That every company safeguard works

questions.prompt: 20. What is useful follow-up on a coordination improvement?

options.label: Check whether later comparable work identifies and controls its interfaces and preserves required holds
Only count signatures
Assume a closed action proves lasting effectiveness

courses.title: H04 — Hazardous energy isolation / LOTO
courses.purpose: Control unexpected startup and residual energy.
courses.practicalBoundary: 29 CFR 1910.147(c)(7)(i), (iv) — Employees with the specified roles in covered general-industry energy-control work; excludes oil/gas well drilling/servicing and the other exclusions in (a)(1)(ii): Provide the specified assigned-role energy-control training and employer certification identifying employee and training date. This paragraph does not prescribe a universal separate independent practical examination. Source: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.147

content.title: H04 — Hazardous energy isolation / LOTO
content.description: Complete guided H04 training: six taught lessons, two worked scenarios, six checks and a 20-question final. Separate first-answer and remediated scores; wrong answers require explicit correction acknowledgment.

explanations.H04_check1: A stop command can leave power, pressure and automatic restart available. The approved isolation procedure must address all relevant sources and establish the required safe state.
explanations.H04_final_1_1: Isolation must protect the equipment being worked on and its interfaces. Wrong identity or incomplete scope can leave an apparently isolated worker connected to live energy.
explanations.H04_final_1_2: Energy sources are independent. Electrical disconnection alone does not restrain an elevated part or release trapped pressure; each relevant source needs its approved control.
explanations.H04_final_1_3: Leakage, connected systems or process conditions can restore hazardous energy. The procedure must establish how the safe state is maintained and rechecked when required.
explanations.H04_check2: Authorization depends on demonstrated task-specific competence and the employer’s system. Written awareness cannot establish skill in identifying and controlling an actual equipment boundary.
explanations.H04_final_2_1: The restriction protects people who may be exposed inside the equipment. Unauthorized operation or device removal can defeat their protection without their knowledge.
explanations.H04_final_2_2: Different systems can create gaps in device control, verification and handover. Coordination establishes whose procedure and roles protect each exposed person.
explanations.H04_final_2_3: A personal device can represent someone still exposed. Removal outside the controlled exceptional procedure can energize equipment before that person is accounted for and protected.
explanations.H04_check3: Removing one energy source can expose another. The isolation plan must control the elevated mass before a person enters its movement path.
explanations.H04_final_3_1: Different systems have different sources, trapped energy and hazards. The procedure must match the actual equipment rather than a convenient universal sequence.
explanations.H04_final_3_2: An operating control can fail, be overridden or receive another command while energy remains connected. The approved system identifies actual isolating devices.
explanations.H04_final_3_3: Trapped sections and blocked paths can conceal energy. Opening equipment as an improvised test can release it toward the worker; verification must use the prescribed safe method.
explanations.H04_check4: A try-start checks a bounded operating response. It does not prove the absence of all electrical, pressure, gravitational or stored-energy hazards.
explanations.H04_final_4_1: The safeguard must be established before exposure. Changes, reaccumulation or procedure-defined stages can require additional checks during the task.
explanations.H04_final_4_2: A discrepancy shows the assumed safe state is uncertain or wrong. Paper approval cannot override the observed condition; the boundary and method must be reassessed.
explanations.H04_final_4_3: Electrical testing can itself expose a person to shock or arc hazards. Instrument suitability and qualified technique require separate practical competence and authorization.
explanations.H04_check5: A handover must preserve the safe state and personal protection through the transition. Informal reassurance can leave a gap in who is protected and who controls restoration.
explanations.H04_final_5_1: Group arrangements still need individual accountability and protection. Joining late does not remove the need to establish the worker’s authorized participation before exposure.
explanations.H04_final_5_2: Isolation is bounded by equipment and sources, not an administrative job number. Expanded work can expose energy not controlled by the original arrangement.
explanations.H04_final_5_3: The incoming responsible people need the actual protection and work state. Counting devices cannot establish which sources and workers they protect.
explanations.H04_check6: Restoration and testing change the energy state. Exposed people must be protected through the approved clearance and re-isolation sequence rather than a quick informal test.
explanations.H04_final_6_1: Restoration can expose people who still believe isolation is in place. The controlled process establishes readiness and communicates the changed state to affected workers.
explanations.H04_final_6_2: The powered test changed the energy state. Previous verification cannot establish the post-test condition; protection must be restored before the next exposed stage.
explanations.H04_final_6_3: Regulatory scope varies: OSHA 1910.147 has explicit exclusions, including oil and gas well drilling and servicing. Exclusion from that specific provision is not a declaration that uncontrolled energy is acceptable.
explanations.H04_final_scenario1: Isolation depends on correct identity and scope. Similar appearance and an unverified claim about a shared switch cannot establish protection for the equipment being touched.
explanations.H04_final_scenario2: A personal protection device may represent someone still exposed. Only the controlled procedure can establish the conditions for exceptional removal; convenience is not evidence of clearance.

lessons.title: Start here: learning, scores and role boundaries
lessons.body:
# H04: Hazardous energy isolation / LOTO

This original VNDRLY course teaches decisions for service-specific: maintenance, electrical, machinery and pressure systems. Its purpose is to control unexpected startup and residual energy. The six lessons explain the hazard, planning decisions, controls, checks, changing conditions and handback. Worked examples and two fictional scenarios show how those decisions fit together. Read the teaching before answering; no live hazardous activity is needed to complete this course.

There are six lesson knowledge checks and a 20-question final assessment. Submit each answer before viewing its feedback. Your first answer remains in the original score. If an answer is wrong, read the specific explanation and explicitly acknowledge the correction; acknowledged corrections contribute to a separate remediated score. Completion requires all sections and all 26 questions correct or explicitly acknowledged after remediation. A later corrected answer never erases the first-answer record.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Identify every energy source and the correct equipment
lessons.body:
Isolation prevents unexpected energization, movement or release during a defined task. Stopping equipment is different from isolating its energy. A pushbutton, software command or emergency stop can stop motion while power, pressure, gravity or automatic restart remains available. Begin with the equipment identity and actual work limits, using the approved equipment-specific procedure and competent operating knowledge.

Consider electrical feeds and backfeeds, pressure, hydraulic accumulators, pneumatic supplies, springs, elevated components, heat, chemical contents and connected systems. A single motor disconnect cannot establish the state of every connected energy source. Identify stored energy and whether it can reaccumulate while work continues.

Worked example: a pump motor is stopped, but its connected piping remains pressurized. A maintenance worker must not treat the stop command as clearance to open the casing. The isolation authority identifies the complete task boundary and required safe state.

### Applying the mechanism

Build the energy picture around the work the person will actually perform. External inspection may not expose the same sources as removing a guard, opening a casing or reaching into a mechanism. Connected equipment can feed energy across an apparently local boundary. The authorized planner uses controlled equipment information and field confirmation to identify those interfaces. If the machine has been modified, the old procedure may need technical review before use. A worker who finds an unlisted connection should report it and hold the affected exposure. The safe response is not to add another guessed isolation point but to resolve whether the whole task boundary and verification method remain valid.

### Decision principles

Isolation must protect the equipment being worked on and its interfaces. Wrong identity or incomplete scope can leave an apparently isolated worker connected to live energy.

Energy sources are independent. Electrical disconnection alone does not restrain an elevated part or release trapped pressure; each relevant source needs its approved control.

Leakage, connected systems or process conditions can restore hazardous energy. The procedure must establish how the safe state is maintained and rechecked when required.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Understand authorized and affected roles
lessons.body:
An authorized isolation worker is trained and designated for the employer’s isolation system and equipment. An affected worker operates or works around equipment controlled by that system and must understand restrictions. These are functional roles, not permissions created by a job title or an online score. A contractor and site operator must coordinate their systems before exposure.

Personal protection depends on the approved lock, tag and control arrangement. Never borrow keys, remove someone else’s device informally or assume a supervisor’s presence substitutes for your assigned protection. A tag communicates a restriction but does not physically restrain an isolating device in the way a lock can; tagout conditions require the applicable approved system.

Worked example: a helper is asked to enter guarded equipment under another worker’s informal assurance. The helper stops and obtains the specific protection and authorization required by the group arrangement before exposure.

### Applying the mechanism

Role clarity matters most when several employers or shifts share the equipment. One organization may operate the process while another performs maintenance, and neither should assume the other controls every worker’s protection. Before exposure, establish the applicable procedure, who coordinates the boundary, how personal participation is controlled and how verification is communicated. An affected operator needs to know the restriction and must not try to start the equipment. An authorized isolation person needs the equipment-specific skills to establish the control. A supervisor may coordinate both without personally performing technical tests. Documenting these distinctions prevents a broad job title from becoming an unsupported claim of isolation competence.

### Decision principles

The restriction protects people who may be exposed inside the equipment. Unauthorized operation or device removal can defeat their protection without their knowledge.

Different systems can create gaps in device control, verification and handover. Coordination establishes whose procedure and roles protect each exposed person.

A personal device can represent someone still exposed. Removal outside the controlled exceptional procedure can energize equipment before that person is accounted for and protected.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Establish isolation and control stored energy
lessons.body:
The authorized procedure defines notification, shutdown, isolation devices, application of protection and control of stored energy. Follow that sequence and the equipment-specific requirements; this lesson is not an operating procedure. Isolation points must actually separate or restrain the energy and be secured as required. Control circuits and selector switches are not automatically energy-isolating devices.

Stored energy may need discharge, dissipation, blocking, restraint or another engineered method. Venting a gauge connection does not necessarily drain every trapped pocket. An elevated part must not be assumed safe because a hydraulic control is neutral. Technical methods and acceptance criteria belong to the competent procedure.

Worked example: a raised machine assembly can fall under gravity after hydraulic pressure is released. The authorized plan includes its prescribed mechanical support before access; the worker does not place a body beneath it to improvise a block.

### Applying the mechanism

Stored energy can remain mechanically even after the active supply is isolated. A spring can move a part, an elevated load can descend and a trapped pressure volume can release. The approved method establishes suitable blocking, restraint, discharge or other control before people enter those paths. It also addresses what happens if the source can return during work. A temporary block selected by appearance can fail or be displaced, so technical support methods must be approved for the actual load and geometry. The worker should understand which controls they must preserve and must not remove one to improve access without reassessment and authorization.

### Decision principles

Different systems have different sources, trapped energy and hazards. The procedure must match the actual equipment rather than a convenient universal sequence.

An operating control can fail, be overridden or receive another command while energy remains connected. The approved system identifies actual isolating devices.

Trapped sections and blocked paths can conceal energy. Opening equipment as an improvised test can release it toward the worker; verification must use the prescribed safe method.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Verify before relying on the safe state
lessons.body:
Applying devices is not the same as verifying the required safe state. The authorized person uses the prescribed test or inspection method for each source, from a safe arrangement. A try-start may be part of a procedure but cannot establish absence of every electrical or process hazard. Electrical absence-of-voltage testing requires its own qualified methods and suitable instruments.

Verification must match the scope and provide a clear result. An unreadable indicator, failed tester, unidentified point or unexpected response means the condition is not established. Do not proceed by assuming the result that was expected. Maintain any required monitoring where energy can return.

Worked example: the machine does not start, but the electrical worker has not performed the prescribed voltage verification. The maintenance lead does not treat the failed start as proof that exposed conductors are deenergized.

### Applying the mechanism

Verification is a test of the actual condition, not a ritual performed to complete the sheet. The prescribed method must address the relevant sources and remain safe if the expected state is wrong. For electrical work, that means qualified testing and protection while parts may still be energized. For process energy, the method must consider trapped sections and the representation of indicators. If a tester is unsuitable, a gauge is blocked or equipment responds unexpectedly, the result is uncertain. The job stays held while the authorized roles resolve it. A signature made before the check cannot override the physical observation.

### Decision principles

The safeguard must be established before exposure. Changes, reaccumulation or procedure-defined stages can require additional checks during the task.

A discrepancy shows the assumed safe state is uncertain or wrong. Paper approval cannot override the observed condition; the boundary and method must be reassessed.

Electrical testing can itself expose a person to shock or arc hazards.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Protect every person through group work and handover
lessons.body:
Group isolation must provide protection for each exposed worker under the approved system. A group list without control of personal participation can lose track of who is inside the hazard. The procedure identifies coordination, device control, verification responsibilities and how people join or leave the job. New participants must not enter merely because the group has already started.

Shift and personnel changes require a controlled transfer that preserves protection continuously. Do not create a gap by removing outgoing protection before the incoming arrangement is established. A change in task scope can require a changed isolation boundary and re-verification.

Worked example: a night-shift worker arrives after the day shift leaves. The worker follows the group handover and personal protection procedure, confirms the actual equipment state and receives the task briefing. An abandoned lockbox with no accountable handover is not a completed transfer.

### Applying the mechanism

A group system needs a reliable way to know who is exposed and whose protection must remain in place. Joining and leaving the group are controlled actions, not just attendance updates. Before a person enters, they receive the required personal protection and understand the equipment state and task limits. During handover, incoming and outgoing roles transfer responsibility without an unprotected gap. If the group cannot account for a person or a device, restoration remains held under the approved process. Do not assume absence from the immediate work area means a worker is clear; they may be in another part of the equipment boundary.

### Decision principles

Group arrangements still need individual accountability and protection. Joining late does not remove the need to establish the worker’s authorized participation before exposure.

Isolation is bounded by equipment and sources, not an administrative job number. Expanded work can expose energy not controlled by the original arrangement.

The incoming responsible people need the actual protection and work state. Counting devices cannot establish which sources and workers they protect.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Restore through controlled clearance and communication
lessons.body:
Return to service is a separate controlled stage. The authorized process checks the work area, component condition, tools and temporary arrangements; accounts for people; handles each isolation device under its rules; and notifies affected personnel. A completed repair invoice or maintenance signature does not itself authorize energization.

Testing that temporarily requires energy must use the approved controlled sequence, including clearing people and re-establishing protection before further exposed work. Never alternate informally between maintenance and operation while workers assume the previous safe state still applies.

Worked example: a technician wants to jog a motor to check rotation while a colleague is still inside the guarded area. The request is held. The approved testing sequence must establish clearance and communication, and any subsequent maintenance requires its specified re-isolation and verification.

### Applying the mechanism

Restoration should be planned while the job is prepared, particularly where testing introduces temporary energized stages. Define how people, tools and temporary arrangements are cleared, who communicates the state change and how protection is re-established before further exposed work. A technician should not ask for a quick jog while another worker still relies on isolation. The accepted sequence may require several transitions, each with its own checks. Preserve any unresolved defect or temporary restriction in handback so operations does not interpret “maintenance finished” as unrestricted readiness. The isolation system protects both the current crew and people who approach after the equipment state changes.

### Decision principles

Restoration can expose people who still believe isolation is in place. The controlled process establishes readiness and communicates the changed state to affected workers.

The powered test changed the energy state. Previous verification cannot establish the post-test condition; protection must be restored before the next exposed stage.

Regulatory scope varies: OSHA 1910.147 has explicit exclusions, including oil and gas well drilling and servicing. Exclusion from that specific provision is not a declaration that uncontrolled energy is acceptable.

lessons.title: Two applied scenarios and worked decisions
lessons.body:
## Applied scenarios: complete worked decisions

### Scenario 1: The wrong skid

The isolation sheet names compressor C-17. The crew reaches C-18 because both units look alike and the operator says one switch serves the area.

**Worked decision and reasoning.** The crew holds the affected work and resolves identity with the authorized operating and isolation roles. The plan must establish the actual equipment, all relevant sources, stored energy and verification. Nobody relabels the skid to fit the sheet or transfers protection by assumption. After the correct boundary is established, each exposed person follows the approved protection arrangement and the task is rebriefed.

### Scenario 2: The missing worker at restoration

A group repair is finished, but one worker cannot be reached. Their personal device remains in the protection arrangement. Operations wants immediate restart.

**Worked decision and reasoning.** Restoration remains held while the approved personnel accounting and exceptional device-removal process, if applicable, is followed by the designated authority. The crew does not cut the device based on an assumption that the worker went home. The process must establish the worker is not exposed and satisfy all required checks and notification before any permitted removal and restoration. Production urgency cannot replace those safeguards.

lessons.title: Final assessment: 20 individual decisions
lessons.body: Answer the 20 questions individually using the taught principles. Each submission preserves your first answer. Review feedback after submitting. When an answer is incorrect, explicitly acknowledge the correct decision and explanation before moving on. The result must show both the first-answer score and the remediated score across all 26 questions. Do not attempt a live hazardous task to obtain an answer; the assessment is a knowledge and judgment exercise.

lessons.title: Completion and separately assessed practical competence
lessons.body:
## What this completion means

The course is complete only after every section and all 26 questions have been accomplished, through correct responses or explicit acknowledgment of the supplied correction. Preserve the original and remediated results separately. Acknowledgment is a learning action, not evidence that the learner has performed the task safely in the field.

## Legal requirements for the named work role
These apply only when you perform the work described below. They are not additional steps for completing this online course.

29 CFR 1910.147(c)(7)(i), (iv) — Employees with the specified roles in covered general-industry energy-control work; excludes oil/gas well drilling/servicing and the other exclusions in (a)(1)(ii): Provide the specified assigned-role energy-control training and employer certification identifying employee and training date. This paragraph does not prescribe a universal separate independent practical examination. Source: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.147

questions.prompt: A pump has stopped after a button is pressed. What is established?

options.label: Only that it stopped; isolation and verification remain required for the task.
All connected energy is absent.
Every worker may begin maintenance.

questions.prompt: What starts an isolation plan?

options.label: The nearest convenient switch.
A similar machine’s photograph alone.
Correct equipment identity and the actual task boundary.

questions.prompt: Which source can remain after electrical disconnection?

options.label: Only hazards visible on the control display.
Stored hydraulic pressure, gravity or other non-electrical energy.
None, because electricity creates all energy.

questions.prompt: Why consider energy reaccumulation?

options.label: A previously reduced energy state can change during the work.
Verification permanently prevents pressure from returning.
Only the first moment of the task matters.

questions.prompt: Does this course make its graduate an authorized isolation worker?

options.label: Yes, for every electrical disconnect.
Yes, if the worker has a supervisor title.
No; equipment-specific training, practical evaluation and employer designation remain separate.

questions.prompt: What should an affected worker do with an isolation restriction?

options.label: Ask an unassigned coworker to override it.
Respect it and never attempt unauthorized operation or device removal.
Test the machine to see if the restriction is real.

questions.prompt: Why must contractors and operations coordinate isolation systems?

options.label: Their work and protection can depend on shared equipment and boundaries.
Each employer’s paperwork physically separates energy.
Only the contractor’s preferred method matters.

questions.prompt: Can a worker casually remove someone else’s lock?

options.label: Yes, when production is waiting.
Yes, after asking any coworker.
No; only the specific approved exceptional process can address such removal.

questions.prompt: A raised component can fall after pressure is released. What must the plan address?

options.label: A warning to move quickly underneath.
The gravitational movement using an approved restraint or support method.
Only the hydraulic gauge reading.

questions.prompt: What determines the isolation sequence?

options.label: The approved equipment-specific procedure and responsible authorized roles.
A generic online order used for all machines.
Whichever device is easiest to reach.

questions.prompt: Why is a selector switch not automatically sufficient isolation?

options.label: Its color is usually wrong.
Only old equipment needs physical isolation.
It may control operation without physically isolating the energy source.

questions.prompt: What should happen to trapped-energy uncertainty?

options.label: Loosen a connection to find out.
Resolve it through the competent isolation plan before exposure.
Assume a single zero gauge clears every pocket.

questions.prompt: Is a failed start attempt proof that every hazard is isolated?

options.label: No; each relevant source needs its prescribed verification.
Yes, including all exposed conductors.
Yes, if the motor is silent.

questions.prompt: When is verification performed?

options.label: Only after the job is complete.
Only when a device appears damaged.
Before reliance on isolation and again at required triggers.

questions.prompt: What does an unexpected verification result require?

options.label: Proceed if the isolation sheet is signed.
Hold the work and resolve the discrepancy through authorized personnel.
Record the expected value instead.

questions.prompt: Who performs electrical absence-of-voltage testing?

options.label: A person qualified and authorized for that electrical task with suitable equipment and method.
Any learner who owns a multimeter.
The nearest unaffected operator.

questions.prompt: What is the essential aim of an isolation shift transfer?

options.label: Remove all devices before the new crew arrives.
Let incoming workers rely on an informal text.
Maintain continuous protection and clear responsibility for every exposed person.

questions.prompt: What must a new worker do before joining a group isolation job?

options.label: Enter first and add their name later.
Meet the approved participation, protection and briefing requirements.
Assume another worker’s device covers them.

questions.prompt: What if the task expands beyond the protected boundary?

options.label: Hold the added work and reassess the isolation and authorization.
Use the original locks because the job number is unchanged.
Ask a coworker to watch the new section.

questions.prompt: What should a handover communicate?

options.label: Only the estimated finish time.
Only the number of locks on site.
Equipment state, protection arrangement, people, scope and unresolved restrictions.

questions.prompt: A repaired machine needs a powered test while people remain exposed. What happens?

options.label: Let workers stay inside if they wear PPE.
Hold energization and follow the approved clearance and testing sequence.
Jog briefly because the repair is complete.

questions.prompt: What must precede authorized restoration?

options.label: Required equipment checks, personnel accounting, controlled device handling and notification.
Only the repairer’s invoice.
Only the end of the shift.

questions.prompt: What happens after a powered test if more exposed maintenance is needed?

options.label: Rely on the earlier pre-test verification.
Assume the test proves the machine is safe to touch.
Re-establish the prescribed isolation and verify before exposure resumes.

questions.prompt: What does this course establish about legal applicability?

options.label: That no isolation requirements apply to drilling.
Awareness principles; the employer must determine the rules applying to its work.
That OSHA 1910.147 applies identically to all oilfield work.

questions.prompt: What is the decisive gap in the wrong-skid scenario?

options.label: The actual equipment and energy boundary have not been established.
The sheet needs a more general equipment name.
The crew should work on either unit to save time.

questions.prompt: What is the correct response to the missing worker and device?

options.label: Cut the device because the repair is complete.
Ask any coworker to remove it.
Keep restoration held and follow the approved accounting and exceptional-removal process.

courses.purpose: Control atmosphere, engulfment, access and rescue risks.
courses.practicalBoundary: 29 CFR 1910.146(k)(2)(iv) — Employer-designated employees performing covered permit-space rescue: Practice the assigned permit-space rescues at least every 12 months using the specified actual or representative spaces, subject to the real-rescue exception.
