lessons.title: Two applied scenarios and fully worked solutions
lessons.body:
## Applied scenario 1: an incomplete decision chain

A long-serving mechanic transfers into an unfamiliar gate traffic-control role and is rostered alone. At the handover, a second issue is identified: The replacement mentor has experience but no competence in the assigned equipment task. The receiving supervisor has the earlier record but does not yet have evidence that the new issue was resolved. A colleague proposes the following shortcut: Remove the restriction to fill the shift. Work is due to begin on the next shift, so the supervisor needs a defensible decision that protects people and preserves a clear history.

### Worked solution — immediate decision

The first response is: Assess the unfamiliar role and provide suitable supervision and restrictions before assignment. The reason is specific: Company tenure does not establish competence in a changed task or local conditions. Determine which assignment depends on that unresolved condition. Tell the affected people the restriction and who is coordinating resolution. If there is an immediate exposure, move to a safe position and use the established warning or emergency route rather than completing records first. The supervisor must not use a favorable overall company score as a substitute for this missing decision.

### Worked solution — resolve the additional issue

For the handover finding, the next action is: Provide a suitably competent mentor or restrict the assignment to supported work. The supporting record should show: A mentor assignment showing competence, availability, supervision arrangement and handover coverage. This is important because supervision is an active safeguard; a name on a roster cannot provide unavailable observation or intervention. The receiving shift needs the actual status, not an assurance that someone intends to finish the check later. Identify the responsible role and obtain acknowledgment of the restriction. If the required authority or expertise is unavailable, the affected assignment remains unready; unrelated authorized work may be considered only after its interfaces are checked.

### Worked solution — reject the shortcut and verify the result

The proposed shortcut fails because restrictions protect only when the people allocating and performing work understand and apply them. The suitable decision is: Stop the allocation and arrange the specified supervision or reassign to authorized work. Evidence for review would include: A current restriction record acknowledged by dispatch, site supervision and the worker. Separate correction of the immediate problem from confirmation that the change works in later comparable conditions. A reviewer should check the actual control used and the scope represented by the evidence. If the same weakness recurs, reopen the issue and retain both the original decision and the new observation.

### What can be concluded

This solution establishes a bounded route from an identified gap to evidence and responsible acceptance. It does not establish that an assessment, clinical decision, technical test or employer authorization actually happened in a real company. The fictional case teaches how to decide and what to verify. Actual release remains with the designated employer/site authority after the applicable prerequisites are met.

## Applied scenario 2: an incomplete decision chain

A trainee repeatedly misses the pre-use defect escalation step during supervised practice. At the handover, a second issue is identified: The release covers all site work although assessment covered one bounded task. The receiving supervisor has the earlier record but does not yet have evidence that the new issue was resolved. A colleague proposes the following shortcut: Dismiss the concern because release was already signed. Work is due to begin on the next shift, so the supervisor needs a defensible decision that protects people and preserves a clear history.

### Worked solution — immediate decision

The first response is: Give specific feedback, practice the escalation and reassess before reducing supervision. The reason is specific: Missing a critical abnormal decision remains a competence gap even when routine performance is otherwise smooth. Determine which assignment depends on that unresolved condition. Tell the affected people the restriction and who is coordinating resolution. If there is an immediate exposure, move to a safe position and use the established warning or emergency route rather than completing records first. The supervisor must not use a favorable overall company score as a substitute for this missing decision.

### Worked solution — resolve the additional issue

For the handover finding, the next action is: Limit authorization to the demonstrated scope and assess additional tasks before expansion. The supporting record should show: A documented release decision referencing observed performance, remaining limits and authorizer. This is important because elapsed time is not evidence that the required performance standard has been met. The receiving shift needs the actual status, not an assurance that someone intends to finish the check later. Identify the responsible role and obtain acknowledgment of the restriction. If the required authority or expertise is unavailable, the affected assignment remains unready; unrelated authorized work may be considered only after its interfaces are checked.

### Worked solution — reject the shortcut and verify the result

The proposed shortcut fails because an earlier release remains bounded by its assessed scope; changed work can require new support. The suitable decision is: Review the changed task and restore appropriate support pending relevant assessment. Evidence for review would include: A changed-task review linking prior competence, new gaps and revised supervision conditions. Separate correction of the immediate problem from confirmation that the change works in later comparable conditions. A reviewer should check the actual control used and the scope represented by the evidence. If the same weakness recurs, reopen the issue and retain both the original decision and the new observation.

### What can be concluded

This solution establishes a bounded route from an identified gap to evidence and responsible acceptance. It does not establish that an assessment, clinical decision, technical test or employer authorization actually happened in a real company. The fictional case teaches how to decide and what to verify. Actual release remains with the designated employer/site authority after the applicable prerequisites are met.

lessons.title: Final assessment — twenty questions
lessons.body: Answer each question individually. Apply the taught decisions to the facts given. Your first choices are retained. If an answer is wrong, read the specific explanation and explicitly acknowledge the corrected answer. A corrected score records learning after feedback; it does not overwrite the first-answer result. All twenty final questions and all six lesson checks must be completed.

lessons.title: Finish — separate practical qualification
lessons.body:
## Written completion and what it proves

Completion requires all 26 answered correctly or acknowledged remediation. Both first-answer and remediated scores remain separate. Completing the guided course is evidence that you worked through its knowledge and decision questions; it is not an observed practical performance result, a legal license, a provider certification or an employer authorization. Training evidence contributes to review within its scope and validity, rather than automatically establishing the whole company program.

## What needs separate assessment

The assessment should test recognition of an abnormal condition as well as routine performance. A person who can repeat a procedure but cannot identify when to stop has not demonstrated the whole task. Employer authorization should state the person, tasks, equipment or site limits, required supervision and the basis for the decision. Applicable legal, issuer, client and change-trigger requirements govern validity; this course invents no universal renewal period.

## Before actual work

Confirm current local instructions, reporting routes, emergency arrangements and the person who can resolve an operating hold. If assigned work exceeds your assessed scope, say so before accepting it. The Partner's job/site readiness decision remains separate from the company's evidence review. Preserve real records through the authorized process and protect personal information. The fictional examples in this course must never be submitted as evidence that your company performed the actions described.

lessons.title: Start here — Training delivery and practical assessor assurance
lessons.body:
Prevent attendance certificates from being mistaken for competence. This course teaches the decisions needed to implement that purpose in field operations. It covers trainer/assessor suitability, objectives, accessible delivery, evaluation and retraining. The examples involve fictional oilfield crews and companies; none is a real incident record or evidence of a company's implementation.

Read six substantive lessons, answer each attached knowledge check, then study two applied cases and answer the twenty final questions. Every question has three choices and one correct answer. The course records the first answer separately from any correction. Completion requires all 26 answered correctly or acknowledged remediation, including reading the specific explanation for each correction. A remediated result must never replace the original score. There is no speed requirement: take the time needed to explain the decision in your own words.

The audience includes workers who recognize gaps, supervisors who coordinate work and program owners who maintain the system. Each has a different decision boundary. An observer may report an uncertain safeguard without personally being qualified to repair it. A supervisor may coordinate a hold without being the person authorized to clear a technical prerequisite. Learn both the action and the limit on that action.

lessons.title: Lesson 1 — Define measurable learning and performance objectives
lessons.body:
## Define measurable learning and performance objectives

An objective says what the learner must explain or demonstrate and under which conditions. Distinguish knowledge, practical skill and employer authorization. Reading a method can support understanding; performing it safely requires observation by someone capable of judging it. Identify critical steps and abnormal decisions before choosing a course. A provider's impressive catalogue does not show that a particular course covers your actual task.

### Deeper application

An assessable objective might require identifying a defect and selecting the safe escalation route under stated conditions. Understand equipment is too vague to determine success. Define the knowledge to explain, the performance to observe and the limits of the assessment environment. A course may legitimately cover awareness only if that boundary is explicit and the employer arranges the additional required qualification separately.

### Worked oilfield example

A purchased operator course promises competence but lists only attendance and a reading quiz.

This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: A course-to-task mapping distinguishing knowledge results from observed performance criteria. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that the mapping omits the task's defect and stop decisions. The appropriate correction is to add relevant abnormal decisions and ensure they are taught and appropriately assessed. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

An implementation record and a later effectiveness check answer different questions. The first shows whether the required action occurred within the stated scope. The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. In this example, the follow-up should return to the actual gap described above, rather than simply asking whether the file now looks complete. A genuine unknown must remain visible until resolved by appropriate evidence.

lessons.title: Lesson 2 — Select suitable trainers and assessors
lessons.body:
## Select suitable trainers and assessors

A good operator may need support to teach; a skilled presenter may lack the technical competence to assess. Verify provider and assessor scope for the actual equipment and environment. For U.S. powered industrial trucks, the applicable OSHA rule specifically requires trainers and evaluators with suitable knowledge, training and experience. Do not generalize that example into one universal credential for every role.

### Deeper application

Review an assessor's suitability against the judgment they will make. Relevant operating experience supports technical recognition; instructional skill supports learning; assessment skill supports consistent observation and feedback. These qualities can be shared across a teaching team, but the practical signatory must be suitable for the result claimed. A provider's brand or a presenter's confidence cannot stand in for evidence of relevant competence.

### Worked oilfield example

A provider assigns a polished instructor with no relevant equipment experience to judge practical operation.

Assessment quality depends on the evaluator's ability to recognize safe and unsafe performance in that task. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: Verified assessor suitability linked to the specific task and equipment scope. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that the assessor's experience covers different equipment with materially different operating demands. The appropriate correction is to verify matching competence or appoint an appropriately qualified evaluator. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

An implementation record and a later effectiveness check answer different questions. The first shows whether the required action occurred within the stated scope. The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. In this example, the follow-up should return to the actual gap described above, rather than simply asking whether the file now looks complete. lessons.title: Lesson 3 — Deliver accessible current instruction safely
lessons.body:
## Deliver accessible current instruction safely

Teach using current relevant material, understandable language and appropriate equipment. Practice must be controlled and supervised; assessment is not permission to expose learners to danger. Use safe simulation for abnormal judgment where needed. Check that the worker understands technical terms rather than merely repeating them. If the operational method changes during the course, evaluate and communicate the change before continuing dependent practice.

### Deeper application

Safe practice has prerequisites: suitable equipment, controlled surroundings, appropriate supervision and clear stop conditions. A simulation should faithfully test the intended judgment without claiming to demonstrate capabilities it cannot validly assess. For example, a tabletop exercise can test communication decisions but not establish physical equipment handling. Record that limitation so the employer does not treat every completed exercise as equivalent practical evidence.

### Worked oilfield example

A training exercise proposes disabling an actual guard so the candidate can demonstrate detecting the hazard. The decision is to use a safe simulation or other suitable method without defeating the operational safeguard.

Training must not create the hazardous exposure it is meant to prevent. Instructor presence does not make a defeated safeguard acceptable. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: A safe lesson plan identifying current material, accessible delivery and controlled practice conditions. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that the translated lesson uses obsolete equipment controls. The appropriate correction is to correct the technical content and verify understood instruction before further practice. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. lessons.title: Lesson 4 — Observe performance against a standard
lessons.body:
## Observe performance against a standard

A defensible assessment records what the learner actually did, the conditions, criteria and outcome. Avoid vague impressions such as confident or experienced. Observe relevant routine checks, operation, communication and abnormal decisions within safe conditions. State which items were not assessed. An online quiz can demonstrate knowledge within its limits but cannot truthfully be recorded as a field observation.

### Deeper application

Use criteria describing observable behavior. Record what the candidate checked, communicated or did, and any prompts required. An evaluator should identify unassessed items rather than infer success from a smooth routine sequence. Knowledge can be tested through questions, while task performance needs an appropriate practical method. Neither a blank checklist nor a retrospective description of what probably happened constitutes an observation.

### Worked oilfield example

A forklift candidate passes a quiz, and the provider marks workplace evaluation complete without observing operation.

This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: An authentic evaluation record stating observed tasks, workplace conditions, results and evaluator. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that the checklist shows passed but leaves critical observed criteria blank. The appropriate correction is to resolve the missing performance evidence and reassess unobserved criteria before accepting the result. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

An implementation record and a later effectiveness check answer different questions. The first shows whether the required action occurred within the stated scope. The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. In this example, the follow-up should return to the actual gap described above, rather than simply asking whether the file now looks complete. lessons.title: Lesson 5 — Remediate and reassess specific gaps
lessons.body:
## Remediate and reassess specific gaps

Feedback should identify the deficient action, its safety significance and the standard to meet. Provide suitable additional explanation and supervised practice, then reassess the relevant capability. Retain the first attempt and correction separately. Do not issue a competence result merely because the candidate stayed for the full session. Reassessment must establish performance rather than teach the candidate to imitate an answer without understanding.

### Deeper application

Remediation should target the gap. If the candidate misunderstands the stop signal, additional routine driving practice alone may not correct it. Explain the signal's meaning, practice the response safely and reassess application. Retain both outcomes and the assessor's reasoning. A later satisfactory result can support a new decision without changing the historical first attempt into something that did not occur.

### Worked oilfield example

A candidate operates smoothly but repeatedly ignores an established stop signal during assessment. The decision is to record the deficiency, remediate the stop response and reassess before passing the task.

A safety-critical response gap cannot be hidden by averaging unrelated strengths or rewriting the original assessment. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: Separate original and reassessment observations documenting the stop-response standard and outcome. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that the reassessment repeats a memorized verbal answer but does not evaluate the relevant response. The appropriate correction is to use an appropriate safe performance assessment that tests application of the corrected decision. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

An implementation record and a later effectiveness check answer different questions. The first shows whether the required action occurred within the stated scope. The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. In this example, the follow-up should return to the actual gap described above, rather than simply asking whether the file now looks complete. lessons.title: Lesson 6 — Calibrate and assure assessor decisions
lessons.body:
## Calibrate and assure assessor decisions

Assessors should interpret criteria consistently and explain their decisions. Compare judgments on a safe sample case, discuss differences and resolve ambiguous criteria with the technical owner. Check provider records and authentic outcomes rather than trusting card counts. Independence and conflicts should be transparent. Course completion supports employer decisions but does not itself grant work authority or establish company effectiveness.

### Deeper application

Calibration uses the same criteria on a shared sample so assessors can discuss different judgments. Resolve ambiguity with the competent technical owner and update controlled assessment material when needed. Check whether previous outcomes were affected rather than assuming the problem begins today. A useful quality review also samples provider evidence and whether employer authorizations stay within the assessed scope.

### Worked oilfield example

Two evaluators apply different standards to the same communication error, and both issue unrestricted passes. The decision is to calibrate the criteria and review affected decisions through a competent assessment process.

Inconsistent interpretation weakens the assessment's meaning; the criterion and resulting decisions need competent review. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: A calibration record showing the disputed criterion, technical resolution and review of affected outcomes. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that calibration occurred but the outdated checklist remains in use. The appropriate correction is to issue the controlled corrected criteria and confirm assessors apply them in subsequent evaluations. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

An implementation record and a later effectiveness check answer different questions. The first shows whether the required action occurred within the stated scope. The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. lessons.title: Two applied scenarios and fully worked solutions
lessons.body:
## Applied scenario 1: an incomplete decision chain

A purchased operator course promises competence but lists only attendance and a reading quiz. At the handover, a second issue is identified: The assessor's experience covers different equipment with materially different operating demands. The receiving supervisor has the earlier record but does not yet have evidence that the new issue was resolved. A colleague proposes the following shortcut: Disable the guard briefly because an instructor is present. Work is due to begin on the next shift, so the supervisor needs a defensible decision that protects people and preserves a clear history.

### Worked solution — immediate decision

Determine which assignment depends on that unresolved condition. Tell the affected people the restriction and who is coordinating resolution. If there is an immediate exposure, move to a safe position and use the established warning or emergency route rather than completing records first. The supervisor must not use a favorable overall company score as a substitute for this missing decision.

### Worked solution — resolve the additional issue

For the handover finding, the next action is: Verify matching competence or appoint an appropriately qualified evaluator. The supporting record should show: Verified assessor suitability linked to the specific task and equipment scope. This is important because assessment quality depends on the evaluator's ability to recognize safe and unsafe performance in that task. The receiving shift needs the actual status, not an assurance that someone intends to finish the check later. Identify the responsible role and obtain acknowledgment of the restriction. If the required authority or expertise is unavailable, the affected assignment remains unready; unrelated authorized work may be considered only after its interfaces are checked.

### Worked solution — reject the shortcut and verify the result

The proposed shortcut fails because training must not create the hazardous exposure it is meant to prevent. Instructor presence does not make a defeated safeguard acceptable. The suitable decision is: Use a safe simulation or other suitable method without defeating the operational safeguard. Evidence for review would include: A safe lesson plan identifying current material, accessible delivery and controlled practice conditions. Separate correction of the immediate problem from confirmation that the change works in later comparable conditions. A reviewer should check the actual control used and the scope represented by the evidence. If the same weakness recurs, reopen the issue and retain both the original decision and the new observation.

### What can be concluded

This solution establishes a bounded route from an identified gap to evidence and responsible acceptance. It does not establish that an assessment, clinical decision, technical test or employer authorization actually happened in a real company. The fictional case teaches how to decide and what to verify. Actual release remains with the designated employer/site authority after the applicable prerequisites are met.

## Applied scenario 2: an incomplete decision chain

A forklift candidate passes a quiz, and the provider marks workplace evaluation complete without observing operation. At the handover, a second issue is identified: The reassessment repeats a memorized verbal answer but does not evaluate the relevant response. The receiving supervisor has the earlier record but does not yet have evidence that the new issue was resolved. A colleague proposes the following shortcut: Accept both results because consistency is unimportant. Work is due to begin on the next shift, so the supervisor needs a defensible decision that protects people and preserves a clear history.

### Worked solution — immediate decision

Determine which assignment depends on that unresolved condition. Tell the affected people the restriction and who is coordinating resolution. If there is an immediate exposure, move to a safe position and use the established warning or emergency route rather than completing records first. The supervisor must not use a favorable overall company score as a substitute for this missing decision.

### Worked solution — resolve the additional issue

For the handover finding, the next action is: Use an appropriate safe performance assessment that tests application of the corrected decision. The supporting record should show: Separate original and reassessment observations documenting the stop-response standard and outcome. This is important because a safety-critical response gap cannot be hidden by averaging unrelated strengths or rewriting the original assessment. The receiving shift needs the actual status, not an assurance that someone intends to finish the check later. Identify the responsible role and obtain acknowledgment of the restriction. If the required authority or expertise is unavailable, the affected assignment remains unready; unrelated authorized work may be considered only after its interfaces are checked.

### Worked solution — reject the shortcut and verify the result

The proposed shortcut fails because inconsistent interpretation weakens the assessment's meaning; the criterion and resulting decisions need competent review. The suitable decision is: Calibrate the criteria and review affected decisions through a competent assessment process. Evidence for review would include: A calibration record showing the disputed criterion, technical resolution and review of affected outcomes. Separate correction of the immediate problem from confirmation that the change works in later comparable conditions. A reviewer should check the actual control used and the scope represented by the evidence. If the same weakness recurs, reopen the issue and retain both the original decision and the new observation.

### What can be concluded

This solution establishes a bounded route from an identified gap to evidence and responsible acceptance. It does not establish that an assessment, clinical decision, technical test or employer authorization actually happened in a real company. The fictional case teaches how to decide and what to verify. Actual release remains with the designated employer/site authority after the applicable prerequisites are met.

lessons.title: Final assessment — twenty questions
lessons.body: Answer each question individually. Apply the taught decisions to the facts given. Your first choices are retained. If an answer is wrong, read the specific explanation and explicitly acknowledge the corrected answer. A corrected score records learning after feedback; it does not overwrite the first-answer result. All twenty final questions and all six lesson checks must be completed.

lessons.title: Finish — separate practical qualification
lessons.body:
## Written completion and what it proves

Completion requires all 26 answered correctly or acknowledged remediation. Both first-answer and remediated scores remain separate. Completing the guided course is evidence that you worked through its knowledge and decision questions; it is not an observed practical performance result, a legal license, a provider certification or an employer authorization. Training evidence contributes to review within its scope and validity, rather than automatically establishing the whole company program.

## What needs separate assessment

The assessment should test recognition of an abnormal condition as well as routine performance. A person who can repeat a procedure but cannot identify when to stop has not demonstrated the whole task. Employer authorization should state the person, tasks, equipment or site limits, required supervision and the basis for the decision. Applicable legal, issuer, client and change-trigger requirements govern validity; this course invents no universal renewal period.

## Before actual work

Confirm current local instructions, reporting routes, emergency arrangements and the person who can resolve an operating hold. If assigned work exceeds your assessed scope, say so before accepting it. The Partner's job/site readiness decision remains separate from the company's evidence review. Preserve real records through the authorized process and protect personal information. The fictional examples in this course must never be submitted as evidence that your company performed the actions described.

## Legal requirements for the named work role
These apply only when you perform the work described below. They are not additional steps for completing this online course.

29 CFR 1910.178(l)(2), (4), (6) — Operators of powered industrial trucks covered by this standard: Formal instruction, practical training and workplace performance evaluation are required before independent operation, with employer certification and applicable refresher/evaluation duties. A trainer/evaluator needs the knowledge, training and experience specified in (l)(2)(iii); an outside assessor is not universally required. Source: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.178

lessons.title: Start here — Commercial drivers and transport authorization
lessons.body:
# C05: Commercial drivers and transport authorization

Keep driver/legal qualification distinct from general awareness. This course teaches the decisions needed to implement that purpose in field operations. It covers license class, endorsements, applicable carrier obligations, assessment and fitness status. The examples involve fictional oilfield crews and companies; none is a real incident record or evidence of a company's implementation.

Read six substantive lessons, answer each attached knowledge check, then study two applied cases and answer the twenty final questions. Every question has three choices and one correct answer. The course records the first answer separately from any correction. Completion requires all 26 answered correctly or acknowledged remediation, including reading the specific explanation for each correction. A remediated result must never replace the original score. There is no speed requirement: take the time needed to explain the decision in your own words.

The audience includes workers who recognize gaps, supervisors who coordinate work and program owners who maintain the system. Each has a different decision boundary. An observer may report an uncertain safeguard without personally being qualified to repair it. A supervisor may coordinate a hold without being the person authorized to clear a technical prerequisite. Learn both the action and the limit on that action.

lessons.title: Lesson 1 — Classify the transport operation
lessons.body:
## Classify the transport operation

Driver eligibility begins with the vehicle, combination, cargo, route and jurisdiction. A passenger vehicle, a regulated commercial combination and a hazardous-cargo movement can require different qualification evidence. The competent transport owner determines applicable legal and carrier requirements. This awareness course supplies no universal weight threshold or license class. Identify the operation accurately before deciding which evidence to request.

### Deeper application

Describe the operation before asking whether a driver is qualified. Include the actual combination, planned cargo, route and jurisdiction, since a changed trailer or load can change the legal review. This course deliberately supplies no threshold table for universal use. The transport owner should use the applicable authoritative requirements and document why they apply, instead of asking dispatch to infer law from vehicle appearance.

### Worked oilfield example

A pickup driver is allocated a larger regulated vehicle and cargo combination outside the verified qualification scope. The decision is to hold dispatch and have the transport owner verify the required qualifications for that operation.

Qualification depends on the actual operation; a valid license for unrelated driving does not establish eligibility. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: An operation classification linking vehicle, cargo, route, jurisdiction and applicable driver prerequisites. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that the classification omits a trailer added after the original review. The appropriate correction is to reassess the actual vehicle combination and verify matching qualifications before dispatch. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

An implementation record and a later effectiveness check answer different questions. The first shows whether the required action occurred within the stated scope. The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. In this example, the follow-up should return to the actual gap described above, rather than simply asking whether the file now looks complete. A genuine unknown must remain visible until resolved by appropriate evidence.

lessons.title: Lesson 2 — Verify license endorsements and restrictions
lessons.body:
## Verify license endorsements and restrictions

Inspect authentic current evidence for the identified driver, relevant license class, required endorsements and restrictions. Resolve unclear scope with the proper issuing or competent transport source. A photocopy is not a guarantee of present validity. Record verified status and protect personal identifiers. In the United States, FMCSA identifies additional endorsements for certain vehicle and cargo types; the precise requirement must be checked for the actual operation.

### Deeper application

Check identity, category and conditions as well as the expiry date. A credential can be genuine and current while still unsuitable for the assignment. Use authorized verification channels and record the decision without spreading unnecessary personal identifiers. Do not edit a submitted image or convert a restriction into a note that dispatch can ignore. If scope remains unclear, the assignment remains unverified pending resolution.

### Worked oilfield example

A driver's license is current, but its restriction conflicts with the assigned vehicle's configuration. The decision is to assign only work within verified license conditions or obtain an appropriately qualified replacement.

Currency is only one attribute. An active restriction can make a particular assignment unsuitable despite a valid license. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: A verified license check recording matching identity, class, endorsements, restrictions and decision. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that the submitted copy belongs to a different driver with a similar name. The appropriate correction is to resolve identity through the authorized verification process before accepting the evidence. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

An implementation record and a later effectiveness check answer different questions. The first shows whether the required action occurred within the stated scope. The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. In this example, the follow-up should return to the actual gap described above, rather than simply asking whether the file now looks complete. A genuine unknown must remain visible until resolved by appropriate evidence.

lessons.title: Lesson 3 — Separate legal eligibility from task suitability
lessons.body:
## Separate legal eligibility from task suitability

A license establishes a legal qualification within its scope; it does not demonstrate competence for every company route, load or site interface. Use relevant instruction and on-road or task evaluation by suitable assessors. Evaluate decisions such as identifying an unsafe route or stopping when conditions change. Never conduct training by exposing an unqualified driver or the public to an uncontrolled hazard.

### Deeper application

Task assessment should represent the planned work safely: relevant vehicle characteristics, route interfaces, load-related duties and abnormal decisions. The assessor should have matching competence and identify limitations. A familiarization drive cannot automatically establish cargo-handling capability, just as a cargo briefing cannot prove on-road performance. Keep the evidence types distinct and use them together for a bounded employer authorization.

### Worked oilfield example

A legally qualified driver has never used the remote lease road and has no assessment for the assigned transport task. The decision is to arrange relevant familiarization and suitable task evaluation before independent assignment.

Legal eligibility and task suitability answer different questions; unfamiliar operating conditions need appropriate preparation and assessment. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: A relevant route and task evaluation identifying conditions, observed decisions and remaining limits. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that the evaluation covered an empty vehicle but not the materially different planned cargo task. The appropriate correction is to review the cargo-specific gap and arrange suitable assessment before expanding authorization. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

An implementation record and a later effectiveness check answer different questions. The first shows whether the required action occurred within the stated scope. The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. In this example, the follow-up should return to the actual gap described above, rather than simply asking whether the file now looks complete. lessons.title: Lesson 4 — Verify carrier and company prerequisites
lessons.body:
## Verify carrier and company prerequisites

The transport owner should map applicable carrier obligations and driver qualification requirements, including any relevant fitness, records or duty requirements. This course does not replace that jurisdiction-specific mapping. Dispatch must know what is verified and which assignments remain restricted. A folder of documents is not a decision unless their validity and compatibility have been reviewed. Do not pressure a driver to self-approve an unresolved legal prerequisite.

### Deeper application

Transport eligibility can involve more than licensing. The responsible transport specialist maps carrier and jurisdiction obligations for the operation and identifies the required evidence. Dispatch needs a usable approved, restricted or pending status. A thick document file without a supported decision leaves allocation uncertain. If a prerequisite is missing, specify the missing item and alternative assignment rather than inventing a general waiver.

### Worked oilfield example

Dispatch sees a valid license but the transport owner's required qualification review remains incomplete. The decision is to keep the affected assignment unready until required qualification evidence and approval are verified.

A license does not replace other requirements that apply to the carrier and operation. Pending checks remain pending. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: A transport-owner qualification decision showing applicable checks, outstanding items and dispatch restrictions. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that dispatch cannot distinguish pending review from approved status in its roster. The appropriate correction is to make the operational status and restriction explicit before allocating the affected work. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

An implementation record and a later effectiveness check answer different questions. The first shows whether the required action occurred within the stated scope. The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. In this example, the follow-up should return to the actual gap described above, rather than simply asking whether the file now looks complete. lessons.title: Lesson 5 — Handle fitness status without unnecessary disclosure
lessons.body:
## Handle fitness status without unnecessary disclosure

A driver may have health-related qualification conditions or other fitness concerns requiring authorized review. Supervisors need the operational status and restrictions relevant to assignment, rather than a full clinical file. Use the designated process and qualified providers for medical judgments. A driver reporting inability to continue safely should be heard and the assignment reassessed; the supervisor should not diagnose or override a clinician.

### Deeper application

Fitness information should follow the designated occupational or regulatory process. A supervisor can report observed difficulty or a worker's stated concern, but should not make a diagnosis. The operational decision uses valid capacity or qualification status and applicable restrictions. Keep clinical detail in authorized channels. Urgent uncertainty about safe continuation calls for a suitable reassessment and protection, not pressure to finish the route.

### Worked oilfield example

A dispatcher asks for a driver's diagnosis when the necessary information is a verified restriction on driving duties. The decision is to use authorized fitness-status and restriction information through the designated confidential process.

Assignment decisions need valid capacity information, while clinical details remain in appropriately restricted channels. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: A restricted fitness-status record and an operational roster showing only necessary assignment limits. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that a restriction is present but no one translated it into dispatch limits. The appropriate correction is to coordinate authorized clarification and implement compatible assignments before release. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

An implementation record and a later effectiveness check answer different questions. The first shows whether the required action occurred within the stated scope. The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. In this example, the follow-up should return to the actual gap described above, rather than simply asking whether the file now looks complete. lessons.title: Lesson 6 — Maintain authorization through change and expiry
lessons.body:
## Maintain authorization through change and expiry

Employer authorization states permitted vehicles, tasks and conditions based on verified evidence. Track relevant expiry, restriction and change triggers, and suspend affected allocation when required qualification cannot be confirmed. Reuse valid matching evidence; do not invent an annual renewal rule for every document. A changed route, vehicle or cargo can require review even when a credential has not expired. Preserve previous decisions and communicate current limits.

### Deeper application

Plan renewal early enough to preserve coverage, but keep planned and verified renewal separate. A renewal receipt may show an application was submitted without proving the required status is current. Changed cargo or routes may require scope review even after renewal. Preserve historical validity and employer decisions so later audits can examine what supported each assignment at the time it occurred.

### Worked oilfield example

A driver's required credential expires before tomorrow's regulated transport assignment. The decision is to hold that assignment until valid matching qualification is verified or use an authorized replacement.

A planned renewal is not current evidence. Allocation must use the status valid for the intended work date. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: A dated restriction and later verified renewal or replacement decision tied to the actual assignment. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that the renewal is verified but employer authorization still excludes the newly assigned cargo. The appropriate correction is to review and approve the actual cargo scope before dispatch rather than relying on renewal alone. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

An implementation record and a later effectiveness check answer different questions. The first shows whether the required action occurred within the stated scope. The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. In this example, the follow-up should return to the actual gap described above, rather than simply asking whether the file now looks complete. A genuine unknown must remain visible until resolved by appropriate evidence.

lessons.title: Two applied scenarios and fully worked solutions
lessons.body:
## Applied scenario 1: an incomplete decision chain

A pickup driver is allocated a larger regulated vehicle and cargo combination outside the verified qualification scope. At the handover, a second issue is identified: The submitted copy belongs to a different driver with a similar name. The receiving supervisor has the earlier record but does not yet have evidence that the new issue was resolved. A colleague proposes the following shortcut: Assume the license proves suitability for every route and load. Work is due to begin on the next shift, so the supervisor needs a defensible decision that protects people and preserves a clear history.

### Worked solution — immediate decision

The first response is: Hold dispatch and have the transport owner verify the required qualifications for that operation. The reason is specific: Qualification depends on the actual operation; a valid license for unrelated driving does not establish eligibility. Determine which assignment depends on that unresolved condition. Tell the affected people the restriction and who is coordinating resolution. If there is an immediate exposure, move to a safe position and use the established warning or emergency route rather than completing records first. The supervisor must not use a favorable overall company score as a substitute for this missing decision.

### Worked solution — resolve the additional issue

For the handover finding, the next action is: Resolve identity through the authorized verification process before accepting the evidence. The supporting record should show: A verified license check recording matching identity, class, endorsements, restrictions and decision. This is important because currency is only one attribute. An active restriction can make a particular assignment unsuitable despite a valid license. The receiving shift needs the actual status, not an assurance that someone intends to finish the check later. Identify the responsible role and obtain acknowledgment of the restriction. If the required authority or expertise is unavailable, the affected assignment remains unready; unrelated authorized work may be considered only after its interfaces are checked.

The proposed shortcut fails because legal eligibility and task suitability answer different questions; unfamiliar operating conditions need appropriate preparation and assessment. The suitable decision is: Arrange relevant familiarization and suitable task evaluation before independent assignment. Evidence for review would include: A relevant route and task evaluation identifying conditions, observed decisions and remaining limits. Separate correction of the immediate problem from confirmation that the change works in later comparable conditions. A reviewer should check the actual control used and the scope represented by the evidence. If the same weakness recurs, reopen the issue and retain both the original decision and the new observation.

This solution establishes a bounded route from an identified gap to evidence and responsible acceptance. It does not establish that an assessment, clinical decision, technical test or employer authorization actually happened in a real company. The fictional case teaches how to decide and what to verify. Actual release remains with the designated employer/site authority after the applicable prerequisites are met.

## Applied scenario 2: an incomplete decision chain

Dispatch sees a valid license but the transport owner's required qualification review remains incomplete. At the handover, a second issue is identified: A restriction is present but no one translated it into dispatch limits. The receiving supervisor has the earlier record but does not yet have evidence that the new issue was resolved. A colleague proposes the following shortcut: Extend the expiry date in the roster because renewal is planned. Work is due to begin on the next shift, so the supervisor needs a defensible decision that protects people and preserves a clear history.

### Worked solution — immediate decision

The first response is: Keep the affected assignment unready until required qualification evidence and approval are verified. The reason is specific: A license does not replace other requirements that apply to the carrier and operation. Pending checks remain pending. Determine which assignment depends on that unresolved condition. Tell the affected people the restriction and who is coordinating resolution. If there is an immediate exposure, move to a safe position and use the established warning or emergency route rather than completing records first. The supervisor must not use a favorable overall company score as a substitute for this missing decision.

### Worked solution — resolve the additional issue

For the handover finding, the next action is: Coordinate authorized clarification and implement compatible assignments before release. The supporting record should show: A restricted fitness-status record and an operational roster showing only necessary assignment limits. This is important because assignment decisions need valid capacity information, while clinical details remain in appropriately restricted channels. The receiving shift needs the actual status, not an assurance that someone intends to finish the check later. Identify the responsible role and obtain acknowledgment of the restriction. If the required authority or expertise is unavailable, the affected assignment remains unready; unrelated authorized work may be considered only after its interfaces are checked.

lessons.title: Final assessment — twenty questions
lessons.body: Answer each question individually. Apply the taught decisions to the facts given. Your first choices are retained. If an answer is wrong, read the specific explanation and explicitly acknowledge the corrected answer. A corrected score records learning after feedback; it does not overwrite the first-answer result. All twenty final questions and all six lesson checks must be completed.

lessons.title: Finish — separate practical qualification
lessons.body:
## Written completion and what it proves

Completion requires all 26 answered correctly or acknowledged remediation. Both first-answer and remediated scores remain separate. Completing the guided course is evidence that you worked through its knowledge and decision questions; it is not an observed practical performance result, a legal license, a provider certification or an employer authorization. Training evidence contributes to review within its scope and validity, rather than automatically establishing the whole company program.

## What needs separate assessment

The assessment should test recognition of an abnormal condition as well as routine performance. A person who can repeat a procedure but cannot identify when to stop has not demonstrated the whole task. Employer authorization should state the person, tasks, equipment or site limits, required supervision and the basis for the decision. Applicable legal, issuer, client and change-trigger requirements govern validity; this course invents no universal renewal period.

## Before actual work

Confirm current local instructions, reporting routes, emergency arrangements and the person who can resolve an operating hold. If assigned work exceeds your assessed scope, say so before accepting it. The Partner's job/site readiness decision remains separate from the company's evidence review. Preserve real records through the authorized process and protect personal information. The fictional examples in this course must never be submitted as evidence that your company performed the actions described.

lessons.title: Start here — Mobile equipment, forklift and lifting-role assessment
lessons.body:
# C06: Mobile equipment, forklift and lifting-role assessment

Match authorization to equipment and work environment. This course teaches the decisions needed to implement that purpose in field operations. It covers equipment-specific training, workplace evaluation and retraining triggers. The examples involve fictional oilfield crews and companies; none is a real incident record or evidence of a company's implementation.

Read six substantive lessons, answer each attached knowledge check, then study two applied cases and answer the twenty final questions. Every question has three choices and one correct answer. The course records the first answer separately from any correction. Completion requires all 26 answered correctly or acknowledged remediation, including reading the specific explanation for each correction. A remediated result must never replace the original score. There is no speed requirement: take the time needed to explain the decision in your own words.

The audience includes workers who recognize gaps, supervisors who coordinate work and program owners who maintain the system. Each has a different decision boundary. An observer may report an uncertain safeguard without personally being qualified to repair it. A supervisor may coordinate a hold without being the person authorized to clear a technical prerequisite. Learn both the action and the limit on that action.

lessons.title: Lesson 1 — Define equipment and lifting-role scope
lessons.body:
## Define equipment and lifting-role scope

Separate equipment operation, rigging and signaling; capability in one does not automatically establish another. Define equipment type, attachments, loads, workplace conditions and duties. A forklift assessment for one arrangement may not support a changed attachment or environment. Technical suitability and operating limits come from current manufacturer and competent sources. A generic operator card cannot state every workplace condition the person can safely manage.

### Deeper application

Define equipment scope with enough detail to identify meaningful differences, including attachment and relevant workplace conditions. Do not turn every cosmetic difference into an entirely new qualification requirement, but do not ignore changes affecting operation. The competent equipment owner and evaluator decide what additional assessment is needed. Keep equipment suitability, operator competence and lifting-role assignment as related but separate prerequisites.

### Worked oilfield example

A forklift operator assessed with standard forks is assigned a materially different attachment without scope review. The decision is to hold the changed operation and verify equipment suitability plus relevant training and evaluation.

Changing the attachment can change the operation and the competence needed; a generic card cannot resolve that gap. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: A scoped evaluation and authorization identifying attachment and relevant workplace conditions. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that the equipment assessment lists a different attachment model with different relevant characteristics. The appropriate correction is to have the competent owner review actual suitability and matching assessment before release. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

An implementation record and a later effectiveness check answer different questions. The first shows whether the required action occurred within the stated scope. The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. In this example, the follow-up should return to the actual gap described above, rather than simply asking whether the file now looks complete. A genuine unknown must remain visible until resolved by appropriate evidence.

In U.S. powered industrial truck work, OSHA's applicable rule explicitly distinguishes these elements. Use suitable equipment and safe controlled conditions. ### Deeper application

Formal instruction teaches concepts and controls; supervised practice develops the actions; workplace evaluation checks the resulting capability in context. The appropriate balance and requirements depend on the actual equipment and governing rules. An awareness lesson can support the first element without completing the others. The decision is to retain the knowledge evidence and arrange the missing suitable practical elements before authorization.

lessons.title: Lesson 3 — Use a suitable evaluator and criteria
lessons.body:
## Use a suitable evaluator and criteria

The evaluator must be capable of recognizing safe task performance in the relevant equipment and conditions. Observe pre-use decisions, operation, load handling, communication and response to abnormal conditions as applicable. State which criteria were assessed and what was not observed. Assessment should occur safely; never create an uncontrolled suspended-load or traffic exposure as a test. The assessor's authority is bounded by their competence.

### Deeper application

The evaluator needs criteria for routine and abnormal decisions. A candidate who maneuvers accurately but ignores a defect or communication failure has not demonstrated every necessary capability. Use safe controlled methods to test the decision. Record conditions, equipment, prompts and limitations. An assessment performed in one environment should not be represented as covering materially different conditions that were never examined.

### Worked oilfield example

A crane-related role is evaluated by someone whose experience covers only unrelated warehouse equipment. The decision is to obtain a suitably qualified evaluator for the actual lifting role and assessment scope.

Evaluator suitability must match the role and conditions being judged; unrelated experience cannot establish that match. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: A role-specific evaluation identifying evaluator competence, actual criteria and observed outcomes. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

lessons.title: Lesson 4 — Keep operator rigger and signal duties distinct
lessons.body:
## Keep operator rigger and signal duties distinct

A lift requires coordinated roles and understood communication. An equipment operator may not be qualified to select rigging, and a rigger may not be authorized to direct movement as a designated signal person. Identify applicable requirements and assess each assigned role separately. When communication fails or the work exceeds the plan, use the established stop route. This course supplies no load-chart instruction or rigging-selection qualification.

### Deeper application

The crew should know who performs each lifting function and how a change is communicated. Role boundaries help prevent a worker taking on an unassessed task during a rushed handover. Stop when communication becomes uncertain through the established route; do not invent signals during movement. This lesson supports recognition of a role gap, while the actual signaling and rigging techniques require appropriate specialist training and evaluation.

### Worked oilfield example

An authorized equipment operator is asked to serve as signal person based solely on the operator card. The decision is to verify the separate signal-role competence and authorization before assigning that duty.

Different roles have different tasks and assessment bases. Authority for one cannot simply transfer to another. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: A lifting-role roster linking each assigned role to its matching verified assessment and authority. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.
