lessons.title: Lesson 5 — Correct errors while preserving occurrences
lessons.body:
## Correct errors while preserving occurrences

An investigation can refine classification or correct a duplicate, but closing it does not erase that the event occurred. Record the original entry, correction reason, supporting evidence, authorized decision and affected summary versions. A duplicate should be linked and resolved, not silently hidden. Corrections must improve accuracy rather than manipulate outcomes. Retain confidential raw material in restricted channels with deidentified summaries where appropriate.

### Deeper application

An audit trail should show what changed, why, who authorized it and which summary versions are affected. A duplicate resolution removes double counting while preserving a link to the actual occurrence. A later classification decision can alter a category without denying the event. Neither investigation closure nor a successful corrective action justifies deleting history. Accuracy, rather than favorable appearance, is the correction's purpose.

### Worked oilfield example

A manager deletes an incident from history when its investigation closes and corrective actions are complete. The decision is to restore a traceable occurrence record and separate event history from investigation and action status.

Closure describes process progress, not whether an event happened. Event history must remain accurate and traceable. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: An auditable correction preserving the occurrence and documenting classification and status changes. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that a genuine duplicate is removed without linking the surviving event or recording the reason. The appropriate correction is to document the duplicate resolution and preserve a reproducible audit trail to the surviving occurrence. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

An implementation record and a later effectiveness check answer different questions. The first shows whether the required action occurred within the stated scope. The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. In this example, the follow-up should return to the actual gap described above, rather than simply asking whether the file now looks complete. A genuine unknown must remain visible until resolved by appropriate evidence.

lessons.title: Lesson 6 — Keep outcomes separate from maturity and privacy
lessons.body:
## Keep outcomes separate from maturity and privacy

Incident history describes outcomes and reporting coverage; maturity describes verified company practices. Zero incidents earns no automatic full maturity credit, and an occurrence alone does not prove every practice failed. Relevant verified findings can affect the specific evidence decision. Share only necessary deidentified summary data and restrict raw medical or personal records. Reviewer conclusions should state coverage and uncertainty alongside the numbers.

### Deeper application

Keep outcome history visible alongside reporting coverage and verified practice evidence. A company with no recorded injuries may still lack proof of implementation, while one reported event may reveal a strong reporting response and a specific control weakness. Evaluate the relevant findings rather than automatically converting the event count into a maturity penalty or reward. Restrict raw sensitive records and provide necessary bounded summaries.

### Worked oilfield example

A vendor requests full maturity credit solely because its summary shows zero reported injuries. The decision is to assess the required practice evidence separately and disclose the outcome summary's scope and uncertainty.

Outcomes and implementation answer different questions; neither a zero nor a private-file dump establishes company maturity. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: Separate outcome and maturity records with bounded coverage and controlled access to supporting evidence. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that a dashboard displays missing exposure data as a green zero rate. The appropriate correction is to display the measure as unavailable with its coverage gap until supported data is reconciled. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

An implementation record and a later effectiveness check answer different questions. The first shows whether the required action occurred within the stated scope. The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. In this example, the follow-up should return to the actual gap described above, rather than simply asking whether the file now looks complete. A genuine unknown must remain visible until resolved by appropriate evidence.

lessons.title: Two applied scenarios and fully worked solutions
lessons.body:
## Applied scenario 1: an incomplete decision chain

A vendor combines subcontractor incidents with employee-only hours and presents the resulting rate as company-wide. At the handover, a second issue is identified: The reconciliation includes office hours while the stated measure covers only a field contract. The receiving supervisor has the earlier record but does not yet have evidence that the new issue was resolved. A colleague proposes the following shortcut: Enter zero because no report reached the office. Work is due to begin on the next shift, so the supervisor needs a defensible decision that protects people and preserves a clear history.

### Worked solution — immediate decision

The first response is: Reconcile a consistent event and exposure population before calculating or comparing the measure. The reason is specific: A rate requires compatible numerator and denominator scope; real numbers can still produce a misleading comparison. Determine which assignment depends on that unresolved condition. Tell the affected people the restriction and who is coordinating resolution. If there is an immediate exposure, move to a safe position and use the established warning or emergency route rather than completing records first. The supervisor must not use a favorable overall company score as a substitute for this missing decision.

### Worked solution — resolve the additional issue

For the handover finding, the next action is: Correct the exposure scope and retain the adjustment trail and calculation basis. The supporting record should show: A reconciliation documenting source definitions, differences, adjustments and accepted exposure total. This is important because the denominator must represent the defined exposure. Choosing a convenient number distorts the measure. The receiving shift needs the actual status, not an assurance that someone intends to finish the check later. Identify the responsible role and obtain acknowledgment of the restriction. If the required authority or expertise is unavailable, the affected assignment remains unready; unrelated authorized work may be considered only after its interfaces are checked.

### Worked solution — reject the shortcut and verify the result

The proposed shortcut fails because missing information is not evidence of absence. A zero must be bounded by verified reporting coverage. The suitable decision is: Show subcontractor coverage as unknown and reconcile it before claiming a complete zero. Evidence for review would include: A coverage declaration identifying checked sources, confirmed zero scope and outstanding gaps. Separate correction of the immediate problem from confirmation that the change works in later comparable conditions. A reviewer should check the actual control used and the scope represented by the evidence. If the same weakness recurs, reopen the issue and retain both the original decision and the new observation.

### What can be concluded

This solution establishes a bounded route from an identified gap to evidence and responsible acceptance. It does not establish that an assessment, clinical decision, technical test or employer authorization actually happened in a real company. The fictional case teaches how to decide and what to verify. Actual release remains with the designated employer/site authority after the applicable prerequisites are met.

## Applied scenario 2: an incomplete decision chain

A customer asks for a rate comparison, but the vendors use different event definitions and one lacks verified hours. The receiving supervisor has the earlier record but does not yet have evidence that the new issue was resolved. Work is due to begin on the next shift, so the supervisor needs a defensible decision that protects people and preserves a clear history.

### Worked solution — immediate decision

The first response is: Mark the comparison unsupported and explain the missing compatible definitions and exposure evidence. The reason is specific: A numerical comparison is only meaningful when its inputs and definitions are compatible and known. Determine which assignment depends on that unresolved condition. Tell the affected people the restriction and who is coordinating resolution. If there is an immediate exposure, move to a safe position and use the established warning or emergency route rather than completing records first. The supervisor must not use a favorable overall company score as a substitute for this missing decision.

### Worked solution — resolve the additional issue

For the handover finding, the next action is: Document the duplicate resolution and preserve a reproducible audit trail to the surviving occurrence. The supporting record should show: An auditable correction preserving the occurrence and documenting classification and status changes. This is important because closure describes process progress, not whether an event happened. Event history must remain accurate and traceable. The receiving shift needs the actual status, not an assurance that someone intends to finish the check later. Identify the responsible role and obtain acknowledgment of the restriction. If the required authority or expertise is unavailable, the affected assignment remains unready; unrelated authorized work may be considered only after its interfaces are checked.

### Worked solution — reject the shortcut and verify the result

The proposed shortcut fails because outcomes and implementation answer different questions; neither a zero nor a private-file dump establishes company maturity. The suitable decision is: Assess the required practice evidence separately and disclose the outcome summary's scope and uncertainty. Evidence for review would include: Separate outcome and maturity records with bounded coverage and controlled access to supporting evidence. Separate correction of the immediate problem from confirmation that the change works in later comparable conditions. A reviewer should check the actual control used and the scope represented by the evidence. If the same weakness recurs, reopen the issue and retain both the original decision and the new observation.

### What can be concluded

This solution establishes a bounded route from an identified gap to evidence and responsible acceptance. It does not establish that an assessment, clinical decision, technical test or employer authorization actually happened in a real company. The fictional case teaches how to decide and what to verify. lessons.title: Final assessment — twenty questions
lessons.body: Answer each question individually. Apply the taught decisions to the facts given. Your first choices are retained. If an answer is wrong, read the specific explanation and explicitly acknowledge the corrected answer. A corrected score records learning after feedback; it does not overwrite the first-answer result. All twenty final questions and all six lesson checks must be completed.

lessons.title: Finish — separate practical qualification
lessons.body:
## Written completion and what it proves

Completion requires all 26 answered correctly or acknowledged remediation. Both first-answer and remediated scores remain separate. Completing the guided course is evidence that you worked through its knowledge and decision questions; it is not an observed practical performance result, a legal license, a provider certification or an employer authorization. Training evidence contributes to review within its scope and validity, rather than automatically establishing the whole company program.

## What needs separate assessment

The assessment should test recognition of an abnormal condition as well as routine performance. A person who can repeat a procedure but cannot identify when to stop has not demonstrated the whole task. Employer authorization should state the person, tasks, equipment or site limits, required supervision and the basis for the decision. Applicable legal, issuer, client and change-trigger requirements govern validity; this course invents no universal renewal period.

## Before actual work

Confirm current local instructions, reporting routes, emergency arrangements and the person who can resolve an operating hold. If assigned work exceeds your assessed scope, say so before accepting it. The Partner's job/site readiness decision remains separate from the company's evidence review. Preserve real records through the authorized process and protect personal information. The fictional examples in this course must never be submitted as evidence that your company performed the actions described.

lessons.title: Start here — Medical response, restricted records and return-to-work interfaces
lessons.body:
# I06: Medical response, restricted records and return-to-work interfaces

Coordinate care and safe restrictions while protecting worker privacy. This course teaches the decisions needed to implement that purpose in field operations. It covers care escalation, confidential handling, authorized restrictions and safe return coordination. The examples involve fictional oilfield crews and companies; none is a real incident record or evidence of a company's implementation.

Read six substantive lessons, answer each attached knowledge check, then study two applied cases and answer the twenty final questions. Every question has three choices and one correct answer. The course records the first answer separately from any correction. Completion requires all 26 answered correctly or acknowledged remediation, including reading the specific explanation for each correction. A remediated result must never replace the original score. There is no speed requirement: take the time needed to explain the decision in your own words.

The audience includes workers who recognize gaps, supervisors who coordinate work and program owners who maintain the system. Each has a different decision boundary. An observer may report an uncertain safeguard without personally being qualified to repair it. A supervisor may coordinate a hold without being the person authorized to clear a technical prerequisite. Learn both the action and the limit on that action.

lessons.title: Lesson 1 — Arrange care before administrative handling
lessons.body:
## Arrange care before administrative handling

When someone needs medical help, use the established emergency or referral process promptly. Supervisors coordinate response and safe access within their roles; they do not diagnose severity to avoid calling. Protect other people from the same exposure and provide responders with relevant factual hazard information. Complete routine records after immediate care and protection. This course provides no treatment technique, clinical triage rule or clearance to perform medical care.

### Deeper application

A supervisor can supply responders with the known exposure, location and access information while avoiding an unsupported diagnosis. Do not require an injured or unwell worker to finish statements before care. The administrative record should reflect what actually occurred, including uncertain times and who activated the response. If the same exposure threatens others, coordinate protection through the appropriate operating route without delaying the care referral.

### Worked oilfield example

A worker develops symptoms after an exposure, and the supervisor delays referral while collecting a full incident statement. The decision is to arrange appropriate care through the established response route before routine statement-taking.

Care must not be delayed for administrative completeness, and supervisors should not make unsupported clinical judgments. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: A factual response record showing referral or emergency activation and immediate protection actions. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that the referral record says notified but the care route never received the request. The appropriate correction is to verify and activate the appropriate care communication immediately and correct the status to actual facts. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

An implementation record and a later effectiveness check answer different questions. The first shows whether the required action occurred within the stated scope. The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. In this example, the follow-up should return to the actual gap described above, rather than simply asking whether the file now looks complete. A genuine unknown must remain visible until resolved by appropriate evidence.

lessons.title: Lesson 2 — Separate clinical records from operational status
lessons.body:
## Separate clinical records from operational status

Clinical notes, diagnoses and medical questionnaires need appropriately restricted handling. Operational supervisors usually need authorized capacity or restriction information relevant to assignment, not the entire clinical history. Determine recipients through the applicable legal and organizational process rather than assuming every safety employee may see everything. Do not promise that a generic privacy label satisfies every jurisdiction's requirements. Protect records in storage, sharing and exported reports.

### Deeper application

Minimum necessary operational information may include whether the person may perform a duty, the valid restrictions and when review is needed. The exact sharing basis must follow applicable requirements and the authorized process. A general team roster should not become a medical file. Keep clinical records and operational status linked through controlled references where appropriate, so supervisors can allocate safely without reading unrelated diagnoses or questionnaires.

### Worked oilfield example

A supervisor requests a worker's complete medical file to decide whether restricted duties can be allocated. The decision is to obtain necessary authorized work-capacity information through the designated process and keep clinical detail restricted.

Assignment needs valid functional limits; unnecessary clinical disclosure does not improve that decision and creates privacy exposure. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: A restricted clinical reference and a separate operational restriction status shared only with authorized roles. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that the restricted status is correct but a diagnosis appears in an unrestricted attachment. The appropriate correction is to restrict further disclosure and follow the authorized confidentiality response while preserving necessary records. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

An implementation record and a later effectiveness check answer different questions. The first shows whether the required action occurred within the stated scope. The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. In this example, the follow-up should return to the actual gap described above, rather than simply asking whether the file now looks complete. A genuine unknown must remain visible until resolved by appropriate evidence.

lessons.title: Lesson 3 — Translate restrictions into compatible duties
lessons.body:
## Translate restrictions into compatible duties

A valid restriction should be understood in relation to actual task demands. Identify the proposed duties, compare them with authorized capacity information and seek clarification through the designated route where meaning is unclear. A supervisor should not reinterpret a restriction away because work is urgent. Modified duties must be genuinely compatible in practice, including access, travel and incidental tasks, rather than only a renamed job title.

### Deeper application

Compare restrictions with the whole assignment: main tasks, travel, access, incidental handling and credible emergency duties. A light-duty label does not establish compatibility. Provide accurate task demands to the authorized coordinator or clinician when clarification is needed. Do not make the worker privately negotiate exceptions with each supervisor. A coherent duty plan should make the limits usable and protect against incompatible ad hoc requests.

### Worked oilfield example

A worker has an authorized lifting restriction, but proposed desk duties routinely require moving heavy files and equipment. The decision is to review actual task demands and provide compatible duties or obtain authorized clarification before allocation.

Compatibility depends on what the person must actually do, not the assignment's title or a waiver. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: A duty-to-restriction review showing actual tasks, compatibility decision and unresolved clarification needs. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that the main duty fits but emergency or incidental tasks exceed the restriction. The appropriate correction is to review the full duty set and implement a genuinely compatible arrangement through authorized coordination. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

An implementation record and a later effectiveness check answer different questions. The first shows whether the required action occurred within the stated scope. The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. In this example, the follow-up should return to the actual gap described above, rather than simply asking whether the file now looks complete. A genuine unknown must remain visible until resolved by appropriate evidence.

lessons.title: Lesson 4 — Use clinicians for medical decisions
lessons.body:
## Use clinicians for medical decisions

Clinical capacity, treatment and medical clearance require appropriately qualified providers through the authorized process. Supervisors contribute accurate task information and implement valid restrictions. They must not diagnose, shorten recovery or overrule a clinician based on appearance. In respiratory-protection contexts, applicable OSHA requirements distinguish employer operational information from confidential medical evaluation content; this example does not replace the full respiratory program.

### Deeper application

Clinical judgment and job knowledge should inform each other through the designated route. The employer can explain task demands; the qualified provider addresses capacity within their role. A supervisor should not decide that a limitation no longer matters because the worker appears comfortable. Where the note is ambiguous, seek clarification rather than silently choosing the interpretation that permits the most work.

### Worked oilfield example

A supervisor says a worker looks recovered and removes a valid clinical restriction without authorized review. The decision is to maintain the restriction and seek appropriate clinical clarification or updated capacity information.

Appearance and supervisory experience do not authorize a clinical capacity change. Valid restrictions remain until appropriately revised. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: An authorized updated capacity decision linked to communicated task demands and operational implementation. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that the provider's note is unclear about a duty essential to the proposed assignment. The appropriate correction is to seek clarification through the designated authorized route before relying on an unsupported interpretation. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

An implementation record and a later effectiveness check answer different questions. The first shows whether the required action occurred within the stated scope. The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. In this example, the follow-up should return to the actual gap described above, rather than simply asking whether the file now looks complete. lessons.title: Lesson 5 — Coordinate return without disclosing unnecessary detail
lessons.body:
## Coordinate return without disclosing unnecessary detail

Return-to-work coordination needs clear roles: the worker communicates through the designated process, authorized providers supply capacity information and the employer allocates compatible duties. Tell relevant supervisors what restrictions apply and when review is due, without distributing diagnosis or unrelated clinical detail. Confirm changes reach all allocating roles. A worker's return to the site is not automatically unrestricted clearance for every task.

### Deeper application

A return plan should distinguish presence at work from the capacity to resume all previous duties. Communicate necessary restrictions to the people who allocate tasks, including temporary cover and incoming shifts. Confirm that the worker understands the plan and knows how to raise difficulty. Updated clinical information should reach the operational decision through the authorized process, rather than circulate informally through colleagues.

### Worked oilfield example

A returning worker's supervisor receives valid restrictions, but dispatch assigns the worker's previous unrestricted field route. The decision is to stop the incompatible allocation and communicate the current necessary restrictions to authorized dispatch roles.

Return and unrestricted clearance are different states; assignment must use current valid limits with appropriate confidentiality. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: A coordinated return record showing current capacity status, compatible duty limits and acknowledged allocation changes. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that the restriction changes but the incoming shift uses an old duty plan. The appropriate correction is to update the operational plan and confirm receipt of the necessary change before allocation. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

An implementation record and a later effectiveness check answer different questions. The first shows whether the required action occurred within the stated scope. The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. In this example, the follow-up should return to the actual gap described above, rather than simply asking whether the file now looks complete. A genuine unknown must remain visible until resolved by appropriate evidence.

lessons.title: Lesson 6 — Review changes and confidentiality incidents
lessons.body:
## Review changes and confidentiality incidents

Restrictions and capacity information can change, so record current status, review needs and the source of authorized updates. Do not invent a universal medical renewal period. Preserve a traceable history with controlled access. If health information is misdirected, limit further disclosure and activate the designated privacy process without deleting required evidence or concealing the incident. Review whether the assignment process actually maintained restrictions in later work.

### Deeper application

Review whether real assignments matched restrictions and whether updates reached operational users. A correct file can coexist with incompatible work if allocation uses stale information. Confidentiality incidents need their own response even when capacity status is corrected. Limit further disclosure and follow the authorized process; do not destroy required records to hide the mistake. Preserve a traceable history of both the status update and the privacy response.

### Worked oilfield example

An outdated restriction remains in dispatch after an authorized update, while a diagnosis was mistakenly shared in a general chat. The decision is to correct authorized operational status and separately initiate the confidentiality response for the disclosure.

Status accuracy and privacy response are separate obligations; resolving one does not erase the other. This is a decision about the described conditions, rather than a conclusion that every related activity is unsafe. Identify which people and assignments depend on the unresolved point. Maintain the relevant restriction while the responsible person checks the facts; avoid spreading an unsupported approval to another crew or task.

### What the record must show

Useful evidence would be: A traceable status update and a separately restricted confidentiality incident response record. Record what was actually checked and the scope of that check. Distinguish the observation from an opinion about it. A record of the decision should allow the next responsible person to tell what is accepted, what remains unresolved and whose authority is needed. If a check has not occurred, state that it is pending. Do not convert a planned check into a completed result.

### A later challenge to the decision

During follow-up, the reviewer finds that the updated plan is filed but later job records still show incompatible duties. The appropriate correction is to reopen the coordination failure and verify real assignment controls and compatible work before claiming effectiveness. This additional fact changes what can be relied on. Preserve the earlier record and add the correction with its reason; quietly rewriting history would hide how the gap arose. Confirm that anyone relying on the earlier status receives the changed restriction before the next affected assignment.

### Applying the distinction

An implementation record and a later effectiveness check answer different questions. The first shows whether the required action occurred within the stated scope. The second examines whether its intended protection works during relevant later work. Neither an unrelated credential nor a completed form answers both questions. In this example, the follow-up should return to the actual gap described above, rather than simply asking whether the file now looks complete. A genuine unknown must remain visible until resolved by appropriate evidence.

lessons.title: Two applied scenarios and fully worked solutions
lessons.body:
## Applied scenario 1: an incomplete decision chain

A worker develops symptoms after an exposure, and the supervisor delays referral while collecting a full incident statement. At the handover, a second issue is identified: The restricted status is correct but a diagnosis appears in an unrestricted attachment. The receiving supervisor has the earlier record but does not yet have evidence that the new issue was resolved. A colleague proposes the following shortcut: Rename the assignment office work and ignore its physical tasks. Work is due to begin on the next shift, so the supervisor needs a defensible decision that protects people and preserves a clear history.

### Worked solution — immediate decision

The first response is: Arrange appropriate care through the established response route before routine statement-taking. The reason is specific: Care must not be delayed for administrative completeness, and supervisors should not make unsupported clinical judgments. Determine which assignment depends on that unresolved condition. Tell the affected people the restriction and who is coordinating resolution. If there is an immediate exposure, move to a safe position and use the established warning or emergency route rather than completing records first. The supervisor must not use a favorable overall company score as a substitute for this missing decision.

### Worked solution — resolve the additional issue

For the handover finding, the next action is: Restrict further disclosure and follow the authorized confidentiality response while preserving necessary records. The supporting record should show: A restricted clinical reference and a separate operational restriction status shared only with authorized roles. This is important because assignment needs valid functional limits; unnecessary clinical disclosure does not improve that decision and creates privacy exposure. The receiving shift needs the actual status, not an assurance that someone intends to finish the check later. Identify the responsible role and obtain acknowledgment of the restriction. If the required authority or expertise is unavailable, the affected assignment remains unready; unrelated authorized work may be considered only after its interfaces are checked.

### Worked solution — reject the shortcut and verify the result

The proposed shortcut fails because compatibility depends on what the person must actually do, not the assignment's title or a waiver. The suitable decision is: Review actual task demands and provide compatible duties or obtain authorized clarification before allocation. Evidence for review would include: A duty-to-restriction review showing actual tasks, compatibility decision and unresolved clarification needs. Separate correction of the immediate problem from confirmation that the change works in later comparable conditions. A reviewer should check the actual control used and the scope represented by the evidence. If the same weakness recurs, reopen the issue and retain both the original decision and the new observation.

### What can be concluded

This solution establishes a bounded route from an identified gap to evidence and responsible acceptance. It does not establish that an assessment, clinical decision, technical test or employer authorization actually happened in a real company. The fictional case teaches how to decide and what to verify. Actual release remains with the designated employer/site authority after the applicable prerequisites are met.

## Applied scenario 2: an incomplete decision chain

A supervisor says a worker looks recovered and removes a valid clinical restriction without authorized review. At the handover, a second issue is identified: The restriction changes but the incoming shift uses an old duty plan. The receiving supervisor has the earlier record but does not yet have evidence that the new issue was resolved. A colleague proposes the following shortcut: Delete every medical and incident record to eliminate the problem. Work is due to begin on the next shift, so the supervisor needs a defensible decision that protects people and preserves a clear history.

### Worked solution — immediate decision

The first response is: Maintain the restriction and seek appropriate clinical clarification or updated capacity information. The reason is specific: Appearance and supervisory experience do not authorize a clinical capacity change. Valid restrictions remain until appropriately revised. Determine which assignment depends on that unresolved condition. Tell the affected people the restriction and who is coordinating resolution. If there is an immediate exposure, move to a safe position and use the established warning or emergency route rather than completing records first. The supervisor must not use a favorable overall company score as a substitute for this missing decision.

### Worked solution — resolve the additional issue

For the handover finding, the next action is: Update the operational plan and confirm receipt of the necessary change before allocation. The supporting record should show: A coordinated return record showing current capacity status, compatible duty limits and acknowledged allocation changes. This is important because return and unrestricted clearance are different states; assignment must use current valid limits with appropriate confidentiality. The receiving shift needs the actual status, not an assurance that someone intends to finish the check later. Identify the responsible role and obtain acknowledgment of the restriction. If the required authority or expertise is unavailable, the affected assignment remains unready; unrelated authorized work may be considered only after its interfaces are checked.

### Worked solution — reject the shortcut and verify the result

The proposed shortcut fails because status accuracy and privacy response are separate obligations; resolving one does not erase the other. The suitable decision is: Correct authorized operational status and separately initiate the confidentiality response for the disclosure. Evidence for review would include: A traceable status update and a separately restricted confidentiality incident response record. Separate correction of the immediate problem from confirmation that the change works in later comparable conditions. A reviewer should check the actual control used and the scope represented by the evidence. If the same weakness recurs, reopen the issue and retain both the original decision and the new observation.

### What can be concluded

This solution establishes a bounded route from an identified gap to evidence and responsible acceptance. It does not establish that an assessment, clinical decision, technical test or employer authorization actually happened in a real company. The fictional case teaches how to decide and what to verify. Actual release remains with the designated employer/site authority after the applicable prerequisites are met.

lessons.title: Final assessment — twenty questions
lessons.body: Answer each question individually. Apply the taught decisions to the facts given. Your first choices are retained. If an answer is wrong, read the specific explanation and explicitly acknowledge the corrected answer. A corrected score records learning after feedback; it does not overwrite the first-answer result. All twenty final questions and all six lesson checks must be completed.

lessons.title: Finish — separate practical qualification
lessons.body:
## Written completion and what it proves

Completion requires all 26 answered correctly or acknowledged remediation. Both first-answer and remediated scores remain separate. Completing the guided course is evidence that you worked through its knowledge and decision questions; it is not an observed practical performance result, a legal license, a provider certification or an employer authorization. Training evidence contributes to review within its scope and validity, rather than automatically establishing the whole company program.

## What needs separate assessment

The assessment should test recognition of an abnormal condition as well as routine performance. A person who can repeat a procedure but cannot identify when to stop has not demonstrated the whole task. Employer authorization should state the person, tasks, equipment or site limits, required supervision and the basis for the decision. Applicable legal, issuer, client and change-trigger requirements govern validity; this course invents no universal renewal period.

## Before actual work

Confirm current local instructions, reporting routes, emergency arrangements and the person who can resolve an operating hold. If assigned work exceeds your assessed scope, say so before accepting it. The Partner's job/site readiness decision remains separate from the company's evidence review. Preserve real records through the authorized process and protect personal information. The fictional examples in this course must never be submitted as evidence that your company performed the actions described.

lessons.title: Start here: Emergency plan and site interface
lessons.body:
# Emergency plan and site interface

This original VNDRLY course teaches decisions within the company safety program. Work through six lessons, their six checks, two worked scenarios and a 20-question final. All cases are fictional. No equipment operation is required to complete the online learning.

Each of the 26 questions requires a recorded answer. Completion requires a correct answer or explicit acknowledgment of the explanation and corrected answer after an error. Preserve the first-attempt score separately from the remediated score; a correction never rewrites what was first understood. Read the explanation, return to the relevant lesson and resolve uncertainty with the responsible supervisor. The course does not substitute for a site assessment, permit or employer authorization.

The linked references support the subject and identify source context. Client procedures are examples of client requirements, not universal law or endorsement of this course. Apply the governing jurisdiction and actual site procedure; no numerical technical limits or universal renewal interval are invented here.

## Primary reference context

[OSHA Emergency action plans](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.38). Read the reference within its stated scope. Company examples are not universal technical rules; regulatory applicability must be determined for the actual task and jurisdiction.

lessons.title: Lesson 1 - Plan from credible scenarios
lessons.body:
An emergency plan should reflect actual work and location. Identify credible fire, release, injury, severe weather, traffic, security and other events through the risk assessment. A plan copied from an office may not address a remote site, hazardous atmosphere or delayed access.

Define the worker's action and the interface with the site's system. Distinguish an employee's employer, the site operator and external responders. Clarify who raises the alarm, directs evacuation, accounts for people and controls technical response.

Avoid assuming all emergencies use the same route or muster point. A release can make one route unsafe while another event requires shelter. The applicable site plan establishes the response, not a universal instruction invented in this course.

## Worked field example

A remote service crew adopts an office fire plan without reviewing site releases or access.

The safe decision is to develop and coordinate the emergency arrangements for the actual work and site scenarios. An office plan does not automatically address remote industrial hazards or response constraints.

A useful field record is specific: A scenario-based company/site interface review with assigned actions and known limitations. It records observed conditions and the decision, rather than treating a signature as proof that the safeguard existed.

## Detailed emergency-interface application

Build each scenario around the actual work state. A crew replacing a component, a driver waiting at a gate and an office worker can face different warning and escape problems during the same release. The site assessment determines how they receive instructions and what safe action is possible. Do not assume everyone hears the same alarm or sees the same escape signs.

For a remote service, consider access and communication before the crew is isolated. The plan should identify what happens when the nearest public response capability cannot perform the required technical function. An emergency number is a contact mechanism, not a completed capability assessment.

Include interactions between employers. A contractor may have an internal call tree, but the site operator still needs prompt warning of a release or missing person. Agree which calls happen immediately, who coordinates updates and how duplicate or conflicting instructions are resolved. Preserve any uncertainty that prevents the planned activity from being ready.

lessons.title: Lesson 2 - Make alarm and notification actionable
lessons.body:
Workers need to recognize relevant alarms, know what they mean and have a reliable way to report an emergency. Include alternate methods for noise, failed phones, language needs and remote coverage. A contact list is useful only if the intended roles can be reached.

Give clear information: location, event, immediate hazards, people affected and safe access details. Do not delay the initial alarm while collecting every detail. Update the response coordinator as reliable information becomes available and distinguish observation from assumption.

Test receipt as well as transmission. A radio call made on the wrong channel or a message to an unattended number does not establish notification. Maintain a usable backup when the primary route fails.

## Worked field example

A worker sends an emergency message to a group chat that nobody is assigned to monitor.

The safe decision is to use the designated monitored alarm route and confirm the responsible role receives actionable information. A sent message is not evidence that emergency response has been activated.

A useful field record is specific: An end-to-end alarm test and verified current monitored contacts. It records observed conditions and the decision, rather than treating a signature as proof that the safeguard existed.

## Detailed emergency-interface application

An effective alarm instruction distinguishes the signal from the action. Workers should know whether the relevant signal requires evacuation, shelter or another site-specific response. Do not teach one sound as universal across all clients. At a new location, verify the current system and the method for people who cannot rely on the primary signal.

Test a report using usable location information. A receiving role should be able to identify the correct site and entrance from the message without guessing between similarly named gates. If the test exposes confusion, correct the information and repeat the affected link safely.

Provide a backup for foreseeable failure. Poor radio coverage, a discharged phone or an unavailable primary contact should not leave the worker inventing a route. The backup must be understood and available, with clear responsibility for acting. A list containing several numbers does not establish which role is monitoring them.

lessons.title: Lesson 3 - Define command and worker boundaries
lessons.body:
An emergency needs clear coordination. Workers should know the designated site command contact and their own role. They should not receive conflicting instructions from several employers without resolution through the established structure.

Most workers' duties are to alarm, withdraw or shelter, account and communicate. Technical shutdown, firefighting, rescue and medical actions require assigned trained roles and suitable conditions. A person who knows where a valve is located is not necessarily authorized to remain behind and operate it during an emergency.

The plan must identify any people who remain for critical operations and their conditions for withdrawal. Do not create such a role spontaneously after the alarm. Personal willingness does not establish safe capability.

## Worked field example

A general worker is told after an alarm to remain inside and shut down equipment without an assigned emergency role.

The safe decision is to withdraw under the plan and refer the shutdown decision to the designated trained and authorized role. Critical emergency duties must be planned and assigned rather than improvised during exposure.

A useful field record is specific: A role briefing and plan identifying authorized critical-operation duties and withdrawal limits. It records observed conditions and the decision, rather than treating a signature as proof that the safeguard existed.

## Detailed emergency-interface application

Command arrangements should remain understandable when several organizations are present. A contractor supervisor can account for their crew and give reliable information while the site command role coordinates the wider event. Technical specialists advise and act within their own competence. Do not allow a general manager's confidence to replace the required technical decision.

Workers should understand the difference between an assigned emergency action and an impulsive attempt to help. A person may be allowed to operate a remote emergency stop from a safe position under the plan but not enter a hazard to close a manual valve. The actual instruction and conditions define the boundary.

If conflicting directions arise, communicate them through the designated route rather than selecting the more convenient instruction. Report immediate danger and maintain the safe action available under the plan. The later review should identify why the interface failed so the next shift is not left with the same conflict.

lessons.title: Lesson 4 - Evacuate and account for everyone
lessons.body:
Know the site-specific evacuation or shelter instruction, route and destination. Include contractors, visitors, delivery drivers and people away from the main crew. A gate list may not reflect who has left or moved within the site; accountability needs a reliable current process.

On arrival, report through the assigned accountability role and stay available for instructions. Do not leave the muster area without reporting or re-enter to find a missing person. Give the coordinator the last known location and relevant hazards.

A missing name is information for the emergency response, not an invitation to unplanned rescue. The coordinator reconciles records and uses the planned safe response. A confident headcount is not reliable if it omitted an entire contractor group.

## Worked field example

A muster count matches the employee roster but excludes a contractor crew and two visitors.

The safe decision is to reconcile all affected groups through the accountability process and report unresolved people to command. A complete employee count does not establish accountability for everyone on site.

A useful field record is specific: A current reconciled muster record covering employees, contractors and visitors with unresolved cases escalated. It records observed conditions and the decision, rather than treating a signature as proof that the safeguard existed.

## Detailed emergency-interface application

Accountability begins before an alarm. The site needs a reliable method for knowing who is present, including visitors, short-term crews and delivery personnel where relevant. Arrivals, departures and employer handovers should not silently create gaps. The system must remain usable if ordinary network access or the main office is unavailable.

During muster, report the actual status: confirmed present, known safely elsewhere or unresolved. Do not infer safety from a vehicle being parked or a phone showing online. Give command the last reliable information and let the planned response resolve uncertainty.

Workers should remain available for the next instruction and tell the accountability role if they must move. Uncontrolled departure can trigger unnecessary searches or leave command with a false count. After the event, retain the original discrepancy and how it was resolved. A final complete count does not prove that the process worked without failures.

lessons.title: Lesson 5 - Provide usable responder access
lessons.body:
External responders need an accurate location and a usable route to the incident. Verify entrance names, coordinates where appropriate, gate access, approach restrictions and a safe guide arrangement. A postal address or map pin may point to an old entrance.

Coordinate with the site and relevant response services before reliance where the plan requires it. Confirm capabilities and access constraints rather than assuming a public number guarantees every type of technical response. Keep emergency routes clear during normal operations.

During an event, tell responders about changes such as blocked roads, hazardous areas or locked access. Do not position a guide inside an uncontrolled hazard. The guiding role needs a safe location and communication with command.

## Worked field example

The contact sheet directs responders to an old locked entrance behind an active construction zone.

The safe decision is to correct and verify usable access with the site authority and communicate it to all relevant roles. An emergency number cannot overcome inaccurate or inaccessible directions.

A useful field record is specific: A verified current entrance and safe responder-guide arrangement tested with the responsible roles. It records observed conditions and the decision, rather than treating a signature as proof that the safeguard existed.

## Detailed emergency-interface application

Responder access should be checked against the actual vehicle and incident. A small car may reach an entrance that cannot admit an emergency vehicle. A gate key may be stored with a person who is absent overnight. The responsible site roles verify the relevant arrangement instead of assuming an address is sufficient.

A guide needs a safe waiting position and a communication route to command. They should not stand inside an uncontrolled atmosphere, vehicle conflict area or falling-object zone to make themselves visible. If the usual entrance becomes unsafe, command communicates the alternative and any constraints to responders.

Keep ordinary deliveries and spectators from blocking access through the approved traffic plan. Gate workers need a manageable task assignment; processing normal arrivals while directing emergency vehicles can create conflict. The plan should identify when admissions stop, how exits are preserved and who takes over other essential duties.

lessons.title: Lesson 6 - Test and maintain the interface
lessons.body:
Plans become stale when layouts, contacts, staffing, work or response resources change. Review those changes and test the affected interface. A new phone number in a document is not enough until the intended role can actually receive and act.

Exercises should have observable objectives and safe boundaries. Test alarm, accountability, communication and access without introducing real danger. Record failures honestly and verify corrective actions.

Workers need a practical orientation at the actual site or a safe representative setting. Online learning can teach the process, but cannot show that a person recognizes the local alarm, reaches the right shelter or gives usable directions from that entrance.

## Worked field example

A revised emergency contact list is uploaded but night staff cannot access it and the number is untested.

The safe decision is to make the current arrangement accessible and verify the alarm/response route for the affected shift. A document update is not implemented until the people who rely on it can use it.

A useful field record is specific: A night-shift access and notification test with recorded receiver response. It records observed conditions and the decision, rather than treating a signature as proof that the safeguard existed.

## Detailed emergency-interface application

A useful interface exercise can test a fictional alarm from a remote work point, the receiving role's interpretation, the crew's accountability and the access directions. Record what was simulated and which actions were actually demonstrated. Do not introduce a real release or send people into live traffic to create realism.

Correct the specific failed link. If the receiver cannot identify the entrance, adding more general emergency posters may not solve it. Update the information, confirm access and repeat the relevant communication check. If a contractor crew is missing from muster, correct the current-person interface and retest that function.

Review after changes in layout, staffing, services or available responders. A plan can remain well written while becoming operationally stale. Preserve prior versions and decisions so users know which arrangement is current, and make the current instruction accessible to every affected shift before work relies on it.

## Further application

Keep the current instruction usable.

lessons.title: Two applied scenarios and worked solutions
lessons.body:
## Scenario 1

A fictional service crew arrives at a remote site after dark. Its company plan points to an old entrance. The site alarm differs from the one described in induction, and the crew has two visitors not on its employee roster. A supervisor says the existing plan is enough because the emergency telephone number is correct.

### Worked solution

The crew resolves the interface before affected work starts. The site authority confirms the actual alarm meanings, withdrawal or shelter instructions, routes, accountability process and usable responder entrance. Visitors are included. The company and site assign notification and command contacts and test the relevant communication. A correct telephone number is one component, not the entire plan. The crew receives an understandable briefing and demonstrates the assigned actions safely. Unresolved access or response limitations remain visible and may prevent the affected activity. The record identifies actual roles and conditions rather than merely recording induction attendance.

## Scenario 2

During a fictional release alarm, one contractor is missing from muster. A worker volunteers to search, while a manager wants everyone to leave the site immediately in personal vehicles.

### Worked solution

The accountability role gives command the unresolved name, last known location and reliable information. No unplanned search is authorized by willingness alone. Workers remain under the site evacuation/shelter and accountability instructions; uncontrolled departure can confuse the count and conflict with emergency traffic. Qualified response roles assess the search and other technical actions. Updates are recorded and passed to command, and any release from muster is communicated through the established process. Later review checks the roster interface and whether visitors and contractors were included. A resolved count does not erase a failure in the process.

lessons.title: Final assessment - 20 questions
lessons.body: Answer each question without consulting an answer key. There are 20 final questions in addition to six lesson checks. Incorrect responses require reading and explicitly acknowledging the explanation. Both the first-attempt and remediated results must remain visible.

lessons.title: Finish - Practical evaluation and work authorization

courses.title: R02 — Rescue plans and emergency equipment readiness
courses.purpose: Avoid relying on unavailable rescue or unplanned entry.
courses.practicalBoundary: 29 CFR 1910.146(k)(2)(iv) — Employer-designated employees performing covered permit-space rescue: Practice the assigned permit-space rescues at least every 12 months using the specified actual or representative spaces, subject to the real-rescue exception. This is a rescue-team duty, not a practical test required of every awareness-course learner. Source: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.146

content.title: R02 — Rescue plans and emergency equipment readiness
content.description: Original guided company-program course with six lessons, six checks, two worked scenarios and 20 final questions. First and remediated scores remain separate.

explanations.R02_check1: Hold the affected elevated work until qualified rescue planning verifies feasible available capability. A telephone number alone does not establish access, removal method or capable resources.
explanations.R02_check2: Verify a qualified rescue service with capability for the actual space and method. First-aid competence does not establish technical rescue competence.
explanations.R02_check3: Hold the affected work until suitable rescue availability is re-established and verified. Past capability does not prove that the required resources are available now.
