lessons.title: Start here: Management of change and renewal review
lessons.body:
# Management of change and renewal review

This original VNDRLY course teaches decisions within the company safety program. Work through six lessons, their six checks, two worked scenarios and a 20-question final. All cases are fictional. No equipment operation is required to complete the online learning.

Each of the 26 questions requires a recorded answer. Completion requires a correct answer or explicit acknowledgment of the explanation and corrected answer after an error. Preserve the first-attempt score separately from the remediated score; a correction never rewrites what was first understood. Read the explanation, return to the relevant lesson and resolve uncertainty with the responsible supervisor. The course does not substitute for a site assessment, permit or employer authorization.

The linked references support the subject and identify source context. Client procedures are examples of client requirements, not universal law or endorsement of this course. Apply the governing jurisdiction and actual site procedure; no numerical technical limits or universal renewal interval are invented here.

## Primary reference context

[OSHA Process safety management — covered processes only; check applicability](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.119). Read the reference within its stated scope. Company examples are not universal technical rules; regulatory applicability must be determined for the actual task and jurisdiction.

lessons.title: Lesson 1 - Recognize a safety-relevant change
lessons.body:
Changes can involve services, people, equipment, materials, software, layout, work methods, schedules and surrounding operations. Temporary changes can be as consequential as permanent ones. Screen the actual effect before implementation rather than only checking whether purchasing calls it a replacement.

A like-for-like claim requires evidence. A hose with a different rating, a new chemical formulation or a relocated gate can alter hazards and interfaces despite a familiar name. Ask what is different and which earlier assumptions may no longer hold.

Workers should report scope creep and unexpected conditions. The change process should provide a practical route to hold the affected activity and obtain review, not encourage people to hide small changes until they accumulate.

## Worked field example

A replacement chemical has a new formulation but is treated as like-for-like because the trade name is familiar.

The safe decision is to screen the actual formulation and affected controls before use. A familiar label does not prove unchanged hazards or assessment assumptions.

A useful field record is specific: A documented change screen linked to the actual formulation and task. It records observed conditions and the decision, rather than treating a signature as proof that the safeguard existed.

## Detailed application and verification

Screen change by effect rather than its administrative label. A purchasing system may call a new product a replacement, while the formulation, rating or operating instructions differ. A staffing change may alter monitoring or supervision even though no equipment moves. Temporary workarounds also deserve screening.

The worker or supervisor should describe the proposed difference and identify which existing assumptions might change. The responsible process then determines the level of technical and operational review. Do not demand that a worker independently solve every consequence before they are allowed to report the change.

Keep an accessible hold route. A change system that can be used only by office staff may fail during night work. The crew needs to know how to make the affected task safe, whom to contact and what cannot proceed without review. A verbal request to keep production moving does not resolve the missing decision.

lessons.title: Lesson 2 - Review technical and worker interfaces
lessons.body:
Identify affected hazards, controls, competence, documents, emergency arrangements and other employers. Involve appropriate technical specialists and the people who perform the work. A change can improve one task while creating exposure elsewhere.

Clarify the approval boundary. A manager may authorize expenditure without being qualified to approve a technical method. A vendor's recommendation may support review but does not automatically establish site suitability.

Record assumptions and unresolved questions. If a required technical condition is unknown, the affected startup is not ready. Do not fill a form with guessed values to make the workflow proceed.

## Worked field example

A new storage rack clears an exit but changes the forklift turning route.

The safe decision is to review the whole layout with affected workers and the appropriate traffic and facility authorities. A local improvement can transfer risk into another operation.

A useful field record is specific: An interface review covering emergency access, handling and vehicle movement. It records observed conditions and the decision, rather than treating a signature as proof that the safeguard existed.

## Detailed application and verification

Map the affected interfaces before approval. A relocated pump can alter hose routing, electrical supply, pedestrian access, noise and rescue access. A software change can alter alarms or safety-critical behavior. Review the whole affected system rather than a single favorable feature.

Involve the relevant workers because they know how the task is performed, including variations and workarounds. Their input complements technical expertise; it does not replace specialist design authority. Record both the practical issue and who makes the technical determination.

Where responsibilities cross employers, agree the decision and communication path. A contractor’s equipment approval may not establish suitability for the client’s process. Likewise, a client request does not supply the vendor’s missing operator competence. Keep each prerequisite identifiable so one signature is not used to imply every interface has been cleared.

lessons.title: Lesson 3 - Approve before implementation within defined authority
lessons.body:
The review should produce a clear decision: approved scope and conditions, required actions, restrictions, responsible roles and the period or triggers that limit reliance. Approval must precede the affected implementation unless an applicable controlled process explicitly governs an emergency change.

Do not confuse submission with approval. Uploading a renewal or sending a proposed procedure is evidence that review was requested. It does not restore expired permission or authorize changed work.

Preserve the basis and version of the decision. A later signature should not be backdated to imply an unreviewed period was authorized. Where work proceeded outside the process, report the actual state and control the exposure.

## Worked field example

A temporary authorization expires while a renewal file waits in a review queue.

The safe decision is to stop reliance on the expired authorization and obtain the required current decision and verified controls. A pending submission is not an approval or an extension.

A useful field record is specific: A current authorized decision with its scope, conditions and verified prerequisites. It records observed conditions and the decision, rather than treating a signature as proof that the safeguard existed.

## Detailed application and verification

Approval should identify the actual scope and version. Include conditions, required actions, restrictions and the person or role authorized to decide. A general signature without the reviewed configuration may be difficult to distinguish from permission for another arrangement.

Keep proposed, submitted and approved states separate. A renewal request can be complete as a submission while the operating authorization has expired. The system should display that distinction and prevent people from treating an upload as automatic extension.

If work has already proceeded outside the process, record the actual sequence and apply the required safe response. Do not backdate a signature to create the appearance of prior approval. The responsible authority evaluates the current condition and corrective action. Honest history supports learning and future control; rewritten history hides the failure mechanism.

lessons.title: Lesson 4 - Communicate and verify pre-start readiness
lessons.body:
Before startup, confirm required actions are complete, people understand the changed method and affected documents match the approved version. Include contractors and relief shifts, not just the people who attended the design meeting.

A document acknowledgment does not demonstrate operation of unfamiliar controls. Use the appropriate safe equipment-specific assessment and authorization.

Verify the field arrangement against the approved change: equipment identity, layout, protective functions, emergency access and any relevant technical checks. The exact verification follows the change scope; do not invent a generic technical test from this awareness lesson.

## Worked field example

The safe decision is to hold affected startup until the approved readiness actions and operator requirements are verified. Design approval does not establish that the operating shift can safely use the changed system.

A useful field record is specific: A pre-start verification linking approved actions, current instructions and assessed operators. It records observed conditions and the decision, rather than treating a signature as proof that the safeguard existed.

## Detailed application and verification

Pre-start verification connects the approved decision to the field. Confirm equipment identity, configuration, protective functions, documents, competence and emergency arrangements relevant to the change. The verifier should not tick actions they expect will be completed later.

Instruction must reach the shifts and contractors who operate the changed arrangement. Explain the difference, limits and failed-control response. A signed document acknowledgment is not proof that an operator can use an unfamiliar control.

A failed readiness item stays visible. The responsible authority may sequence unaffected work where safely justified, but cannot label the changed operation ready while required controls remain missing. Record the actual hold and next step. Startup occurs only through the defined authority after the applicable prerequisites are verified.

lessons.title: Lesson 5 - Control temporary changes and expiry
lessons.body:
Temporary changes need ownership, conditions and a defined path to restoration, extension through review or formal permanent adoption. Track the actual installed state, not only the planned end date. A temporary label does not reduce technical consequences.

Before expiry, the responsible role decides through the required review whether to restore the original arrangement, approve a revised temporary period or complete permanent change. An extension is a new controlled decision, not an automatic spreadsheet update.

If the authorization expires without a valid decision, stop relying on it and apply the appropriate safe operating restriction. Do not normalize a bypass merely because it has been in place for several shifts.

## Worked field example

A temporary protective-system bypass remains after expiry because production is stable.

The safe decision is to apply the required safe restriction and obtain competent technical/site resolution before further reliance. Stable production does not extend an expired authorization or restore the missing protective function.

A useful field record is specific: A tracked temporary-change status and verified restoration or valid reviewed authorization. It records observed conditions and the decision, rather than treating a signature as proof that the safeguard existed.

## Detailed application and verification

A temporary change register should reflect the real installed state. Identify the owner, approved conditions, expiry or review trigger, restoration method and required verification. The temporary label does not make a protective-system change low risk.

Monitor expiry early enough to obtain a real decision. Options may include restoration, a reviewed extension or permanent adoption through the appropriate process. Simply editing a date is not an extension. A submission pending at expiry does not preserve permission unless the governing authorization explicitly provides such an arrangement.

At expiry without a valid decision, use the required safe restriction and notify the responsible technical and operating roles. Do not treat stable output as proof that the missing safeguard is unnecessary. Preserve the original approval and each later decision so the authorization history remains understandable.

lessons.title: Lesson 6 - Validate operation and preserve history
lessons.body:
After startup, check whether the change performs as intended and whether new hazards or workarounds appear. Include worker feedback and the relevant technical measures. Successful installation is not the same as validated operation.

Close the change only after required actions and verification are complete. Preserve original assessment, decision, implementation and validation records, including restrictions and failed checks. Later reviewers need to understand what actually changed and why.

Renewal review should confirm current scope, evidence and governing requirements. It is not merely replacing an expired date. The applicable authority sets any validity period; this course imposes no universal renewal interval.

## Worked field example

A change is closed after installation even though operators report a new unsafe workaround.

The safe decision is to keep or reopen the change and verify the operating result and unresolved exposure. Installation completion does not establish that the changed work is safe and usable.

A useful field record is specific: A post-start validation record including worker feedback and resolved control issues. It records observed conditions and the decision, rather than treating a signature as proof that the safeguard existed.

## Detailed application and verification

Post-start validation asks whether the changed system works as intended under relevant conditions. Include worker feedback, technical results and new interfaces. A successful installation check can coexist with an operating problem that appears only during a delivery surge or shift handover.

Close required actions only on evidence. If a new control creates a workaround, investigate why and adjust the method through the appropriate review. Keep the change open or reopen it until the protective result is verified within the defined scope.

Renewal review should confirm current duties, equipment, evidence and applicable requirements rather than only replace a date. Preserve superseded records and clearly identify the current instruction. The course establishes no common validity period for all evidence. Technical, employer and site authorities retain their respective decisions, while online learning remains evidence of understanding the process.

## Further application

A software or scheduling change can be safety relevant even when no physical component is replaced. Changing an alarm priority, automatic action, monitoring contact or shift coverage can affect how a hazard is detected and managed. Screen the actual effect and involve the appropriate technical and worker roles before implementation.

For a controlled temporary arrangement, make restoration practical. Identify what must be removed or reinstated, who performs the work, how the safe state is verified and what documents or training return to the original version. An expiry date without a restoration path can leave the operation dependent on an unsupported workaround.

The handover must describe the installed state, not just the approved plan. If implementation differs, hold affected startup and return the difference for review. A project completion percentage cannot resolve a missing protective function or an operator who has not been assessed.

During validation, compare intended behavior with actual operation and worker experience. An alarm that functions technically but is routinely misunderstood may still leave a control gap. Preserve the finding and obtain the necessary correction and verification. Closing the change requires the defined actions and evidence; it does not erase the need to monitor future defects and reassess later changes.

Communicate every remaining operating restriction to the receiving shift.

lessons.title: Two applied scenarios and worked solutions
lessons.body:
## Scenario 1

A fictional site relocates its gate booth and installs a new access device. The layout reduces waiting time but sends pedestrians across a delivery lane. The device is technically installed, while night staff have not used it. The project owner wants immediate release.

### Worked solution

The change review addresses the complete interface rather than only queue performance. The traffic authority and affected workers review the pedestrian route, vehicle sweep, safe checking position and emergency access. Appropriate technical roles verify the device and protective functions. Night staff receive the current instruction and demonstrate assigned actions safely. Required actions are checked in the actual layout before startup. The owner records the approved configuration and limits. Post-start observation confirms whether pedestrians and vehicles use the intended arrangement without unsafe workarounds. Installation alone is not the release decision.

## Scenario 2

A fictional temporary equipment bypass reaches expiry. A renewal request is uploaded but has not been reviewed. The supervisor changes the spreadsheet date and continues because no fault has occurred.

### Worked solution

Reliance on the expired authorization stops through the required safe process. The appropriate technical and site authorities assess restoration or any revised authorization and verify controls. The upload is recorded as pending, not approved. The spreadsheet is corrected to preserve actual dates and the unauthorized gap rather than backdating a decision. The review examines why expiry monitoring failed and whether interim restrictions were maintained. Any approved continuation has explicit scope and conditions. A stable operating history does not establish that the missing protection is unnecessary.

lessons.title: Start here: Environmental release and spill emergency interface
lessons.body:
# Environmental release and spill emergency interface

This original VNDRLY course teaches decisions within the company safety program. Work through six lessons, their six checks, two worked scenarios and a 20-question final. All cases are fictional. No equipment operation is required to complete the online learning.

Each of the 26 questions requires a recorded answer. Completion requires a correct answer or explicit acknowledgment of the explanation and corrected answer after an error. Preserve the first-attempt score separately from the remediated score; a correction never rewrites what was first understood. Read the explanation, return to the relevant lesson and resolve uncertainty with the responsible supervisor. The course does not substitute for a site assessment, permit or employer authorization.

The linked references support the subject and identify source context. Client procedures are examples of client requirements, not universal law or endorsement of this course. Apply the governing jurisdiction and actual site procedure; no numerical technical limits or universal renewal interval are invented here.

## Primary reference context

[OSHA Hazardous waste operations and emergency response — check scope](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.120). Read the reference within its stated scope. Company examples are not universal technical rules; regulatory applicability must be determined for the actual task and jurisdiction.

lessons.title: Lesson 1 - Recognize a release and protect people
lessons.body:
A release may be a visible pool, spray, odor, sheen, damaged package or unexpected process condition. Identify what is known without entering the area to investigate. The material, energy, atmosphere and spread can all be uncertain.

The first concern is safe recognition, alarm and protection of people. A worker does not need to identify every chemical before reporting an emergency. Give the location, observations and known product information while clearly stating uncertainty.

Do not assume a small visible footprint means a minor event. Vapor, pressure, underground migration or a continuing source can create hazards beyond the pool. The authorized response determines the assessment. Keep others clear through the safe site process rather than standing inside the hazard to warn them.

## Worked field example

A fuel release produces an unfamiliar atmosphere near a working gate.

The safe decision is to keep people clear and raise the alarm through the approved release plan. Visible liquid does not describe all vapor, energy and spread hazards.

A useful field record is specific: An actionable alarm with location, observed conditions, known material and uncertainty stated. It records observed conditions and the decision, rather than treating a signature as proof that the safeguard existed.

## Further application

The initial report should distinguish observations from identification. A sheen, odor, spray or unusual equipment condition can justify warning without proving the exact material. Describe what is seen from safety and provide reliable labels or process information already available. Do not approach the source simply to make the report more precise.

A release can change quickly. Material may continue entering the area, vapors may move beyond the liquid and weather may alter the affected direction. The responsible response coordinator needs updates through the agreed route. General workers should know how to withdraw and keep other people clear without creating another traffic or access hazard.

Include people beyond the immediate crew. A gate attendant, adjacent contractor or cleaner may encounter the release without understanding its origin. The plan should provide usable warning and safe route information. A small incident footprint on a form does not establish that all exposed groups have been considered.

lessons.title: Lesson 2 - Know the response boundary before work
lessons.body:
The plan defines who can take initial actions and under what conditions. A trained worker may have a limited assessed role, but a spill kit alone does not establish competence, suitable PPE or safe atmospheric conditions. Know the stop and withdrawal triggers.

Distinguish an incidental condition within the trained role from an uncontrolled or uncertain emergency requiring specialist response. The competent employer/site process establishes the boundary; this course does not invent a universal spill-volume threshold.

Never enter an unknown atmosphere or approach uncontrolled energy to protect property or a drain. If a safe remote action is assigned and the conditions are verified, follow the plan. Otherwise withdraw and provide information to the responsible response roles.

## Worked field example

An untrained worker is told to enter an unknown vapor area because absorbent pads are available.

The safe decision is to withdraw and obtain the authorized specialist response instead of entering with the kit. Equipment availability does not establish a safe response capability.

A useful field record is specific: A role-specific response plan and verified trained, equipped and authorized resources. It records observed conditions and the decision, rather than treating a signature as proof that the safeguard existed.

## Further application

Response capability depends on the person, equipment, material and conditions together. A worker may be trained for a limited known spill on an open floor but not for an unknown atmosphere, pressurized release or reactive mixture. The role boundary must be explicit enough to guide stopping and escalation.

The spill kit should match the assessed scope and be accessible without entering the danger area. Check its status through the approved process. Missing absorbents or damaged protective equipment can invalidate the limited initial response, while a complete kit still does not authorize emergency entry.

When the situation exceeds the planned capability, withdraw and activate qualified assistance. Do not use the absence of visible symptoms or a colleague’s confidence as proof that conditions are safe. The competent response authority makes the technical assessment. The worker's useful action is prompt recognition and reliable communication within a protected role.

lessons.title: Lesson 3 - Coordinate alarm, access and command
lessons.body:
Environmental response interfaces with fire, medical, security, operations and external services. The plan must identify who coordinates the response and who controls technical actions. Avoid conflicting instructions from different employers.

Provide usable directions, safe access and current hazards. Gate staff may need to stop ordinary arrivals, keep emergency routes clear and direct responders from a safe location. They must not guide responders through an unassessed release area.

Keep communication factual and current. Report changes in wind, spread, blocked access or people affected through command. A rumor about the material should not be passed as a confirmed identity. Do not delay urgent warning while waiting for a polished report.

## Worked field example

Responders are directed to an entrance now downwind of the release and blocked by a delivery.

The safe decision is to notify command and coordinate a verified safe access and traffic arrangement. An entrance listed in the plan may become unsuitable during the actual event.

A useful field record is specific: A current responder-access decision and communicated gate/traffic controls. It records observed conditions and the decision, rather than treating a signature as proof that the safeguard existed.

## Further application

Command should coordinate technical control, worker protection, environmental action and external assistance. Different employers may need to make internal notifications, but those calls must not delay the site alarm. Agree who passes updates and who confirms the current access arrangement.

Gate and traffic roles can be important during a release. Ordinary arrivals may need to pause, emergency routes remain clear and drivers need a safe holding instruction. The attendant must not stand in the affected atmosphere to enforce access. Use the reviewed safe position and emergency traffic method.

A responder guide should know the current entrance, route restrictions and contact with command. If wind or spread changes the route, update the direction promptly. An old map can be useful background but cannot override current hazards. Preserve uncertainty and report changes rather than sending responders toward the nearest familiar gate by habit.

lessons.title: Lesson 4 - Prevent spread only within an authorized safe role
lessons.body:
The desire to protect soil or water does not justify exposure. Source isolation, drain protection and containment require the appropriate competence, equipment and safe access. A visible valve may be within a hazardous atmosphere or connected to stored energy.

Where the plan permits a limited initial action, confirm the prerequisites and withdrawal conditions. Do not improvise berms, pumps or chemicals without review; they can redirect the release, create incompatibility or expose another area.

The specialist response considers source control, atmosphere, ignition, spread and recovery together. General workers provide reliable information and preserve the boundary. They should not start cleanup merely because the release has stopped visibly.

## Worked field example

A worker is asked to reach a valve through a liquid pool to protect a nearby drain.

The safe decision is to keep clear unless the assigned authorized response has verified safe access and conditions. Protecting the environment does not remove the worker’s exposure to material and energy hazards.

A useful field record is specific: A specialist decision on source/drain controls with verified access and assigned roles. It records observed conditions and the decision, rather than treating a signature as proof that the safeguard existed.

## Further application

Containment should not transfer the hazard. An improvised barrier can redirect liquid toward another occupied area, and an unsuitable absorbent or chemical can create incompatibility. Technical responders determine the appropriate method for the material and conditions.

Source control may involve pressure, electrical equipment or process isolation. The fact that a valve is reachable does not establish that operating it is safe or within the worker's authority. If a safe remote action is assigned in the plan, follow its conditions; otherwise provide information and remain clear.

Drain protection and environmental urgency are part of the response, but not a waiver of worker safety. A person must not enter an unknown atmosphere or cross a hazardous pool to protect a receptor. Qualified roles balance source, atmosphere, ignition, spread and recovery through the approved response. Ordinary awareness training does not authorize those technical decisions.

lessons.title: Lesson 5 - Route reporting through responsible owners
lessons.body:
Environmental notification requirements depend on material, quantity, location, receiving environment and jurisdiction. The responsible environmental/legal authority determines the applicable reporting route and timing. This course supplies no universal reportable quantity or deadline.

Workers should promptly report observations and preserve reliable information: time, location, known material, source, estimated extent with uncertainty, actions and affected receptors. Do not fabricate precision or delay escalation until every figure is confirmed.

Company, site, regulator and emergency-service notifications may serve different purposes. Confirm who owns each obligation and keep a record of actual contacts and instructions. A message to a supervisor is not automatically proof that every required external notification occurred.

## Worked field example

A supervisor assumes an internal incident form satisfies every environmental reporting duty.

The safe decision is to refer notification decisions to the responsible environmental authority and record actual required contacts. Internal reporting and external obligations are distinct processes with scope-specific requirements.

A useful field record is specific: A notification decision and contact record showing responsible owner, basis and actual actions. It records observed conditions and the decision, rather than treating a signature as proof that the safeguard existed.

## Further application

Reporting information often develops over time. Begin with reliable observations and clearly marked estimates, then update the responsible owner as better information becomes available. Do not postpone urgent notification merely because the exact quantity or full material identity is uncertain.

The environmental authority determines applicable obligations from jurisdiction, material, location, quantity and impact. This course gives no universal reportable volume, deadline or regulator list. Internal notification, emergency calls and external environmental reporting can have different owners and purposes; the plan should make each responsibility visible.

Keep a factual contact record. Identify who was contacted, when, what information was supplied and any instructions received. A completed internal form does not show that a required external call occurred. Where confidentiality or legal review affects documentation, use the authorized process without fabricating certainty or deleting the operational history.

lessons.title: Lesson 6 - Control cleanup, waste and return to use
lessons.body:
Cleanup can create new exposure through contaminated soil, absorbents, equipment and recovered material. Use qualified personnel and the approved waste route. Do not place hazardous residues in general waste or return contaminated tools to ordinary use without review.

Return to use requires the responsible authority to verify the area, equipment, remaining restrictions and any environmental follow-up. A clean-looking surface does not establish that the atmosphere, ground or drainage is acceptable.

Review the cause and response interfaces after the event. Check whether alarms, access, response resources and reporting worked. Preserve the original record, corrective actions and verification. Online learning and a completed spill form remain separate from specialist cleanup and technical handback.

## Worked field example

A cleaned yard is reopened while unsealed contaminated absorbents remain beside an occupied walkway.

The safe decision is to maintain suitable control until cleanup, waste handling and return-to-use conditions are verified. Visible surface cleaning does not resolve remaining contaminated material or exposure.

A useful field record is specific: A scope-specific cleanup/waste record and authorized handback with remaining restrictions clear. It records observed conditions and the decision, rather than treating a signature as proof that the safeguard existed.

## Further application

Cleanup and disposal need their own controlled work scope. Contaminated absorbents, soil, clothing and equipment can continue to expose workers after the visible liquid is removed. Identify who handles them, what information they need and the approved packaging, storage, transport and receiving route.

Return to use should state the actual area and conditions verified, the responsible authority and any remaining restrictions or follow-up. A clean photograph does not establish atmosphere, subsurface condition or waste acceptability. Technical verification and environmental decisions remain with the appropriate competent roles.

The post-event review asks how the release occurred and how the response functioned. Examine alarms, access, materials, equipment, staffing and reporting interfaces. Correct the actual failed mechanism and verify the result in relevant work. Preserve the original event, estimates, decisions and later updates. A revised training record alone does not establish that a defective transfer system or incompatible waste arrangement has been corrected.

A release review should include people who encountered the event outside the main response team. A driver may have received conflicting gate instructions, or a cleaner may have handled contaminated material after the technical crew left. Their information can reveal a handover gap that the incident timeline otherwise misses.

The owner then defines a correction that addresses that interface and verifies it safely. A revised contact list, waste label or access instruction must reach the actual users. Check the receiving role and field arrangement rather than counting distributed messages. Preserve any limitation and unresolved specialist decision so the next operation does not mistake an administrative update for verified response capability.

lessons.title: Two applied scenarios and worked solutions
lessons.body:
## Scenario 1

At a fictional fuel delivery area, a hose fails and liquid spreads toward a drain. The air has an unfamiliar odor, and trucks are still arriving. A manager hands an untrained gate worker a spill kit and asks them to cross the pool to close a valve.

### Worked solution

The worker stays clear, raises the alarm and uses the approved gate/traffic response from a safe location. They do not cross the pool or enter the uncertain atmosphere. Command receives the known fuel, location, continuing source, drain concern and traffic conditions, with uncertainty explicit. Qualified response roles determine source isolation, atmosphere, ignition and containment. Environmental urgency does not authorize unprotected entry. Responders receive a safe verified access route rather than the nearest entrance by habit. After control, the responsible environmental owner determines reporting and waste arrangements. Return to use follows the authorized verification, not the disappearance of visible liquid.

## Scenario 2

A fictional cleaning release is absorbed from the floor. Workers put used pads into an open general-waste bin. The material identity is uncertain, and the internal form estimates a precise quantity without a basis. Management proposes closing the event because the floor is dry.

### Worked solution

The area and waste remain controlled while the competent authority establishes the material information, contamination and suitable handling/disposal route. The estimate is corrected to show its basis and uncertainty rather than preserving invented precision. The environmental owner determines applicable notification and follow-up. Authorized people verify return-to-use conditions, including waste and adjacent areas. The review examines product identification, response limits and why cleanup was treated as complete before waste was controlled. A dry floor is one observation, not a comprehensive handback.

lessons.title: Final assessment - 20 questions
lessons.body: Answer each question without consulting an answer key. There are 20 final questions in addition to six lesson checks. Incorrect responses require reading and explicitly acknowledging the explanation. Both the first-attempt and remediated results must remain visible.

content.title: G01 — Hazardous-material transportation: recognition and safe handoff
content.description: Finished VNDRLY foundation instruction in recognizing transport functions, protecting containment, checking information, stopping unsafe handoffs and escalating within assigned authority.

explanations.G01_check1: Answer: B. Loading authorization does not automatically cover classification or certification. The approved determination and the person responsible for that function must be established before the shipment proceeds.
explanations.G01_check2: Answer: C. The load and its approved information must agree. A placard cannot resolve a package identity or quantity mismatch, and an unauthorized handwritten change can create another error.
explanations.G01_check3: Answer: A. Possible loss of containment requires a controlled response. Unknown exposure, unsuitable tools or improvised repackaging can increase the hazard.
explanations.G01_check4: Answer: B. Transport compatibility and segregation depend on the actual shipment. Neither sealed packages nor improvised spacing establishes that the combination is permitted or adequately controlled.
explanations.G01_check5: Answer: C. Awareness training does not equip a worker for a hazardous-atmosphere rescue. A second casualty delays rescue and exposes responders to additional danger.
explanations.G01_check6: Answer: C. Changing function or mode can introduce requirements outside the previous training. The employer must establish and verify the additional instruction and authorization.
explanations.G01_final1: Answer: A. Preparation and offering functions can affect transport safety before departure; the requirements are not limited to drivers.
explanations.G01_final2: Answer: B. Waste composition and shipment conditions matter. Similar names or prior loads cannot replace a verified determination.
explanations.G01_final3: Answer: C. Package, document and placarding checks have different functions and must be reconciled.
explanations.G01_final4: Answer: A. Changing regulated shipment information requires the appropriate function knowledge and authority.
explanations.G01_final5: Answer: B. Access to information is useful but does not itself establish classification competence or authority.
explanations.G01_final6: Answer: C. Bulging can indicate a containment or pressure problem. Opening or transporting it without a controlled decision can increase exposure.
explanations.G01_final7: Answer: A. An overpack has specific uses and cannot be treated as an improvised compliance or leak-repair solution.
explanations.G01_final8: Answer: B. Draining does not eliminate every hazard or settle the regulatory status of residue packaging.
explanations.G01_final9: Answer: C. Movement with connected equipment can rupture hoses and cause a release. Follow the controlled procedure.
explanations.G01_final10: Answer: A. Appearance and available space cannot establish chemical compatibility or transport compliance.
explanations.G01_final11: Answer: B. Loss of a required control is a reason to stop, not replace it with an unapproved assumption.
explanations.G01_final12: Answer: C. Vehicle identity does not verify compartment selection, compatibility or remaining capacity.
explanations.G01_final13: Answer: A. Accurate safe-position information helps responders without creating another casualty.
explanations.G01_final14: Answer: B. Release magnitude alone does not establish a safe response level, especially when the substance is unknown.
explanations.G01_final15: Answer: C. The concern needs authorized investigation without exposing sensitive routing information or creating confrontation.
explanations.G01_final16: Answer: A. A new regulated function can require different instruction, testing and employer authorization.
explanations.G01_final17: Answer: B. The recurrence interval does not excuse missing instruction for a new function or changed requirements.
explanations.G01_final18: Answer: C. A learner cannot treat a regulatory deadline as self-authorization to work independently.
explanations.G01_final19: Answer: A. Online knowledge completion and practical or function-specific authorization are distinct evidence.
explanations.G01_final20: Answer: B. The record must describe the training actually completed and must not exaggerate its scope.

lessons.title: Before you begin
lessons.body:
This VNDRLY course teaches how to recognize a hazardous-material transport task, protect a shipment handoff, detect mismatches and act within your authority. It is intended for workers whose duties may include preparing, offering, loading, unloading, dispatching or transporting hazardous material. It uses U.S. highway-related examples; actual materials, functions, transport modes and jurisdictions determine the employer’s additional requirements.

Work through six lessons and answer each knowledge check. Read two worked scenarios, then answer the twenty-question final assessment. You must resolve all twenty-six questions to complete this guided course. Your first answers remain in the original score. After an incorrect answer, read the explanation and explicitly acknowledge the correction; the corrected score records that remediation. Completion requires 100% correct after any remediation.

lessons.title: Recognize the transportation task before touching the load
lessons.body:
Hazardous-material transportation begins before a truck leaves the yard. A person who chooses a package, prepares shipping information, loads a vehicle or accepts a shipment can affect transportation safety. A driver’s license does not establish that everyone upstream has performed those functions correctly. Your first decision is to identify the exact job you are being asked to perform: prepare, package, document, offer, load, unload, drive, or arrange transportation. Your employer must establish which requirements apply to each function. If your authorization covers loading only, do not assume it also authorizes classification or shipping-paper preparation.

A familiar product name is not a transportation classification. An SDS can provide useful information, including a transportation section, but the actual material, formulation, condition, concentration and shipment circumstances must be considered by the person responsible for classification. A used solvent or oilfield waste can differ from the unused product. “Produced water,” “empty,” “nonhazardous waste” and “it went this way last time” do not independently settle transportation requirements. Ask for the approved classification or documented determination for this load. Do not invent a proper shipping name or select a UN number from a similar product.

Compare the request with your training and assigned authority. If a dispatcher asks you to sign a shipper certification that you have never been trained or authorized to make, stop that step and contact the responsible shipping specialist. Explain what is missing: the material identity, the approved determination, the packaging instruction or your function-specific authorization. This is a controlled handoff, not a refusal to communicate. Other work can continue only where the supervisor confirms it does not depend on the unresolved shipment.

This course teaches recognition and safe handoff. It does not authorize you to classify every chemical or prepare every mode of shipment. Air, highway, rail and vessel shipments can have different requirements. An additional employer-directed module must teach the exact functions you perform, and the employer must test, certify and retain the applicable training records.

lessons.title: Read the shipment as one consistent set of information
lessons.body:
A shipment communicates its hazards through several coordinated elements. Depending on the shipment, these can include shipping papers, package marks and labels, vehicle placards and emergency-response information. These elements perform different jobs. A package label communicates a hazard on the package; a placard provides a larger transport warning where required; a shipping paper describes the consignment. One does not automatically replace another. Your function-specific instruction must show which elements are required for your material, quantity, package and transport mode.

Before accepting or loading, compare the actual load with the approved shipment information within your assigned role. Check the product or waste identity, package count and type, and any required markings and labels against the controlled documents. Use the employer’s approved checklist. Do not rely on a truck already having a placard as proof that every package and document is correct. A placard remaining from an earlier load can mislead responders and does not validate the current consignment.

Suppose the load sheet says two drums while three are staged, and the third drum has a different product label. Do not “correct” the paperwork to match what is in front of you unless you are trained and authorized to make that change using verified information. Hold acceptance or loading, segregate the disputed item through the approved process, and have the responsible person reconcile the physical load and the documents. Record the specific discrepancy rather than a vague note such as “paperwork issue.”

Emergency-response information must be available in the manner required for the shipment, including during transportation. Drivers need their mode-specific instruction on accessibility and location; office staff need their instruction on providing accurate information. An emergency telephone number printed on a form is useful only if the approved response arrangements meet the applicable requirements. Never replace the approved number with someone who has not accepted that responsibility.

When a document is revised, confirm that everyone relying on the old version receives the corrected controlled information. A dispatcher’s text message saying “all good” is not a substitute for resolving a material mismatch.

lessons.title: Inspect packages and protect containment
lessons.body:
Packaging is a containment system, not just a container that happens to fit. The approved package must be suitable for the material, its quantity and condition, and the transportation circumstances. Closures, gaskets, liners, pressure provisions and any overpack are part of that system. A drum that looks identical to another may have different specifications or closure instructions. Your job-specific training must identify the approved package and tell you which inspections and closure tasks you may perform.

Perform the employer’s pre-loading acceptance checks from a safe position. Look for visible damage, wetness, staining, corrosion, bulging, missing closures and inconsistent markings. Do not open, sniff, touch or tighten an unknown leaking package to discover what it contains. A strong smell is a warning; the absence of smell is not proof that a package is safe. If you see a possible leak, stop handling, keep people away, notify the designated supervisor and follow the site’s release procedure. The response depends on the substance and conditions, and must be directed by people trained for that response level.

Do not improvise repairs with tape, an available cap or a second container. An overpack is not permission to conceal a leaking or noncompliant package. Authorized specialists must decide whether recovery, repackaging, salvage packaging or another action is appropriate. Keep identification and required hazard communication available during the controlled response.

Empty packaging may retain hazardous residue. A tank, tote or drum that has been drained can still contain vapor, liquid films or pressure. Do not remove required hazard communication or treat it as unrestricted cargo merely because the delivery is complete. The responsible person must establish the applicable empty-package or residue status.

At handoff, distinguish a package you inspected from one you merely saw on the pallet. If your checklist requires individual inspection, sample checking is not equivalent. Report defects with the package identifier and observed condition, and prevent the rejected item from being accidentally loaded by the next shift.

lessons.title: Control loading, unloading and incompatible work
lessons.body:
Loading is an operating task with moving vehicles, stored energy and possible chemical exposure. Before starting, establish who controls the vehicle and loading area. Follow the approved vehicle-securement, access-control and communication procedures. A driver moving unexpectedly while a hose is connected or a loader is inside the vehicle can create a serious release or crush injury. Do not assume that another person has secured the vehicle because it is stationary.

Check the load plan and compatibility instructions for the actual materials. Products that are individually contained can still require separation during transportation. A general chemical-storage chart is not a complete transport segregation instruction. If the instructions do not cover the proposed combination, stop and obtain a determination from the authorized shipping specialist. Do not decide that two sealed packages are compatible simply because they cannot normally touch.

For bulk transfers, verify the approved source, receiving compartment, material compatibility, available capacity, connections and communication method through the site’s transfer procedure. Confirm the trained operator has performed the required equipment checks. A correct truck number is not enough if the wrong compartment is selected. Stop transfer if there is unexpected movement, leakage, loss of communication, an abnormal instrument indication or a person entering the exclusion area. Your authority to stop does not depend on proving the exact failure first.

Secure cargo using the approved method for the package, vehicle and journey. Restraints must prevent the movement they are intended to control without damaging the packages. The right number of straps cannot compensate for an unsuitable restraint system or a damaged anchor point. Any loading, unloading, cargo-securement or bulk-transfer qualification beyond this awareness course must be assessed on the actual equipment and task.

Before release, reconcile the final physical load with the approved documents and confirm that rejected cargo is excluded. Pass the receiving driver the required information through the designated process. A hurried change of driver or trailer is a new handoff that needs checking; it is not an administrative detail to fill in after departure.

lessons.title: Recognize emergencies and protect yourself before reporting
lessons.body:
A transportation incident may begin as a small wet patch, an unusual hiss, a shifted package or an unexpected vapor cloud. You do not need to identify the exact chemical before stopping an unsafe task and notifying the designated contact. Keep a safe distance, move away from the exposure and prevent others from approaching where you can do so without entering danger. Avoid low areas or enclosed spaces where a released substance might accumulate. Follow the site emergency plan and responder instructions for the actual conditions.

Do not walk into the release to read a label. Give responders information already available from a safe place: location, vehicle or package identification, observed conditions, people affected and the approved shipping information. State clearly what you do not know. Guessing a substance or quantity can misdirect a response. If someone is overcome, do not make an unprotected rescue entry. Call the designated emergency response and provide the casualty’s last known location.

Response authority is separate from ordinary loading or driving authority. A loader trained to report an incident is not thereby trained to stop a leak, enter a vapor area or manage a hazardous-material emergency. Some minor, incidental releases can be handled under an employer’s established procedure by appropriately trained people; that determination must come from the actual conditions and competent response arrangements. Do not downgrade an unfamiliar release to avoid calling for assistance.

Security concerns also need prompt reporting. An unexplained broken seal, unauthorized access, a suspicious routing request or a missing package may affect the shipment’s safety and security. Follow the employer’s reporting process without confronting a potentially violent person or circulating sensitive routing information publicly. Employees assigned duties under a required security plan need instruction in the relevant plan, beyond general awareness.

After the immediate response, preserve the information needed for investigation without delaying medical help or entering an unsafe area. Record observed facts and the actions you took. Incident reporting and regulatory notifications must be handled by the designated responsible people; a worker’s internal report should get accurate information to them promptly.

lessons.title: Confirm authorization when jobs, materials or modes change
lessons.body:
Training must match the functions you actually perform. Before starting a new transport-related duty, tell your supervisor what has changed. Examples include moving from loading to shipping-paper preparation, changing from highway to air shipments, handling a new material or operating a different bulk-transfer system. Prior experience with a similar task is useful background, but it does not establish the specific knowledge and demonstrated capability required for the new function.

PHMSA describes a training program that includes general awareness, function-specific training, safety and security awareness, and in-depth security training where a security plan is required. Applicable mode-specific instruction is also necessary. This foundation course contributes to recognition and safe handoff; it is not a blanket statement that those elements have all been completed. The employer must determine the full program, test the employee as required, certify the training and keep the necessary records.

For U.S. HMR duties, PHMSA states that recurrent training is required at least every three years. A new or changed function also requires the applicable training; the three-year cycle is not permission to wait while performing unfamiliar duties independently. Although the regulations provide a supervised-training route in specified circumstances, a learner must not self-authorize using a deadline. The employer must establish that the conditions for that route are satisfied and provide the required direct supervision. Other jurisdictions and transport modes can impose additional requirements.

Keep your training evidence accurate. A completion record should identify the actual course and version, the date, the original result and any remediation, and the person or organization responsible for the training. Do not rename this foundation as a complete dangerous-goods shipping qualification. A perfect remediated score means the course’s questions have been resolved; it does not prove equipment skill or qualify every function.

When you discover a gap, document the affected task and notify the responsible supervisor before performing it independently. The useful outcome is a clear assignment of the missing instruction, supervised practice or assessment, followed by verified authorization. A row marked complete in software cannot make an untrained shipment safe.

lessons.title: Worked scenarios: resolve the handoff
lessons.body:
Scenario 1 — An urgent waste pickup. You are a loader trained to move approved, sealed packages. The staged shipment contains two drums listed on the load sheet and an additional tote marked only “used treatment chemical.” A dispatcher says the customer needs everything gone and suggests using the UN number from last month’s load.

Step 1: Identify your function and limits. You can inspect and load an approved shipment; you cannot classify an unidentified waste through comparison. Step 2: Stop the disputed acceptance/loading step and keep the tote out of the approved load through the yard’s controlled hold process. Do not erase its existing identification or open it to investigate. Step 3: Tell the supervisor exactly what is missing: verified identity, approved classification and shipment instructions for the tote. Step 4: The authorized shipping specialist obtains the needed information and reconciles packaging, documentation and the proposed transport arrangement. Step 5: Recheck the final approved load before release. If the two drums depart separately, that shipment must have its own accurate information; removing the tote must not leave incorrect counts or references.

The outcome is not “the loader chose a more conservative UN number.” The correct outcome is that an authorized determination and safe handoff replace an unsupported guess. Urgency changes the need for communication, not the worker’s classification authority.

Scenario 2 — A bulk-transfer interruption. During a planned transfer, a radio fails. The receiving operator is no longer visible, and a bystander says there is probably enough capacity. A wet patch appears near a connection.

Step 1: Stop through the approved transfer procedure because communication has been lost and containment may be compromised. Do not continue to an estimated volume. Step 2: Keep people away from the possible release and notify the designated response contact from a safe position. Do not tighten a leaking connection under pressure. Step 3: Give responders the known material and shipment information, the location and your observations. Do not enter the area to obtain more detail. Step 4: Authorized personnel assess and resolve the release, verify equipment condition, receiving capacity and communications, and determine whether restart is permitted. Step 5: Before resuming, the trained operator completes the required checks and briefs everyone affected by the interruption.

Your foundation training supports the stop and report decisions. Repair, recovery, emergency response and restart authorization remain with people trained and assigned for those functions.

lessons.title: Final assessment
lessons.body: Answer every final question using the decisions taught in the lessons. Do not infer authorization from urgency, a familiar product name or a prior certificate. Any incorrect first answer remains in your original score and must be explicitly remediated.

lessons.title: Complete the knowledge component; confirm the next task
lessons.body:
After all checks and final questions are correctly resolved, this course’s knowledge component is complete. Keep both the original and remediated results. Before independent work, confirm your employer’s instruction, testing, certification and authorization for the actual materials, functions and transport modes. This course is not that evaluation.

If your current duties exceed the training recorded for you, report the specific gap to the responsible supervisor. Do not label this foundation as complete hazardous-material shipping qualification. Your employer’s approved shipment procedures and current applicable requirements remain the working instructions.

## Legal requirements for the named work role
These apply only when you perform the work described below. They are not additional steps for completing this online course.

49 CFR 172.702(d), 172.704(a), (d) — Hazmat employees performing functions covered by the Hazardous Materials Regulations: Provide the applicable function-specific training and testing and retain the employer training record specified in (d). No universal separate practical examination or VNDRLY evidence upload is prescribed by these provisions. Source: https://www.phmsa.dot.gov/training/hazmat/training-requirements-industry

questions.prompt: You are trained to load approved packages. A supervisor asks you to classify an unfamiliar waste and sign the shipper certification. What should you do?

options.label: Choose the classification used for a similar waste.
Hold that step and obtain the approved determination and authorized shipping specialist.
Sign because the supervisor requested it.

questions.prompt: Three drums are staged, but the approved load information lists two and the third has a different label. What is the correct action?

options.label: Load all three because the vehicle has placards.
Cross out the package count and continue.
Hold the discrepancy for authorized reconciliation before acceptance or loading.

questions.prompt: A drum is wet around its closure and the contents are unfamiliar. What should the loader do?

options.label: Stop handling, keep others clear and initiate the designated release/defect response.
Tighten the closure with whatever tool is available.
Put the drum in an overpack and hide the old label.

questions.prompt: The approved load plan does not cover a proposed combination of two hazardous materials. What should happen?

options.label: Load them together if the packages are sealed.
Obtain an authorized compatibility/segregation determination before loading.
Ask the driver to keep the packages at opposite ends without further review.

questions.prompt: A worker collapses near an unidentified vapor release. You have awareness training only. What is the correct first response?

options.label: Enter quickly while holding your breath.
Move the leaking package before calling for help.
Stay clear, call the designated emergency response and report the casualty location.

questions.prompt: A highway loader is now asked to prepare an air shipment. What establishes readiness?

options.label: The previous loader certificate covers every transport mode.
Completion of this foundation alone.
Employer-confirmed instruction, testing and authorization for the new function and applicable mode.

questions.prompt: Which task can directly affect hazardous-material transportation safety?

options.label: Preparing shipment documents.
Only driving on a public road.
Only responding after an accident.

questions.prompt: What establishes the transport classification of an unfamiliar waste?

options.label: Its informal yard name.
An approved determination for the actual material and shipment.
The label on a similar unused product.

questions.prompt: A placard is already on the trailer. What can you conclude?

options.label: Every package is correctly documented.
The present load is automatically acceptable.
The placard alone does not validate the load or its documents.

questions.prompt: Who should resolve a shipping-paper mismatch?

options.label: A trained, authorized person using verified shipment information.
Whoever can edit the form fastest.
The newest worker as practice without supervision.

questions.prompt: When may a loader classify a chemical?

options.label: Whenever the driver asks.
When trained and authorized for that function using the approved process.
Whenever the SDS is available.

questions.prompt: What is the safest response to a bulging unknown package?

options.label: Open it slightly to release pressure.
Load it last so it is easy to reach.
Stop handling and notify the designated responsible person from a safe position.

questions.prompt: What does an overpack automatically accomplish?

options.label: It does not automatically make a leaking or noncompliant package acceptable.
It cancels all marking requirements.
It allows unknown chemicals to be combined.

questions.prompt: A tank has been drained. What remains to be checked?

options.label: Nothing; drained always means unrestricted.
Whether residue, vapor, pressure and empty-package requirements remain.
Only the outside paint condition.

questions.prompt: What should happen before a driver moves during a connected bulk transfer?

options.label: The driver should move slowly.
The loader should hold the hose.
The transfer must be safely stopped and the authorized disconnection/release process completed.

questions.prompt: What determines whether two hazardous materials may be loaded together?

options.label: The approved compatibility and transport segregation requirements for the actual load.
Whether the packages are the same color.
Whether there is spare floor space.

questions.prompt: What is the correct action when transfer communication is lost?

options.label: Keep pumping until the estimated amount is reached.
Stop according to the transfer procedure and restore safe communication before restart.
Ask an unbriefed bystander to wave.

questions.prompt: Which item is sufficient to establish correct bulk receiving capacity?

options.label: The truck registration number alone.
The driver saying it usually fits.
The approved check of the actual receiving compartment and available capacity.

questions.prompt: Where should you obtain release information for responders?

options.label: From documents and observations available without entering danger.
By walking through vapor to read the package.
By opening an unknown drum.

questions.prompt: What should an awareness-trained worker do about an unknown leak?

options.label: Attempt a repair to show initiative.
Report and follow the emergency plan within assigned response limits.
Assume every small leak is incidental.

questions.prompt: An unexplained seal is broken. What is the appropriate response?

options.label: Ignore it if no product is visible.
Post the vehicle route publicly.
Use the employer’s security reporting and shipment-hold procedure.

questions.prompt: What training change requires review before independent work?

options.label: Moving from loading to shipping-paper preparation.
Changing the color of a lunch box.
Taking the same authorized route at the planned time.

questions.prompt: Does a three-year recurrent training cycle permit unfamiliar work now?

options.label: Yes, until the next renewal date.
No; changed functions and applicable requirements need timely employer review and training.
Yes, if the shipment is urgent.

questions.prompt: Who determines whether a supervised-training provision can be used?

options.label: The learner alone.
Any passenger in the vehicle.
The employer through an applicable, properly supervised training arrangement.

questions.prompt: What does a 100% remediated foundation score establish?

options.label: The learner resolved this course’s questions; separate task qualification remains necessary.
The learner may ship all dangerous goods in every mode.
Every practical evaluation can be waived.

questions.prompt: Which record description is truthful for this course?

options.label: Complete international dangerous-goods certification.
Hazardous-material transportation recognition and safe-handoff foundation, with the actual version and scores.
All-mode shipping authorization.

courses.title: G02 — Hazardous waste and spill response: role limits and safe handoffs
courses.purpose: Teach workers to recognize and escalate hazardous-waste/response training gaps without claiming specialist capability.
courses.practicalBoundary:
29 CFR 1910.134(e), (f), (k)(1) — Required respirator users; tight-fitting facepieces require the applicable fit test: Complete the required medical evaluation before fit testing or use, the applicable fit test, and training that enables demonstration of the listed knowledge and respirator-use skills. These duties apply to the actual respirator assignment, not everyone taking awareness training. Source: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.134
29 CFR 1910.120(e)(3), (e)(4), (q)(6) — Workers whose actual hazardous-waste or emergency-response duties fall within the cited provisions: Apply the training and supervised field-experience or response-role competence requirements specified for that actual assignment. Do not assign the hazardous-waste field-experience requirement to ordinary waste handling or awareness-only roles. Source: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.120

content.title: G02 — Hazardous waste and spill response: role limits and safe handoffs
content.description: Complete original foundation teaching on applicability, changed conditions, response roles, zones, decontamination interfaces, exposure reporting and cleanup handoff.

explanations.G02_check1: Answer: B. The physical conditions have changed the task. A routine pickup assignment does not authorize investigation or emergency control of an unknown release.
explanations.G02_check2: Answer: C. Release size and a nearby kit do not establish substance hazards, exposure conditions or worker capability. Use the established competent assessment and escalation process.
explanations.G02_check3: Answer: A. Customer urgency and a short task duration do not change response-level competence or authorize source-control entry.
explanations.G02_check4: Answer: B. Appearance does not establish that contamination is removed. Uncontrolled transfer into a clean vehicle can expose others, and improvised decontamination can create further hazards.
explanations.G02_check5: Answer: C. Unknown atmospheres and casualty rescue require suitable trained capability. Awareness knowledge and a personal detector do not authorize entry.
explanations.G02_check6: Answer: A. The cleanup phase and a new crew require their own applicable readiness and handoff. Stabilization is not unrestricted return-to-work authorization.
explanations.G02_final1: Answer: A. A catalog category is not the regulatory applicability determination, and other safety requirements can remain relevant.
explanations.G02_final2: Answer: B. The changed physical conditions invalidate assumptions underlying the routine pickup.
explanations.G02_final3: Answer: C. Hazards, exposure conditions and capable controls must be considered through the established process.
explanations.G02_final4: Answer: A. Response organization and competence must be established; urgency and first arrival do not confer authority.
explanations.G02_final5: Answer: B. The employee must stay within the assigned function and request the trained response.
explanations.G02_final6: Answer: C. Site familiarity and broad titles cannot replace role-specific competence and assignment.
explanations.G02_final7: Answer: A. Source control can create close approach and exposure; it requires the appropriate response capability.
explanations.G02_final8: Answer: B. Zones are operating controls, not visual suggestions or permission to investigate.
explanations.G02_final9: Answer: C. Unrecorded movement can produce missing-person risks and interfere with response decisions.
explanations.G02_final10: Answer: A. Improvised methods can spread contamination or cause reactions.
explanations.G02_final11: Answer: B. Contamination control protects people beyond the immediate work zone.
explanations.G02_final12: Answer: C. Accurate facts support competent care and response without pretending to make a clinical determination.
explanations.G02_final13: Answer: A. Unprotected entry can create additional casualties.
explanations.G02_final14: Answer: B. Instrument capability, sampling method and gas-testing authority must match the actual hazard.
explanations.G02_final15: Answer: C. An emergency plan must be applied to actual conditions; a route passing through danger is not made safe by being printed.
explanations.G02_final16: Answer: A. Containment, cleanup, re-entry and restart are different decisions.
explanations.G02_final17: Answer: B. A changed phase or crew requires an appropriate readiness assessment and handoff.
explanations.G02_final18: Answer: C. It does not provide the duration, practical experience or specialist endorsements of other training programs.
explanations.G02_final19: Answer: A. New hazard information can change the previous authorization and must be resolved.
explanations.G02_final20: Answer: B. Trustworthy records preserve what was actually taught, answered and assessed.

lessons.title: Start here: this course and your response limits
lessons.body:
This original VNDRLY foundation teaches how to recognize an unresolved hazardous-waste or spill-response assignment, communicate changed conditions, respect response roles and handle the transition to cleanup. It is for affected workers, waste-service personnel, supervisors and program owners. The examples are fictional and do not authorize entry, cleanup, leak control or rescue.

Read six lessons and complete six checks. Study the two worked scenarios, then answer twenty final questions. Completion requires all twenty-six questions resolved correctly, including explicit acknowledgment of corrections where needed. The first-answer score remains separate from the remediated score. Passing this course does not represent a time-based HAZWOPER program, supervised field experience, a specialist response qualification or an employer’s site-specific authorization. Those remain separate evidence requirements.

lessons.title: Separate a waste-service label from a response assignment
lessons.body:
A service catalog tells you what a company offers. It does not establish what every worker may do at an incident. “Waste disposal,” “environmental cleanup” and “spill response” can describe very different work. A driver collecting a properly characterized load, a worker investigating an uncontrolled waste site and a technician approaching an active chemical leak do not have interchangeable duties. Before starting, identify the operation, the hazards and your assigned function. Ask who has assessed the task and which training and authorization cover it.

HAZWOPER is not a universal certificate for anything involving waste. Its U.S. scope includes specified hazardous-waste operations and hazardous-substance emergency response. The responsible employer must determine which provisions apply. Other rules can still apply when HAZWOPER does not. A worker should not decide coverage from a waste code, a cleanup invoice or a familiar product name alone. Likewise, an employer cannot avoid needed response competence by renaming an emergency “housekeeping.”

Compare the written work request with the physical conditions before committing to the task. If the request describes collecting sealed containers but you find leaking drums, vapor and people moving away, the conditions no longer match the assumed pickup. Stop the dependent work from a safe place. Tell the designated contact what you observed and what changed. Do not start opening containers or taking samples to make the job fit the original order.

Your course completion is a knowledge foundation for recognizing these boundaries. It does not represent a 24-hour, 40-hour, responder-level or refresher qualification. Those programs have their own content, duration, experience, exercise and employer-verification requirements. A company must retain the actual qualification evidence needed for the work. The useful question before a task is not whether a person has “some HAZWOPER,” but whether the person is trained, assessed and assigned for this operation and this role under current conditions.

lessons.title: Recognize the difference between incidental cleanup and an emergency
lessons.body:
A small release can be dangerous, and a visible volume is not enough to decide the response. Consider the substance, its concentration and behavior, where it has gone, the people exposed, the available controls and the capabilities of the people expected to act. An unfamiliar liquid in a poorly ventilated room can create a greater immediate threat than a larger known release in a controlled setting. You must use the employer’s established decision and escalation process rather than making an unsupported downgrade.

Incidental releases can be controlled by appropriately trained people under suitable conditions and procedures. That statement is not permission for every worker to absorb an unknown chemical. If the substance is uncertain, a person feels unwell, conditions are escalating, the release is uncontrolled or the required response exceeds local capability, stop and initiate the designated emergency process. Do not wait for an injury to establish that the conditions are serious.

At a safe distance, describe facts: the location, visible leak or cloud, apparent affected area, injured people, container or equipment identification already known, and any changes you observed. Clearly distinguish a confirmed material identity from a guess. Do not enter the affected area to collect better details. Information from a work order or inventory can help responders, but it must not be presented as proof that the released substance matches the record.

The site’s response leaders determine protective zones and response actions using competent assessment and monitoring. Do not choose a universal “safe distance” or decide that a wind direction alone guarantees protection. Terrain, enclosure, release behavior and changing weather can alter exposure. Keep to the route and assembly instructions that are safe for the actual situation. If the normal route is affected, use the emergency plan’s alternative and tell the designated contact.

lessons.title: Stay within the response level you actually hold
lessons.body:
An emergency organization assigns different functions because the tasks create different exposures. Someone who recognizes a hazardous-substance emergency and notifies the designated authority has a different role from a responder who takes defensive action, a technician who approaches to stop a leak, a specialist providing substance expertise or the incident commander directing the response.
