A safe foundation exercise can use a fictional support request, a simulated uncertain indication and a handover record. The learner identifies the responsible roles, protects access information, reports facts and explains the hold. Do not use a live production system, real malicious device or uncontrolled change to make the exercise realistic.

Keep learning, technical performance and authorization as separate records. A corrected quiz answer shows remediated understanding. A safe practical observation addresses specific actions under recorded conditions. An employer’s authorization assigns a bounded duty. None automatically creates the others, and a general IT credential does not establish process-operation or functional-safety engineering competence.

Review repeated workarounds and weak signals with the affected workers and technical owners. If remote support repeatedly bypasses the approved route, investigate access availability and work organization as well as behavior. Assign a correction with a real verification outcome. Counting closed tickets or reporting no recent incidents does not establish that the original control weakness is resolved.

Preserve the original event, decision and verification history. If an action fails, reopen it and communicate the current restriction. The company can improve its knowledge foundation while technical qualification and site readiness remain visibly outstanding. No universal renewal interval or automatic approval is created by this course.

lessons.title: Two applied cases with worked solutions
lessons.body:
## Case 1 — the urgent remote-support shortcut

A fictional terminal has a loading-automation fault. The local display intermittently stops updating, while the physical process is still under the operating team’s control. An outside support technician says their approved account is unavailable. They send a link to a different remote-support tool and ask the local service worker to install it on a connected workstation. The caller says a reboot will probably clear the fault and asks the worker to approve any authentication prompts. A delivery queue is building and a supervisor wants the ticket closed before shift change.

The local worker has completed ordinary IT support training. Their assignment permits reporting faults and coordinating approved support, not modifying the loading control system. They do not know whether the proposed workstation is only a reporting display or provides control functions.

### Work through the decision

Identify what the worker can do immediately, what information is needed, and who must authorize further action. Decide whether queue pressure, a known caller or a working alternative connection changes the boundary.

### Worked solution

The worker holds the proposed installation, authentication approval and reboot. They report the unreliable display and current loading state through the operations route and follow the assigned instruction for loss of trustworthy indication. They do not declare the operation safe or unsafe from the computer symptom alone; the qualified operating role makes the necessary physical-operation decision.

They verify the support request through the established contact and involve the designated technical and security owners. The team identifies the actual workstation, its control and reporting functions, dependencies, approved access route, proposed actions and responsible local contact. The alternative tool is a new connection requiring review, not a harmless substitute because the caller is familiar.

The worker records the observed fault, times, requested actions and what was held. They do not run an unapproved diagnostic, remove logs or disconnect devices to collect more evidence. If operations requires a restriction while indication is uncertain, that restriction remains clear to the gate and receiving teams so the queue is managed safely.

Any authorized technical repair follows the applicable change and verification process. Recovery includes the necessary operating and protective functions, not only a responsive screen. The receiving shift is told what was changed, which checks were performed and what remains restricted. The ticket accurately distinguishes a reported issue, completed technical activity and authorized return to service. Urgency is communicated, but it does not create a new access or operating permission.

## Case 2 — the restored screen and incomplete handback

At a fictional service facility, a contractor replaces a component supporting a tank-farm display. A configuration file on a personal drive is labeled “last good.” The contractor proposes restoring it because it worked during a previous visit. The new display uses a different presentation from the one the night operators practiced. The contractor can log in and see changing values, but no record is available showing whether the required alarm and protective interfaces were verified. The day supervisor says production was stable before the work and wants the night team to learn the display during operation.

The night operator notices the gap during handover. They are authorized for the normal operating procedure, but have not been assessed on the changed interface. The operator is not an OT recovery engineer.

### Work through the decision

Explain which facts are insufficient for release, how the recovery source and operational state should be resolved, and what the receiving operator needs before reliance. Do not design a live test or choose technical settings.

### Worked solution

The operator reports the incomplete handback and maintains the applicable safe restriction through the designated operating authority. A successful login and changing values establish limited observations. They do not prove that the configuration is the approved one, the data is trustworthy or the required protective functions are available.

The responsible technical team establishes the recovery source’s identity, provenance, version and relationship to the current approved configuration. A personal file name and a previous successful visit are not enough. The operations and technical authorities determine the suitable recovery and verification method. The operator supplies observations and follows the assigned process; they do not select or restore the file.

The team reviews the component and display changes through the applicable change process. Required functions and dependencies are checked using the authorized safe method. This exercise does not instruct anyone to defeat an interlock, generate a hazardous condition or test a live defense. If a required check cannot be completed, the uncertainty and operating limit remain visible.

A sign-off that only acknowledges receipt of release notes cannot establish that capability. The handover identifies actual configuration, completed checks, remaining issues and the people who accept return to service.

After the immediate work, management reviews why an uncontrolled recovery file and production-based learning were proposed. The corrective action addresses usable backup/change arrangements, contractor boundaries and operator readiness. Closing the repair ticket is separate from proving that those improvements work. First and remediated online scores remain learning evidence; they do not turn the operator into a recovery or functional-safety specialist.

lessons.title: Final assessment — twenty operational decisions
lessons.body: Answer each question individually using the work boundary, role, physical state and evidence supplied. Retain every first answer. An incorrect answer requires reading and explicitly acknowledging its explanation and corrected response. Both the first and remediated results remain visible across all twenty-six course questions.

lessons.title: Finish — confirm the actual next duty
lessons.body:
## Knowledge completion

Complete every section, six lesson checks and twenty final questions correctly or through explicitly acknowledged remediation. Keep first-attempt and remediated results separate. A knowledge record can contribute to the applicable company training component; it is not the entire safety score or evidence that every company system is secure.

## Separate technical and practical requirements

The assessor records the actual actions, assistance, conditions and limits. Do not create a real cyber incident, hazardous state or unauthorized system connection for training. Technical operation and qualification need their own appropriate evaluation.

Before the next actual duty, confirm the assigned system and task, current instructions, permitted access, responsible contacts, operational coordination and failed-control response. If scope or readiness remains uncertain, use the established hold and escalation process. Changes to the task, system, access route or recovery method require the relevant review. This course establishes no universal renewal interval and no automatic restart permission.

questions.prompt: A worker is asked to move an unfamiliar connection supporting an operational display. What should they do first?

options.label: Identify the asset, physical function and authorized work boundary with the responsible roles.
Unplug it briefly to identify what stops.
Assume every workstation is ordinary office IT.

questions.prompt: A vendor’s approved remote account fails and they propose a different support tool. What is the appropriate response?

options.label: Install it if the caller knows the equipment name.
Hold the alternative connection for authorized access and change review.
Approve authentication prompts until one connection succeeds.

questions.prompt: A programmer calls an alarm-display edit “only visual” during loading. What is needed?

options.label: Make the edit during a quiet moment without review.
Let live loading demonstrate whether the new display is understandable.
Review the actual operating interface, change authority, verification and affected-person readiness.

questions.prompt: A display freezes while an unexpected remote-access message appears. What should the worker do?

options.label: Report observations through operations and security routes and follow the assigned safe procedure.
Click through the message to find the person responsible.
Reboot the controller immediately without coordinating operations.

questions.prompt: A restored screen responds and shows changing values. What does that establish?

options.label: Every protective function is now proven available.
Limited screen behavior; required system functions and return-to-service conditions still need verification.
The latest approved configuration must have been restored.

questions.prompt: The incoming operator has not been assessed on a changed interface. What should the handover do?

options.label: Treat release-note receipt as practical competence.
Let the operator learn unfamiliar controls during production.
Keep the readiness gap explicit and obtain the appropriate instruction, assessment and authorized decision.

questions.prompt: Which feature makes a digital support task potentially relevant to OT safety?

options.label: It can affect monitoring or control of a physical activity.
Its screen has an industrial-looking background.
It uses a laptop rather than a desktop.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes a helpdesk account?

options.label: It qualifies its user to alter any connected protective function.
It provides only the access authorized for its assigned purpose, not automatic operating authority.
It replaces the site’s technical change process.

questions.prompt: Which information belongs in the initial scope check?

options.label: Only the desired ticket completion time.
Only whether the contractor has worked for the company before.
Asset identity, physical function, operating state, responsible contacts and proposed actions.

questions.prompt: How should an unexpected caller requesting urgent remote access be handled?

options.label: Verify through the established channel and involve the responsible access and operating roles.
Share a colleague’s login to avoid delay.
Accept the request because the caller names the site correctly.

questions.prompt: A worker finds an unfamiliar USB device beside an operational workstation. What is the safe course decision?

options.label: Connect it to discover its owner.
Keep it unconnected and follow the approved reporting and media-handling process.
Try it on another operational device first.

questions.prompt: What should happen to temporary remote access after the approved task?

options.label: Leave it available indefinitely for convenience.
Assume the contractor will remove it without verification.
End or formally review it through the authorized process and record the actual remaining state.

questions.prompt: Why can an office-tested software package still require operational review?

options.label: The actual equipment, dependencies and safety conditions may differ from the office test.
An office test proves all industrial systems compatible.
Only the package’s release date matters.

questions.prompt: Which activity is outside this foundation’s authorization?

options.label: Reporting an observed message through the approved route.
Intrusive scanning or exploratory changes on live production equipment.
Identifying the responsible operating contact.

questions.prompt: A temporary configuration measure reaches its review limit. What is required?

options.label: Keep it because production has appeared stable.
Extend its date without review.
Use the applicable safe restriction and obtain the responsible reviewed decision before further reliance.

questions.prompt: What is the correct way to describe an unexplained indication during an incident report?

options.label: State the observed behavior, time and context, distinguishing assumptions from facts.
Declare a confirmed attack without evidence.
Omit uncertainty so the report sounds decisive.

questions.prompt: Why should a general worker avoid automatically unplugging every connected system after a cyber concern?

options.label: Every connection must remain active regardless of danger.
Abrupt loss of communications or power can itself affect the physical operation.
A cyber concern is never relevant to operations.

questions.prompt: An operational indication may be unreliable. Who determines the appropriate physical operating response?

options.label: Any person who can restart the display.
The person who submitted the support ticket first.
The qualified assigned operating role using the actual procedures and information.

questions.prompt: Which backup description most directly supports a recovery decision?

options.label: Identified provenance, configuration/version, relevant date and tested recovery arrangements.
A personal file called “latest.”
A file that was once used successfully on another visit.

questions.prompt: Why might restoring one server be insufficient?

options.label: A server can never be used in an operational system.
Required communications, data, access and protective dependencies may still be unavailable or unverified.
A successful login proves every field function.

questions.prompt: Who controls return to service after technical recovery?

options.label: The contractor solely because their repair activity is complete.
Any user who sees a green indicator.
The designated responsible authority after required technical and operating prerequisites are verified.

questions.prompt: What must a shift handover preserve?

options.label: Current configuration, completed checks, restrictions, pending work and accountable contacts.
Only that the ticket is closed.
Only a statement that the previous shift saw no incident.

questions.prompt: What does the CSB Bayer example contribute to this course?

options.label: Proof that every control-system accident is a cyberattack.
A documented lesson about control-system change, operator readiness and safeguards.
A technical recipe for bypassing interlocks.

questions.prompt: Which exercise stays within this foundation’s scope?

options.label: A deliberately unauthorized connection to a live controller.
A real protective-function defeat to see whether the learner notices.
A fictional support request and simulated indication used to practice reporting, holds and handover.

questions.prompt: In Case 1, why does the familiar vendor’s alternative remote tool remain held?

options.label: The new route and proposed actions still require verified authorization and operational coordination.
A familiar vendor can never provide legitimate support.
The queue automatically authorizes any available workaround.

questions.prompt: In Case 2, what must be resolved before relying on the recovered system?

options.label: Only the ability to see changing values.
Recovery provenance, required-function verification, operator readiness and authorized handback.
Only the contractor’s promise that the file is “last good.”

lessons.title: Start here: task, records and passing standard
lessons.body:
Shipment discrepancy review: build a defensible hazardous-material handoff

This course teaches a bounded task: reconcile a shipment work packet, identify contradictions and issue an accurate hold or handoff without inventing classifications Work only with the fictional records supplied in the lessons and cases. No learner needs to enter a hazardous area, connect equipment, handle material or perform a live test. Read each of the six lessons, answer its check, then work both cases before completing the twenty final questions.

All twenty-six decisions require a response. The passing standard is 100 percent after explicit remediation. Preserve every original response, first-attempt correct count and original percentage. When an answer is incorrect, study its explanation and acknowledge the specific correction; retain the corrected response, remediation time and remediated score separately. A corrected score does not replace the original evidence.

The course uses primary sources as bounded authority for the concepts stated, and original fictional exercises to teach review and communication. A document that is acceptable in a classroom is not approval of a real job. Actual applicability, equipment, materials, procedures and responsibilities must be confirmed by the employer. No model example establishes a universal legal requirement.

Primary-source reading: [PHMSA hazardous-material training requirements](https://www.phmsa.dot.gov/about-phmsa/hazardous-materials-training-requirements); [FMCSA — How to comply with federal hazardous materials regulations](https://www.fmcsa.dot.gov/regulations/hazardous-materials/how-comply-federal-hazardous-materials-regulations). Read the scope and task guidance together with the actual employer procedure. These references do not issue this course's learner any license or work authorization.

lessons.title: 1. Establish the shipment identity before comparing documents
lessons.body:
A shipment review begins with a stable identity. Collect the order reference, consignor, receiving destination, material or product reference, batch or source when relevant, package or tank identity, quantity basis and planned transport mode. Those fields describe what is actually being offered. A purchase-order line saying “fluid service” is a commercial description; it does not establish what a particular tank contains. The reviewer connects the transaction to the actual material using the employer's accepted source records.

Use an identity crosswalk on paper: order 417, product reference M-8, source batch B-16, container T-62 and shipment packet revision C. Each connection should have a source, not just a repeated claim. If a dispatch email uses T-26 while the release record uses T-62, record the mismatch exactly. Do not silently transpose the digits because one arrangement seems more plausible. A corrected document must come from the person authorized to correct the underlying record.

Distinguish identity from classification. The material name and safety data sheet help locate the correct information, but the reviewer must not derive a transport classification by matching a familiar word. Composition, concentration, form, transport mode and applicable rules may matter. Refer a missing or inconsistent classification to the designated qualified shipping function. An old packet for a similar product is a lead for investigation, not authority for this load.

Define your own role before approving anything. A dispatcher may check completeness, a trained preparer may create regulated documents, and an authorized loading person may verify the physical package. One signature must not imply that all three duties were demonstrated. On the review sheet, state exactly what you checked and what remains with another role. This makes a handoff useful rather than merely reassuring.

The immediate task product is a review header with a single shipment reference, a list of source revisions and any identity contradictions. If identity cannot be established, stop the affected preparation or handoff through the employer's procedure. Do not ask a loader to inspect an unidentified substance by smell, opening or sampling to resolve a desk discrepancy.

lessons.title: 2. Reconcile fields without manufacturing a shipping description
lessons.body:
Compare corresponding fields across the authorized packet, the release record and the information the assigned worker is expected to use. Read full identifiers rather than recognizing a few words. Distinguish a product's commercial name from the regulated shipping description. Where the actual shipment requires specific shipping-description elements, verify them against the approved classification record and applicable employer procedure; do not supply missing wording from memory.

Mark each comparison as consistent, inconsistent, absent or outside the reviewer's scope. These four outcomes prevent an empty field from being treated as agreement. A document can be internally neat yet describe the wrong load. Conversely, a changed trade name does not by itself prove that the underlying classification changed. Send the specific discrepancy to the owner of that decision and preserve the original source.

Quantity review requires a stated unit and basis. If a fictional order requests 12 drums and a loading list records 10 drums, the shortage is two drums relative to that order. This arithmetic says nothing about an acceptable package, legal quantity limit, fill level or safe load. If one record states kilograms and another liters, no direct numerical comparison is valid without an authorized material-specific conversion basis. Do not assume a liquid has the density of water.

Review the destination as carefully as the product. A receiving company can have several facilities with different capabilities and approved materials. An address correction can therefore alter the practical acceptance question. Resolve a changed destination through dispatch and the responsible receiving contact, then ensure the final documents agree. A driver should not have to infer which destination or contact is current while traveling.

Use discrepancy language that supports action: “Loading list revision B names 12 drums; order release revision D names 10 drums; preparer to reconcile the quantity before handoff.” Avoid “paperwork wrong” or “probably fine.” Record who owns the correction and which downstream documents must be regenerated. The review is complete only when the corrected authoritative record and the associated copies are consistent, or an explicit hold preserves the unresolved issue.

lessons.title: 3. Review packaging evidence and its limits
lessons.body:
A package is a physical containment system, not just a description on a spreadsheet. The packet may include its identity, specification information, inspection status, permitted service, closure instruction and relevant maintenance or test records. The exact evidence depends on the package and task. A reviewer checks that the evidence refers to the actual package and current intended use; this course does not select a package or teach a closure method.

Compare serial or container identifiers character by character. A valid inspection report for T-62 cannot establish T-26's condition. Compare dates and scope as well. A report may cover an external inspection while the actual task requires other evidence under the employer's approved process. A photograph can help document a visible condition but cannot prove an unobserved internal condition, material compatibility or correct closure.

When reviewing a closure record, identify the instruction revision and the person authorized to perform and verify the operation. Do not substitute a verbal “we always tighten it that way” for the applicable instructions. The classroom reviewer can find a missing record but cannot certify an unobserved closure by checking a box.

Visible damage or suspected leakage is not a request for the desk reviewer to approach, touch or repair the package. The worker follows the site's safe reporting and isolation arrangements within their assigned role. Record what was reported, where it was observed from and what is unknown. A phone report saying “wet around base” should remain that observation until an authorized person determines its significance.

Create a package-evidence line for each relevant unit or traceable group, as allowed by the employer's process. Record matched identity, source document, status and unresolved limitation. If one unit is held, do not label the entire shipment released unless the authorized process has separated the held unit and corrected the remaining shipment information. Evidence must follow what actually moves, not the original commercial plan.

lessons.title: 4. Plan the loading interface as a responsibility handoff
lessons.body:
Loading is an interface between the shipping information, physical cargo, vehicle or container and receiving operation. A desk review prepares that interface by identifying the responsible people, approved method, communication route and the conditions that would invalidate the plan. It does not prescribe positioning, connections, transfer rates, valve sequences, pressure settings or emergency intervention.

Read the proposed sequence as responsibilities: who confirms the shipment identity, who checks the assigned equipment, who controls access, who performs the loading, who receives the completed records and who releases movement. These may be different people. If every line says “driver,” ask whether the employer has actually assigned and verified those duties. A driving credential alone is not proof of package preparation or transfer competence.

Look for simultaneous work that changes the interface. A maintenance job near the loading position, a blocked exit, another cargo, an unexpected receiver or a changed vehicle can invalidate assumptions. The responsible site roles decide the specific controls. The reviewer records the conflict and holds the affected handoff until the responsible authority confirms the revised arrangement. A schedule entry is not a risk-control decision.

Use read-back for critical identity information: the sender states the shipment and package references, the receiver repeats them, and discrepancies are resolved before the next authorized step. Read-back is useful because it exposes transposed numbers and stale documents. It does not replace visual checks or the worker's practical duties. Record only the checks actually completed, not a broad “all safe” statement.

The handoff packet should identify its final revision and withdraw or clearly supersede conflicting working copies through the employer's process. If a last-minute correction changes the load, verify which documents, labels, instructions or receiving arrangements are affected with the qualified shipping function. Do not assume an email attachment automatically replaces the driver's printed information. Confirm receipt and understanding through the designated channel before declaring the information handoff complete.

lessons.title: 5. Turn observations into useful emergency information
lessons.body:
A discrepancy review should prepare the worker to report a problem accurately without turning an untrained person into a responder. Distinguish a document inconsistency from an actual or suspected loss of containment. Both may justify holding a handoff, but a suspected release also requires the site's emergency reporting and protective actions. Follow the approved plan and your actual role rather than trying to determine severity by approaching the material.

A useful initial report contains the location, shipment and package identity if already known, what was observed, when it was observed, people possibly affected, immediate protective actions already taken and the safe callback route. Separate facts from interpretations. “A worker reports liquid beneath T-62 at bay 3” is different from “the tank has ruptured.” Include uncertainty so the designated responders can choose an appropriate assessment.

Keep required emergency information accessible through the actual transport process. A record stored in an inaccessible office system may not help a driver or receiving worker at the point of need. Verify the employer's approved availability arrangements and contact route; do not publish sensitive security details into an unrestricted chat or invent a replacement emergency number.

Do not transfer or open an unknown package to identify it. Do not neutralize, plug, reconnect, sample or move a suspect load unless those actions are part of your specific authorized role and training. The desk exercise is to prepare the information and hold the affected handoff, not to practice intervention. Evacuation, notification and accountability remain governed by the actual plan.

After an event, distinguish immediate emergency control from disposition of the shipment. A report that responders have left does not itself release the cargo for transport. The responsible shipping and site authorities must establish package condition, information accuracy, any required follow-up and the next authorized action. Keep the original observation, corrected records and release decision connected. This avoids a later shift treating an old dispatch instruction as current authority.

lessons.title: 6. Close discrepancies with traceable, bounded decisions
lessons.body:
A discrepancy log becomes a release tool only when each item has a resolution that can be checked. Use one row per issue: source observation, affected shipment element, responsible owner, required evidence, current state and disposition. Separate “owner contacted,” “response received” and “verified against final packet.” A message saying “fixed” is not the same as seeing the corrected authoritative record.

Resolve in dependency order. Identity and classification questions influence package, information and mode requirements. Quantity and destination corrections may affect dispatch and receiving acceptance. A package defect can change which units are included. If the underlying material is still unresolved, polishing the loading list does not make the shipment ready. Keep preparatory administrative work separate from release.

Record the exact scope of an approval. “Document packet revision E reconciled to order 417 for ten listed units” is more defensible than “hazmat approved.” The first statement tells a downstream person what evidence was reviewed and which load it covers. It also makes a later change visible: adding an eleventh unit is outside that statement and needs the actual process's review.

A job change can require different competence even when the shipment looks familiar. Moving from highway dispatch to air shipment preparation, changing material, changing package type or assigning unloading duties changes the function. PHMSA distinguishes general and function/mode-related training elements; the employer must determine and document the actual applicable program. This course does not claim to satisfy every required component or certify the employee.

Finish with an explicit handoff: identify the final packet, remaining hold if any, owner of the next action and the work the receiver may perform under their existing authorization. Preserve original and corrected versions according to the employer's record controls. A reviewer who finds and maintains an honest hold has produced a useful result. A completed screen should represent the actual disposition, never pressure the reviewer to erase a material uncertainty.

lessons.title: Two fictional worked desk cases
lessons.body:
Case A: a quantity and identity conflict

Fictional order 417 requests twelve drums of product M-8 for receiving facility North. The shipping preparer's release revision D authorizes ten drums from batch B-16. The loading list revision B still lists twelve drums and names South receiving. Container references on the physical-check report cover drums 01 through 10 only. A dispatcher asks the reviewer to change the total to twelve because “the order proves what the customer wanted.” No actual chemicals or packages are used in this exercise.

First establish the facts. The commercial order and the authorized release disagree by two drums. That subtraction measures a documentary difference, not permission to create additional cargo. The receiving destination also disagrees, and the available physical-check evidence identifies ten units. These are three related discrepancies with different consequences: commercial quantity, shipping release and receiving acceptance.

The correct desk response is to hold the affected handoff, reference the exact revisions and route the quantity and destination questions to the authorized shipping and dispatch roles. Do not copy the commercial request over the release record. The employer may ultimately approve ten or twelve units, but either decision needs a reconciled packet and evidence for the units actually offered. A packet for ten inspected units cannot prove two additional units suitable.

Suppose the responsible preparer confirms ten units to North and issues revision E. The reviewer checks the release, loading list and receiving information against that decision, confirms the physical-check report identifies the same ten units, and verifies the old destination copy has been superseded in the actual handoff. The review statement names ten units and revision E. The original twelve-unit order remains part of the commercial history; it is not silently rewritten as though no discrepancy existed.

Case B: a valid record for the wrong container

A fictional bulk shipment packet names tank T-62. Its attached inspection report identifies T-26. A yard worker calls from a safe location and reports wetness below the tank at bay 3. The driver has a previously printed packet and a new email that says “same as last week.” The reviewer's job is to prepare the discrepancy and emergency-information handoff, not inspect or repair the tank.

There are two independent issues. The inspection evidence does not match the package identity, and the reported wetness may indicate a release or another condition that requires assessment. Do not treat a valid-looking inspection date as proof for a different tank. Do not dismiss the observation because the document mismatch appears clerical. The affected handoff is held, and the site's reporting and protective process is used for the reported condition.

A useful report says: “Shipment packet names T-62; attached inspection identifies T-26; worker reports wetness below the bay-3 tank; cause and material are unconfirmed; handoff held; safe callback through dispatch.” It avoids declaring a rupture and avoids sending someone closer to obtain a photograph. The designated roles arrange assessment and determine the actual package condition.

If the authorized reviewer later establishes the correct tank identity and supplies matching acceptable evidence, that resolves only the record issue. The suspected-release disposition still needs the responsible site's decision. Before any movement release, the final package, condition, packet and receiving information must refer to the actual shipment and all affected holds must be resolved by the responsible authority. The driver's stale packet must be superseded through the approved communication process. Neither a successful document correction nor emergency attendance alone proves the shipment ready.

lessons.title: Final assessment: twenty task decisions
lessons.body: Answer all twenty questions using the taught review methods. Identify the record, discrepancy, responsible decision and unresolved prerequisite rather than guessing operating values. Review the explanation for each incorrect response and record remediation while preserving the original score.

lessons.title: Finish: evidence and practical assessment remain distinct
lessons.body:
Knowledge completion and actual work release

You have practiced reconcile a shipment work packet, identify contradictions and issue an accurate hold or handoff without inventing classifications Preserve the actual exercise result and the mistakes corrected. Use those mistakes to identify what the supervisor must verify in the real work packet. Do not substitute an online score for a demonstration, a current product document, an assigned responsibility or an approval by the person who holds it.

Before the actual assignment, obtain the specific evidence listed with this course. The assessor records conditions, limitations and any required reassessment. No worker should manufacture an unsafe situation to demonstrate readiness. Unresolved items stay open against their named owner; an administrative completion label cannot authorize hazardous execution.

## Legal requirements for the named work role
These apply only when you perform the work described below. They are not additional steps for completing this online course.

49 CFR 172.702(d), 172.704(a), (d) — Hazmat employees performing functions covered by the Hazardous Materials Regulations: Provide the applicable function-specific training and testing and retain the employer training record specified in (d). No universal separate practical examination or VNDRLY evidence upload is prescribed by these provisions. Source: https://www.phmsa.dot.gov/training/hazmat/training-requirements-industry

questions.prompt: Order says fluid service; tank contents are unverified. What comes first?

options.label: Establish actual material and container identity from accepted source records.
Infer identity from the customer name.
Use last week's classification.
Accept the order description as the final package inspection.

questions.prompt: A record states 800 kg and another 800 L. What is defensible?

options.label: Declare them equal.
Flag different quantity bases; obtain an authorized conversion basis if comparison is needed.
Assume water density.
Convert liters to kilograms using a universal cargo factor.

questions.prompt: Inspection identifies T-26 while packet names T-62. What does the report establish?

options.label: Both tanks are inspected.
The tank digits are interchangeable.
Evidence for its stated tank only; the actual package remains unresolved.
Use the report because its date is recent regardless of identity.

questions.prompt: The loading vehicle changes after review. What should the coordinator do?

options.label: Keep the old approval automatically.
Let the driver decide every loading role.
Let a revised vehicle identifier silently replace every instruction.
Refer the changed interface for the actual required review before handoff.

questions.prompt: A worker reports wetness under a tank. Which initial message is best?

lessons.title: Start here: task, records and passing standard
lessons.body:
Waste and release work packets: determine response scope before assigning people

This course teaches a bounded task: prepare a waste-task or release-response scope record, distinguish facts from unresolved hazards and route work to the correct program Work only with the fictional records supplied in the lessons and cases. No learner needs to enter a hazardous area, connect equipment, handle material or perform a live test. Read each of the six lessons, answer its check, then work both cases before completing the twenty final questions.

All twenty-six decisions require a response. The passing standard is 100 percent after explicit remediation. Preserve every original response, first-attempt correct count and original percentage. When an answer is incorrect, study its explanation and acknowledge the specific correction; retain the corrected response, remediation time and remediated score separately. A corrected score does not replace the original evidence.

The course uses primary sources as bounded authority for the concepts stated, and original fictional exercises to teach review and communication. A document that is acceptable in a classroom is not approval of a real job. Actual applicability, equipment, materials, procedures and responsibilities must be confirmed by the employer. No model example establishes a universal legal requirement.

Primary-source reading: [OSHA hazardous waste operations and emergency response](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.120); [OSHA — Hazardous waste operations and emergency response overview](https://www.osha.gov/emergency-preparedness/hazardous-waste-operations). Read the scope and task guidance together with the actual employer procedure. These references do not issue this course's learner any license or work authorization.

lessons.title: 1. Separate the service contract from the covered operation
lessons.body:
A waste-service contract describes a purchase. A safe work assignment describes what people will actually encounter and do. Begin the work packet by identifying the location, material or waste stream, source of the information, planned activities, worker roles and expected condition of containment. “Dispose of waste” might mean transporting sealed containers, sampling unknown drums, maintaining a treatment process or responding to an unexpected release. Those activities cannot be assigned from the service label alone.

Build a scope statement with verbs. “Collect ten sealed identified containers from the designated storage area using the approved handling method” is different from “open and characterize unknown containers.” The first does not automatically authorize the second. List activities explicitly excluded from the assignment, especially opening, sampling, entering affected areas, controlling a release or handling contaminated rescue equipment. Exclusions prevent an ordinary service crew from inheriting emergency duties when conditions change.

The employer determines whether and which hazardous-waste or emergency-response provisions apply. The U.S. OSHA standard distinguishes categories of covered operations, and its different sections do not form one interchangeable course requirement. Record the employer's applicability decision, its basis and the person responsible. An online course title, a customer demand for a certificate or a vendor's broad marketing claim is not that determination.

Review the information that supports the planned condition. Ask whether waste identity, containment, exposure pathways and receiving arrangements are known. “Nonhazardous” on an invoice does not explain how the conclusion was reached or whether the current load matches it. Record uncertainty precisely rather than changing the material description to fit the crew available. The purpose of a scope review is to expose missing information before people are assigned.

The first useful deliverable is therefore an activity-and-boundary record. It states what the crew may do under the approved method, the information relied on, the conditions requiring a hold and the person who will decide a change. This record is preparatory.

lessons.title: 2. Build a defensible incident description without entering to investigate
lessons.body:
When a release is reported, begin with the information available from a safe position or existing records. Record time, location, material identity if already known, what was observed, affected people, changing conditions and protective actions already taken. Distinguish direct observation from a second-hand report. “Caller reports a sharp odor near the south door” is useful; converting it to a named chemical and a safe concentration without evidence is not.

The initial decision must respect uncertainty. The size of a visible puddle alone cannot establish whether an event is an incidental cleanup or an emergency. Material properties, amount and potential release, exposure, circumstances, available controls and the capabilities assigned under the actual program matter. A small release of an unknown substance or a changing atmosphere can create a problem beyond a routine service role. Do not ask the crew to approach to settle the classification.

Create two columns in the incident note: established facts and unresolved questions. A fictional note might state that container D-8 is reported leaking, two workers have moved to the assembly location and the gate is held. Unresolved questions might include actual contents, ongoing release, exposure significance and whether other containers are affected. This format keeps a responder's next assessment from being confused with a conclusion already reached.

Use the employer's reporting and protective process. A coordinator can notify, maintain accountability and communicate a hold within their assignment. They must not give improvised instructions to neutralize a substance, enter a cloud, plug a leak or retrieve an unconscious person. Those are different tasks requiring specific capabilities. A desire for more information is not authority to create an exposure.

Update the record with timestamps as information changes. If an earlier report is corrected, retain the sequence and identify the source of the correction. A new fact may change the response scope and invalidate an old plan. Clear uncertainty is more helpful than premature certainty: it tells the designated decision maker what still needs competent assessment and prevents the incoming shift from treating a guess as a verified condition.

lessons.title: 3. Match assigned duties to a real response role
lessons.body:
A person's previous course or job title does not automatically match the role now needed. Write the proposed duty first: recognize and report, assist defensive protection under an assigned plan, approach to stop a release, direct the response, or conduct cleanup after control. Then ask the responsible program authority which role and competence apply. This lesson teaches the review logic; it does not designate anyone a responder or teach intervention.

Check the evidence against the task, not simply its presence. A certificate may establish attendance in a named subject but not supervised experience, current employer designation, equipment familiarity or the worker's ability to perform the assigned skills. A general awareness result is especially limited: it may support recognizing a problem and reporting it while leaving all entry and intervention work outside scope.

Create an individual role matrix. Do not place private medical details in the matrix. Where medical or respiratory eligibility is relevant, the authorized occupational-health process provides the appropriate status through a confidential route. The coordinator needs a valid readiness determination, not a diagnosis or a copy of personal health history.

Evaluate support duties too. Traffic control, equipment staging, communications and receiving contaminated items can create exposure or critical dependencies. A worker who remains outside the immediate release area still needs instruction for their actual function and the site's boundaries. Avoid assigning someone to “help wherever needed.” That phrase hides the point at which an untrained helper may become an entrant or decontamination worker.

If evidence is missing, do not solve the staffing gap by relabeling a higher-risk duty as awareness. Keep the affected task unassigned or held and route the gap to the program authority. A useful conclusion names the missing item: “No observed proficiency record for the assigned protective equipment” or “Site-specific response duties not established.” Specific gaps can be resolved; “needs more training” gives neither the worker nor the supervisor an actionable next step.

lessons.title: 4. Review boundaries, accountability and decontamination as a system
lessons.body:
A response plan needs a controlled interface between affected areas and people outside them. At the desk-review stage, ask who establishes and changes boundaries, how workers are accounted for, how communication works and how contaminated people or equipment will be managed. Do not prescribe zone distances from this course. The actual material, site assessment and response leadership determine suitable arrangements.

Review the site drawing for clarity rather than pretending it is a live hazard map. It should identify the intended reporting and assembly arrangements, access-control responsibilities and relevant routes under the approved plan. A drawing created before an incident can be a planning aid, but wind, access, release conditions or other events may make a route unsuitable. The incident authority must communicate current boundaries; an old printed diagram cannot override them.

Accountability means knowing who has been assigned, where they are permitted to be, how their status is checked and what happens if contact is lost. A sign-in list alone does not prove someone left an affected area. Ask how the assigned supervisor reconciles people, how visitors and contractors are included and who communicates a missing-person report to the appropriate response leadership. Do not send an unqualified coworker to search.

Decontamination planning must be connected to the hazard and assigned role. The reviewer checks that a real procedure, suitable resources, trained personnel and a waste disposition are provided where needed. Do not invent a washing chemical or assume water is always appropriate. A contaminated glove, tool or vehicle can transfer exposure beyond the initial area if the exit interface is uncontrolled.

Review secondary interfaces: ambulance access, clean supplies, waste collection, food and drink areas and handover to receiving medical care. The point is to identify responsibility and prevent contamination from being carried into an area assumed clean. An apparently organized response can still fail if the plan ends at the scene boundary and no one owns what happens to used equipment or potentially exposed people.

lessons.title: 5. Prepare exposure and rescue information without creating another casualty
lessons.body:
An exposure report and a rescue request are urgent information tasks. Record the person's location if known, observed condition, material information already available, time and route of possible exposure, and actions already taken within the assigned role. Do not delay the established emergency contact while trying to complete every field. Information can follow as it becomes available from safe sources.

Keep the rescue boundary explicit. An unconscious person near a suspected hazardous atmosphere does not make entry safe for a coworker. The correct desk decision is to activate the approved response, maintain protective separation and provide location and hazard information to the designated rescuers. This course teaches no entry, retrieval or respiratory-protection method. A dramatic need does not supply missing equipment, training or backup.

The medical interface needs accurate information and privacy. Give authorized medical responders the relevant available substance and exposure information through the designated route. Keep diagnoses, treatment details and personal health history out of general work-order comments and group messages. A public task status can say that the authorized medical process was contacted and the work restriction remains open without disclosing confidential details.

Make time visible in the report. Distinguish when the event was observed, when it was reported, when contact was made and when a later correction arrived. A note entered at noon about a 10:15 observation should not imply the event began at noon. This matters to understanding exposure and coordinating follow-up. Record estimates as estimates rather than manufacturing exactness.

After the immediate response, the employer's applicable program governs exposure follow-up, incident review and any reassignment decision. A worker saying they feel well does not establish absence of exposure, and a coordinator must not give medical clearance. Preserve the relevant factual record, follow the confidential route and ensure the next shift knows the actual work restrictions. The goal is useful coordination while leaving clinical and specialist decisions with the roles qualified to make them.

lessons.title: 6. Distinguish emergency control from cleanup and return to service
lessons.body:
The end of an emergency action is a transition, not automatic permission for ordinary crews to begin cleanup. Residual material, contaminated equipment, damaged containment, waste handling and changed site conditions may remain. Ask the responsible authority what state has actually been achieved and which activities are now authorized. “No visible leak” is an observation; it does not characterize all remaining hazards.

Build a handover that names the scope of the next phase. It should identify the area or equipment, known and unresolved hazards, boundaries still in force, material characterization, cleanup method owner, worker requirements, waste disposition and the authority for further change. A response leader may transfer control to a cleanup organization, but the actual transfer must be communicated to the people expected to act. Do not assume the original service contract already covers the new conditions.

Check dependencies before scheduling the next crew. If characterization is incomplete, the cleanup method may remain unresolved. If contaminated tools are held, maintenance personnel need the correct information before handling them. If a receiving facility has not accepted the waste stream, moving it off site is not a completed disposition plan. Keep those individual prerequisites visible rather than replacing them with a single “incident closed” label.

The release decision must state who may do what, where and under which documents. “Routine container collection resumes in storage area B; damaged-container area remains held for the specialist contractor” is more useful than “all clear.” A partial release can be appropriate only when the responsible authority has established and communicated the actual separation. This course cannot make that technical determination.

Use the event review to improve the work packet without rewriting history. Ask which assumptions failed, whether people recognized the changed scope, how communication worked and which evidence was unavailable. Preserve the original response and corrected understanding in this course as well. A corrected answer demonstrates remediation; it does not prove that the learner has performed the site-specific response role or that every follow-up requirement has been completed.

lessons.title: Two fictional worked desk cases
lessons.body:
Case A: sealed-container pickup becomes an unknown-release problem

A fictional vendor is assigned to collect eight sealed, identified waste containers from a marked storage area. The approved work packet excludes opening, sampling and release control. The coordinator receives a call: one container has a damaged lid, there is staining below it and the material label is unreadable. The customer says the crew should simply tighten the lid and load it because the waste invoice says nonhazardous.

The first step is to compare the actual reported condition with the assigned scope. Collection of sealed identified containers was the task. A damaged lid, possible release and unreadable label remove important assumptions. The commercial invoice does not resolve the current material identity or safe handling question. The crew should not be directed to approach, tighten, sample or load the affected container as an improvised investigation.

The coordinator records the safe-source observations and holds the affected work under the site's reporting process. The note distinguishes the reported damaged lid and staining from the unconfirmed cause, contents and extent. It identifies the crew's existing assignment and exclusions so the site authority does not mistake them for a response team. The responsible program determines the appropriate assessment and response scope.

Suppose the customer later provides an old waste profile and a certificate showing that one crew member attended general awareness training. Neither item resolves the entire problem. The profile must be connected to the actual container and current contents; the certificate must be assessed against the actual proposed role. Awareness does not authorize the worker to control an unknown release.

The worked result is an honest hold with named missing evidence: actual container/material identification, competent condition assessment, applicable response/handling method and appropriately qualified assigned people. Other collection work can proceed only if the responsible site authority establishes and communicates its safe separation; the classroom reviewer cannot assume that separation.

Case B: an emergency closes, but the cleanup handover does not

At a fictional processing yard, designated responders have completed their immediate action. A supervisor receives the message “leak stopped.” A night-shift maintenance crew is scheduled to dismantle a nearby pump. The incident note still lists potentially contaminated tools, an unresolved waste stream and a restricted area. One employee is undergoing confidential exposure follow-up. The supervisor is asked to mark every task complete before shift end.

The correct review separates four decisions. Stopping the leak concerns the immediate release. The area restriction concerns current access. The tools and waste concern contamination and disposition. The employee's follow-up concerns the authorized medical route and work status. No single phrase establishes all four as resolved.

The supervisor requests a bounded handover from the responsible incident/site authority. The handover must say whether the pump area is released for the specific maintenance work, what hazards remain and which method and qualifications apply. The maintenance crew should not inherit cleanup duties without a real scope and capability review. Potentially contaminated tools must remain under the applicable controls until their disposition is established.

For the employee, the general work record should preserve only necessary status and the designated follow-up route, without publishing a diagnosis or personal health history. Feeling well and completing an online quiz are not medical clearance. The authorized occupational-health process makes the appropriate determination.

The worked final status is deliberately specific: immediate release control reported complete; pump maintenance authorization pending the actual area/task handover; tool and waste dispositions open with named owners; medical follow-up retained through the confidential route. The supervisor can close only the items supported by observed evidence. This creates an actionable next-shift record and prevents administrative pressure from converting unresolved hazards into a false all-clear.

lessons.title: Final assessment: twenty task decisions
lessons.body: Answer all twenty questions using the taught review methods. Identify the record, discrepancy, responsible decision and unresolved prerequisite rather than guessing operating values. Review the explanation for each incorrect response and record remediation while preserving the original score.

lessons.title: Finish: evidence and practical assessment remain distinct
lessons.body:
Knowledge completion and actual work release

You have practiced prepare a waste-task or release-response scope record, distinguish facts from unresolved hazards and route work to the correct program Preserve the actual exercise result and the mistakes corrected. Use those mistakes to identify what the supervisor must verify in the real work packet. Do not substitute an online score for a demonstration, a current product document, an assigned responsibility or an approval by the person who holds it.

Before the actual assignment, obtain the specific evidence listed with this course. The assessor records conditions, limitations and any required reassessment. No worker should manufacture an unsafe situation to demonstrate readiness. Unresolved items stay open against their named owner; an administrative completion label cannot authorize hazardous execution.

## Legal requirements for the named work role
These apply only when you perform the work described below. They are not additional steps for completing this online course.

29 CFR 1910.132(f)(2), (g) — Employees using the eye/face, head, foot, hand or personal fall protection covered by paragraph (g): Before that work, demonstrate understanding of the PPE training and ability to use the PPE properly. This is not a separate independent certification requirement. Respirators and electrical protective equipment follow their own standards rather than paragraph (f). Source: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.132

29 CFR 1910.134(e), (f), (k)(1) — Required respirator users; tight-fitting facepieces require the applicable fit test: Complete the required medical evaluation before fit testing or use, the applicable fit test, and training that enables demonstration of the listed knowledge and respirator-use skills. These duties apply to the actual respirator assignment, not everyone taking awareness training. Source: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.134

29 CFR 1910.120(e)(3), (e)(4), (q)(6) — Workers whose actual hazardous-waste or emergency-response duties fall within the cited provisions: Apply the training and supervised field-experience or response-role competence requirements specified for that actual assignment. Do not assign the hazardous-waste field-experience requirement to ordinary waste handling or awareness-only roles. Source: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.120

questions.prompt: A contract says waste disposal. What defines the assignment?

options.label: The actual activities, material conditions, location and assigned roles.
The invoice label alone.
Any activity the customer requests on arrival.
The available crew can define the hazard by what it knows how to handle.

questions.prompt: A caller reports odor near a door. Which record is appropriate?

options.label: Declare a safe concentration.
Record the caller's observation and unknown material/exposure significance.
Name a familiar chemical without evidence.
Record a guessed material as a confirmed laboratory finding.

questions.prompt: A worker holds an awareness attendance certificate. What should a reviewer conclude?

options.label: The worker can stop any leak.
The worker is medically cleared.
Check its actual scope; it does not by itself authorize intervention.
The worker is automatically the incident commander.

questions.prompt: A pre-incident map conflicts with current response boundaries. What controls access?

options.label: The oldest printed diagram.
The shortest route.
The shortest path proposed by a visiting driver.
The current boundaries communicated by the authorized incident/site role.

questions.prompt: A person is unconscious near a suspected hazardous atmosphere. What may an unqualified coworker do?

options.label: Activate the approved response and provide safe-source location/hazard information.
Enter immediately without appropriate capability.
Try an unfamiliar respirator.
Enter only long enough to determine whether breathing is possible.

questions.prompt: Leak stopped is the only handover message. What remains?

options.label: Release every cleanup and maintenance task.
Clarify residual hazards, boundaries and authorization for the specific next task.
Erase the incident note.
The response contract automatically covers every cleanup method.

questions.prompt: Which scope statement is more useful?

options.label: Help with everything.
Waste duties as needed.
Collect identified sealed containers; opening and sampling excluded.
Complete whatever nearby staff mention informally.

questions.prompt: Who determines applicable hazardous-waste program coverage?

options.label: A course title.
A customer's marketing description.
A certificate vendor decides all legal applicability.
The responsible employer/program authority using actual operation facts.

questions.prompt: Why distinguish observed facts from open questions?

options.label: To prevent uncertainty becoming an unsupported conclusion in the next handoff.
To postpone every notification.
To make guesses look official.
To avoid telling the response authority about unknown conditions.

questions.prompt: Is puddle size alone a sound incidental-versus-emergency test?

options.label: Yes, if the puddle looks small.
No; hazard, circumstances, controls and capability also matter.
Yes, if the invoice says nonhazardous.
Yes, the word small proves the worker is qualified.

questions.prompt: The material is unknown. How should the desk reviewer obtain more information?

options.label: Tell the collector to smell it closely.
Have an unassigned worker open the lid.
Use existing safe sources and route assessment to designated competent roles.
Ask a visitor to taste or touch the material.

questions.prompt: Which role-matrix entry is actionable?

options.label: Needs something.
Safe enough.
All duties approved because a name is on a roster.
Assigned communication duty; site-specific instruction evidence absent; supervisor owns resolution.

questions.prompt: What medical detail belongs in a general task matrix?

options.label: Only appropriate readiness status through the authorized confidential process.
Full diagnosis and treatment history.
A copied personal health file.
An unverified rumor about a colleague's diagnosis.

questions.prompt: A helper stages used tools outside the scene. What must be reviewed?

options.label: Nothing because the helper is outside.
The actual contamination interface and assigned instruction/control needs.
Only the helper's job title.
Only whether the helper has previously visited the yard.

questions.prompt: What should not be used to solve a response staffing gap?

options.label: Holding the unassigned task.
Seeking the qualified program authority.
Relabeling an intervention duty as awareness.
Obtaining a competent decision on the actual role scope.

questions.prompt: Does signing in establish that everyone left the affected area?

options.label: Yes, automatically.
Only if the list is typed.
Yes, a check-in time also proves a safe exit time.
No; the actual accountability process must reconcile people and status.

questions.prompt: What is the correct desk approach to decontamination?

options.label: Verify a hazard-appropriate procedure, resources, trained roles and waste disposition.
Invent a universal washing mixture.
Assume water always makes an item safe.
Use whichever cleaning chemical is nearest.
