content.title: G65 — Engineering requirements, design assumptions and technical review decisions
content.description: Six fully written engineering review lessons, two worked unit/interface cases and 26explained decisions. Actual design qualification remains separate.

explanations.G65_check1: A requirement needs a defined claim and evaluation basis; preference and assurance language do not establish them.
explanations.G65_check2: The arithmetic is valid after conversion, but the physical route, configuration and required allowances remain separate questions.
explanations.G65_check3: Identical labels do not establish a common reference or denominator.
explanations.G65_check4: Validation addresses intended use; bounded component evidence alone cannot answer that whole question.
explanations.G65_check5: Review dependencies to identify what changed and what remains applicable, rather than accepting or rejecting all evidence without analysis.
explanations.G65_check6: Knowledge completion and application permissions do not establish professional signing or technical approval authority.
explanations.G65_final1: Record the reason for a real constraint; labeling a preference does not create that basis.
explanations.G65_final2: An assumption can support provisional reasoning but must not silently become a verified installed condition.
explanations.G65_final3: Traceability links specific claims and evidence, rather than relying on resemblance.
explanations.G65_final4: Quantity identity and physical conditions are part of the calculation basis.
explanations.G65_final5: Software execution does not validate the engineering model or its use.
explanations.G65_final6: Read the declared subtraction order; the sign alone is not an approval decision.
explanations.G65_final7: Integration depends on agreed meaning and ownership across the connection.
explanations.G65_final8: A component claim has bounded scope and cannot establish all integrated behavior.
explanations.G65_final9: Representative use conditions matter to validation and human interfaces.
explanations.G65_final10: Configuration differences need technical assessment; evidence may be useful without being sufficient.
explanations.G65_final11: Those links establish what the evaluation actually covered.
explanations.G65_final12: The evidence should be used within its tested scope.
explanations.G65_final13: The administrative queue cannot establish continuing technical authorization.
explanations.G65_final14: Equivalence depends on properties and application, not the commercial label.
explanations.G65_final15: A design instruction and an observation of the installed arrangement are different evidence.
explanations.G65_final16: Jurisdiction-specific examples do not establish a universal licensing requirement.
explanations.G65_final17: A bounded assessment needs a defined task and credible evaluation evidence.
explanations.G65_final18: Follow dependencies to evaluate the effect of the actual resolution.
explanations.G65_final19: Coverage is a specific applicability question, not a conclusion from a catalog label.
explanations.G65_final20: Knowledge, qualified technical judgment, observed performance and operational authorization remain distinct.

lessons.title: Start here — engineering review knowledge and its limits
lessons.body:
This original course teaches assigned engineers, design coordinators and technical reviewers how to make requirements, assumptions and evidence usable. The examples are fictional paper exercises. There is no live system or equipment activity.

Complete six taught lessons, six checks, two worked cases and twenty final questions. Passing requires all 26 questions correct or explicitly acknowledged question-specific remediation. Original answers and first-attempt scores remain recorded alongside corrected results. A remediated knowledge result cannot establish unobserved technical performance.

lessons.title: Develop a bounded, evaluable requirement
lessons.body:
An engineering requirement connects an intended function to a condition that can be evaluated. A request to make a system reliable expresses a concern but leaves designers and reviewers guessing what result is acceptable. Begin with the intended user, operating context and consequence of failure. Identify what the system must do, the conditions in which it must do it and the evidence the owner expects before accepting it. Do not choose an arbitrary numerical target merely to make a sentence measurable. The responsible technical and operating authorities must establish a justified target.

Separate function, performance and constraint. Function describes the required activity. Performance describes how well that activity must be accomplished under stated conditions. A constraint limits the available solution, such as an established interface, site restriction or governing specification. A proposed product is a solution candidate, not automatically the requirement itself. “Use pump model Q” can hide the real need for a specified duty and compatible process interface. When an existing approved asset really is a constraint, record that reason rather than pretending the model name supplies every operating requirement.

Make the scope of each requirement identifiable. Assign a stable reference and link it to the source decision, relevant system or component, revision and intended verification. Use one independently evaluable obligation rather than bundling unrelated expectations into a single vague sentence. Record assumptions and open decisions separately. An assumption is information temporarily used for reasoning; it is not a confirmed property of the installed facility. If a design depends on an assumed ambient condition, the owner must know who will establish that condition and what happens if it is different.

In a fictional remote monitoring installation, “the display must be easy to use and always available” contains several unresolved needs. The reviewer separates readability for the intended users, availability under the approved operating conditions and behavior during loss of communication. They ask the operating owner to establish acceptance criteria and the technical team to identify feasible verification methods. They do not turn “always” into an unsupported guarantee or decide an alarm response time from memory.

A useful requirement review therefore produces specific questions: which user and activity does this serve; which condition bounds it; what evidence can show it was met; and who accepts the result? NASA's systems engineering guidance provides a requirements-development example, not a mandatory oilfield design code. Apply the actual project and jurisdiction requirements.

lessons.title: Check quantities, assumptions and calculation meaning
lessons.body:
A calculation can be arithmetically correct and still answer the wrong physical question. Before checking numbers, identify the quantity, units, reference conditions, sign convention, boundary and applicable range. A mass flow and a volume flow are different quantities; converting between them requires an appropriate density and its conditions. A dimension labeled overall length does not necessarily establish the available clearance for installation or maintenance. The reviewer must understand what the input represents before treating it as usable evidence.

Write a compact input ledger for the particular calculation. For each material input, record its value or range, unit, source and revision, operating condition and whether it is measured, specified or assumed. This ledger is not a substitute for a competent design calculation. It makes the technical basis visible so that a reviewer can identify a missing input or a mismatch. Retain uncertainty and variability where they matter. A single nominal value cannot represent an entire range merely because the spreadsheet accepts one number.

Use dimensional checks to expose simple errors. In a fictional planning exercise, an asset is 2.4 metres long and a sketch labels a clear opening as 2,500 millimetres. Converting 2.4 metres to 2,400 millimetres gives an apparent 100-millimetre difference. That arithmetic does not prove installation is possible: the drawing may omit handles, packaging, lifting orientation, movement path and required clearance. State the narrow conclusion: the two supplied nominal dimensions differ by 100 millimetres. Refer the actual installation geometry and required allowances to the responsible discipline.

Sign conventions matter in comparisons. If a review defines difference as proposed minus permitted, a positive result indicates that the proposed quantity is above the stated limit. Reversing the subtraction reverses the sign. State the convention next to the calculation rather than relying on what a positive number usually means in another team's spreadsheet. Keep the original figures and show conversions so another reviewer can reproduce the reasoning.

Check the applicability of the model itself. A relationship intended for one material state, geometry or operating regime may not apply after those conditions change. Software completion, a plausible answer and a polished chart cannot establish model validity. The qualified technical reviewer must assess the governing method and assumptions. This lesson teaches how to identify and communicate the basis of a calculation; it supplies no design formula or acceptance threshold for hazardous equipment.

lessons.title: Review interfaces and human use
lessons.body:
An interface is a place where one part of the design depends on another part or on a person, environment or external service. Mechanical connections, electrical supplies, signals, software data, access routes and operating responsibilities are all potential interfaces. A component that meets its own specification can fail as part of the system if the interface assumptions differ. The task of interface review is to make those shared assumptions explicit and resolve them with the people responsible for both sides.

Start with the intended connection and list what crosses it. For a monitoring signal, this may include the measured quantity, engineering units, range interpretation, data quality state, update behavior, loss-of-signal behavior and who responds to the indication. For a physical installation, consider the actual connection geometry, support and environmental assumptions, access and the boundaries of installation responsibility. This list identifies questions for the competent disciplines; it does not authorize a learner to design a circuit, support or protective function.

Distinguish a shared label from an agreed meaning. Two systems can both display “level” while one uses a percent of instrument span and the other uses a percent of usable capacity. The numbers can look reasonable and still describe different quantities. Reconcile definitions and reference conditions before accepting a demonstration. Likewise, a status called normal in a software test may not be the approved safe operating state of the physical process.

Include human interfaces. An alarm or maintenance instruction depends on the intended person's ability to notice, understand and act under actual work conditions. A screen demonstration in a quiet office does not establish visibility in the field or the feasibility of an action during an emergency. Identify the intended users and the circumstances needing validation. The actual employer and technical team determine suitable representative evaluation and the necessary practical safeguards.

Boundary ownership must remain clear after a subcontract handoff. If one supplier provides a sensor, another provides communications and a third provides the display, “the other vendor owns the alarm” is not a completed interface decision. Record which party defines the function, which party implements each part, who verifies the integration and who approves the operational response. The final evidence must connect the actual configuration across those parties rather than collecting unrelated component certificates.

lessons.title: Distinguish verification from validation
lessons.body:
Verification and validation answer different questions. Verification evaluates whether a product satisfies its stated requirements. Validation evaluates whether it is suitable for the intended use and stakeholder need. A product can pass a requirement check yet fail the intended job if the requirement was incomplete or if the evaluation omitted an important use condition. Keep both questions visible when deciding what a test or analysis actually demonstrates.

Choose evidence appropriate to the claim. Inspection can establish an observable attribute within its scope. Analysis can support a prediction using a justified model and inputs. A demonstration can show a behavior under stated conditions. A test can measure response using a controlled method. Those methods are not interchangeable labels for approval. A component inspection does not establish whole-system performance, and a simulation does not prove every physical installation condition. The qualified review team decides the necessary combination and the limits of each result.

Before accepting a verification record, match requirement, item, configuration, method and acceptance basis. Identify what was actually tested, which software or drawing revision applied, the relevant environment and the instruments or reference data used. A report lacking that identity may contain useful observations but cannot automatically close the intended requirement. Review deviations and anomalies rather than treating a pass stamp as a summary of every unresolved condition.

Use a fictional enclosure example. Requirement R-12 concerns the approved installed arrangement. A supplier report evaluates an earlier enclosure with a different cable-entry layout. The report is not necessarily false; it may be valid for its tested configuration. The reviewer records the difference and asks the technical owner whether existing evidence remains applicable or whether additional evaluation is needed. The reviewer does not infer equivalence from the shared product family name.

Treat acceptance as a decision supported by evidence, not as an adjective printed on a document. The decision should state the requirement or use condition covered, relevant limitations and remaining actions. A learner who can explain these distinctions has demonstrated knowledge; a qualified discipline reviewer must still assess actual design adequacy and the employer must still approve the real verification or validation activity. Do not perform live equipment tests to complete the course.

lessons.title: Trace the consequences of change
lessons.body:
A design change is a change in technical meaning, not merely a new file date. A different material, software revision, operating duty, layout, supplier or maintenance approach can affect requirements, interfaces and earlier evidence. Begin a change review by identifying the actual difference between the approved baseline and the proposal. “Equivalent replacement” is a claim requiring a technical basis; the procurement description alone does not establish it.

Follow dependencies outward from the changed item. Ask which calculations, drawings, protective functions, operating procedures, inspections, spare parts, training and acceptance records depend on its properties. A change can leave many items unaffected, but that conclusion must come from an appropriate review rather than from copying every earlier approval. Preserve unaffected evidence with its proper scope and identify exactly which evidence needs revision or re-evaluation.

Assess temporary changes with the same clarity about their boundaries. State the purpose, actual configuration, authorizing decision, responsible owner and conditions or duration of use. The employer's applicable process determines how they are controlled and ended. Do not let a temporary arrangement become the assumed permanent baseline because a work order remains open. Completion of an administrative task does not establish restoration of the physical or digital arrangement.

For a fictional dashboard change, the proposed edit converts a displayed quantity from litres to cubic metres. The arithmetic conversion is simple, but the interface review must consider the label, number of decimal places, connected reports and the user's existing instructions. A training slide showing the old units can create a new mismatch even if the conversion code is correct. The responsible team establishes and evaluates the actual change; the learner identifies its dependency chain without accessing a live system.

Where OSHA process safety management applies to the actual process, its change provisions address specific technical and safety considerations. Applicability must be determined from the real process and governing regime; the presence of an oilfield engineering service in the catalog does not establish coverage. The broader learning point is to connect change, affected evidence, instruction and accepted configuration. Neither this course nor a successful software download authorizes startup or return to service.

lessons.title: Keep technical authority and handover bounded
lessons.body:
Technical authority attaches to a defined duty and competence basis. A job title, course score or company administrator account does not establish authority to make every engineering decision. Identify the discipline and decision: preparation of a drawing, independent checking, specialist analysis, approval of a method, acceptance of a deviation and professional signing can require different responsibilities. One person's valid authority for one duty must not be expanded to an unrelated discipline by convenience.

Determine applicable professional requirements through the responsible jurisdiction and actual service. The Texas engineering board is one jurisdiction-specific reference, not proof that every catalog engineering or software service requires a Texas professional engineer. A competent applicability review must establish the regulated act, location, relevant exemptions or limits and acceptable evidence of authorization. The course does not issue a license, validate an individual credential or decide whether a specific project may legally proceed.

Prepare a technical handover that makes the accepted basis usable. Link the released documents and revisions, the intended operating or installation scope, the evidence accepted and any unresolved limitations. Separate an approved design package from an as-built record of what was actually installed. If installation differs, document and review the actual difference rather than silently treating a design drawing as an observation of the facility.

A qualification record also needs boundaries. State the task and discipline evaluated, the evidence reviewed or observed, the evaluator's relevant competence, the result and any limits or follow-up. A successful paper exercise can demonstrate reasoning about requirements or units. It cannot demonstrate field inspection technique, software commissioning behavior or the ability to perform a hazardous technical method. Arrange those separately using an approved safe evaluation plan and the appropriate assessor.

Close a review finding by inspecting its resolution. If a missing assumption is answered, verify which calculations and decisions depended on it. If a drawing is revised, verify that the released set and the receiving team use that revision. If an action is transferred, identify the receiving owner and the conditions limiting use until completion. These are useful engineering review skills, but the authority to accept actual design adequacy and authorize work remains with the properly designated technical and operating roles.

lessons.title: Worked case 1
lessons.body:
Case 1: a fictional equipment layout with a deceptively simple clearance calculation

A planning team proposes moving packaged unit U-7 through opening O-2 at North Creek's fictional training facility. No real move is planned. The supplied sketch lists the unit length as 2.4 metres and the opening width as 2,500 millimetres. A slide says “100 millimetres spare: installation accepted.” The project requirement instead calls for an approved installation route allowing the actual unit and the required handling and maintenance arrangements. The learner is the assigned design review coordinator, not the lifting planner or design approval authority.

First, reproduce the arithmetic without expanding its meaning. Converting 2.4 metres gives 2,400 millimetres. Subtracting from 2,500 gives 100 millimetres. That is the difference between two supplied nominal dimensions. It does not establish clearance along the whole route, orientation, projections, lifting equipment, packaging or the allowances required by the approved method. The review finding therefore identifies an unsupported installation conclusion, rather than calling the subtraction wrong.

Second, inspect input identity. The unit drawing is revision B, while the supplier's current package drawing is revision D. The reviewer cannot decide whether the physical envelope changed from the revision letters alone. They request the authorized comparison and the actual configuration intended for installation. They retain revision B as part of the submitted basis so a later reviewer can understand the original conclusion.

Third, trace interfaces and responsibilities. The civil designer owns the opening geometry, the equipment supplier owns the package definition and the appointed handling team owns its approved movement method within the agreed responsibilities. The coordinator brings the specific interface questions to those owners. They do not test the uncertainty by asking a crew to attempt the move.

Fourth, separate design acceptance and field confirmation. The technical team must establish appropriate geometry and method evidence; the actual site must then be checked through an approved competent process where required. A revised slide saying “reviewed” does not supply those observations. The supported closure would identify the accepted revisions, applicable route and method, the technical decisions and any remaining installation conditions.

The lesson is precise: retain the correct arithmetic, reject the unsupported inference, obtain the missing technical basis and keep the actual movement authorization separate. Passing this case neither qualifies a lifting planner nor approves any real clearance value.

lessons.title: Worked case 2
lessons.body:
Case 2: a fictional monitoring display passes a test but misses the intended user need

A training project changes a monitoring display from litres to cubic metres. The approved use description requires the assigned operator to distinguish current information from unavailable information and use the displayed quantity consistently with the current procedure. A developer demonstrates that the conversion produces 1.8 cubic metres from the fictional input of 1,800 litres. A reviewer is asked to accept the full change because the conversion is correct. No connection to an operational system is part of this exercise.

Begin by identifying the supported verification claim. Because 1,000 litres equals one cubic metre, the supplied conversion is arithmetically consistent. That verifies the particular conversion example under its stated assumptions. It does not establish every value, data path or installed configuration, and it does not validate whether the display meets the intended user's needs.

Next inspect the interface. The old report still labels the number as litres, while a revised screen labels it as cubic metres. The screen test says nothing about the report's meaning. The reviewers identify the inconsistent unit definitions as an interface defect and route it to the responsible change owners. They do not correct one screen and leave the report discrepancy as an undocumented user convention.

Then examine an omitted use condition. The demonstration uses a valid input throughout. It provides no evidence about the approved display behavior when information is unavailable or stale. The team must establish the intended behavior and appropriate verification or validation methods through the responsible technical and operating review. The learner does not invent a timeout, alarm setting or safe fallback value.

Finally consider the people and baseline. The operator instruction and the handover slide still show the earlier units. Even a technically correct display can create a use error if those materials no longer match the accepted configuration. The change review must address the affected instruction and suitable representative evaluation with the intended users, as well as any actual installation or startup controls required by the employer.

The decision is to preserve the valid conversion result as bounded evidence, retain the open interface and use-condition findings and obtain an integrated acceptance decision for the actual change. Calling the entire system failed would discard useful evidence; calling it accepted would outrun that evidence. The qualified technical authority must determine the necessary tests and evaluate actual results. The course records the learner's reasoning, not a software release approval.

lessons.title: Final assessment — evidence and technical authority
lessons.body: Answer twenty decisions applying the taught methods. Review each incorrect answer and explicitly acknowledge its explanation before continuing. The original score remains part of the record; completing remediation does not rewrite the first answer.

questions.prompt: Which requirement is ready for competent evaluation?

options.label: A bounded function with justified conditions and an identified acceptance method.
A promise that the system will always work.
A preferred product name with no intended duty.
The supplier logo on the cover.

questions.prompt: The supplied dimensions are 2.4 m and 2,500 mm. What does their difference establish?

options.label: The drawing revisions must match.
A nominal difference of 100 mm, with installation suitability still unproved.
The unit can safely be moved through the opening.
The handling method is approved.

questions.prompt: Two displays both show level, one as percent of span and one as percent of usable capacity. What is needed?

options.label: Using whichever value looks normal.
Treating matching labels as matching quantities.
An agreed quantity definition and interface interpretation.
Averaging the two percentages.

questions.prompt: What is validation principally asking?

options.label: Whether a document has a pass stamp.
Whether a calculation file opens.
Whether every component has a supplier certificate.
Whether the product suits the intended use and stakeholder need.

questions.prompt: A change converts a displayed quantity to cubic metres. Which items may need review?

options.label: Labels, linked reports, user instructions and the relevant configuration/evaluation evidence.
Only the arithmetic statement.
Only the purchase order.
No prior evidence because a change invalidates everything automatically.

questions.prompt: A course graduate is asked to sign an unrelated discipline design. What establishes authority?

options.label: The urgency of the project.
The actual discipline, designated duty and applicable competence/professional authorization.
Their online score alone.
Their administrator access.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes a constraint from a solution preference?

options.label: A preference needs no explanation once called a constraint.
All constraints can be ignored during a trade study.
A constraint has an established basis limiting available solutions.
A constraint is whatever product the first supplier sells.

questions.prompt: An assumed ambient condition is used in design reasoning. What must remain visible?

options.label: Only the final calculated number.
A statement that assumptions are always facts.
An unqualified guarantee that the installed site matches it.
Its source/status, dependent decisions and the person responsible for confirming it.

questions.prompt: Why assign a stable reference to a requirement?

options.label: To trace its source, implementation, revision and evaluation evidence.
To replace its actual content with a number.
To avoid discussing intended use.
To make any similarly numbered report acceptable.

questions.prompt: Can mass flow be treated as volume flow without additional information?

options.label: Yes, if both appear in a spreadsheet.
No; the quantities differ and conversion needs an appropriate basis such as density and conditions.
Yes, if the displayed numbers are close.
Yes, for every liquid.

questions.prompt: A spreadsheet completes successfully. What remains to review?

options.label: Only the color of its chart.
Only whether the author is available.
The intended physical question, model applicability, inputs, units and relevant limits.
Nothing; execution proves physical validity.

questions.prompt: Difference is defined as proposed minus permitted. A positive value means what?

options.label: It is automatically a safety margin.
The proposed quantity is lower.
The calculation grants approval.
The proposed quantity exceeds the stated permitted quantity under that convention.

questions.prompt: What belongs in an interface review?

options.label: The actual shared quantities, conditions, responsibilities and failure/use states.
Only each component supplier name.
Only the project invoice.
A statement that interfaces are somebody else’s responsibility.

questions.prompt: A component meets its own specification. What follows about system suitability?

options.label: No user validation can ever be useful.
It remains to be evaluated with the actual interfaces and intended system use.
The entire system is automatically suitable.
Every other component can be omitted from review.

questions.prompt: An office demonstration is readable. What additional question concerns field use?

options.label: Whether the screen can be photographed.
Whether readability removes all communication duties.
Whether intended users can perceive and act on the information under the relevant actual conditions.
Whether the demo used a large conference room.

questions.prompt: A report tests an earlier configuration. How should it be used?

options.label: Change the report date and accept it.
Discard it without looking at the difference.
Assume a shared family name proves equivalence.
Retain its valid scope and have competent reviewers assess applicability to the proposed configuration.

questions.prompt: What makes a verification record traceable?

options.label: Links among requirement, actual item/configuration, method, conditions and acceptance basis.
A pass stamp by itself.
A report number with no item identity.
A current file creation date.

questions.prompt: A conversion works at one supplied input. What is supported?

options.label: The operator’s full competence.
That bounded example, not unrestricted operation or all use conditions.
Every possible input and failure mode.
The current installed software configuration automatically.

questions.prompt: A temporary arrangement is still present after its authorization conditions end. What is needed?

options.label: Hiding it from the baseline.
Calling it permanent because production continued.
Review by the responsible authority of its actual state and permitted continuation or restoration.
Treating an open work order as an extension of approval.

questions.prompt: A changed material is described as equivalent. What supports that claim?

options.label: The description equivalent by itself.
Matching packaging color.
A lower purchase price.
A competent technical comparison against the actual requirements and affected evidence.

questions.prompt: A drawing is approved for design. Does it prove what was installed?

options.label: No; actual installation and any differences need appropriate competent confirmation.
Yes, design and as-built always mean the same thing.
Yes, if the file is a PDF.
Yes, if the drawing is newer than the invoice.

questions.prompt: Who decides applicable engineering licensure requirements?

options.label: The fact that Texas has an engineering board.
A competent applicability review using the actual duty and governing jurisdiction.
The course quiz automatically.
A catalog keyword alone.

questions.prompt: What should a practical qualification record identify?

options.label: Only the employee’s department.
Only a score with no task definition.
Actual task, evaluator competence, evidence/observations, result and limits.
Only course attendance.

questions.prompt: A requirement finding is answered by a revised assumption. What else needs checking?

options.label: Only whether an email was sent.
Nothing once the action is marked complete.
Every unrelated design must be redesigned automatically.
The calculations and decisions that depended on that assumption.

questions.prompt: Does OSHA process safety management apply to every catalog engineering service?

options.label: No; actual process coverage and governing requirements must be established.
Yes, the word engineering makes every process covered.
Yes, every software change is automatically covered.
No process could ever be covered.

questions.prompt: What does completing this course establish?

options.label: Permission to run live acceptance tests.
Recorded knowledge of the taught review reasoning, with actual design authority and practical competence still separately evidenced.
Unlimited design signing authority.
Approval of the fictional installation dimensions for real use.

courses.title: G67 — Electrical and instrument work-pack interpretation and commissioning evidence
courses.purpose: Interpret electrical/instrument work boundaries, reconcile technical records and review bounded commissioning claims without performing hazardous testing.

content.title: G67 — Electrical and instrument work-pack interpretation and commissioning evidence
content.description: Interpret electrical/instrument work boundaries, reconcile technical records and review bounded commissioning claims without performing hazardous testing.

explanations.G67_check1: The work description governs the interfaces; the service label does not remove a pressure connection.
explanations.G67_check2: A plausible typographical explanation is not traceability evidence.
explanations.G67_check3: A number and signature do not identify the technical criterion.
explanations.G67_check4: A test result applies to its actual configuration and exclusions.
explanations.G67_check5: Conflicting records require authorized verification, not an assumption or configuration action.
explanations.G67_check6: Related experience is background evidence; it is not proof of the different task skills.
explanations.G67_final1: These elements make the assignment and its boundary reviewable.
explanations.G67_final2: A drawing must be suited and current for the proposed use.
explanations.G67_final3: Explicit unknowns preserve uncertainty for technical resolution.
explanations.G67_final4: Consistent identifiers are useful but do not demonstrate physical performance.
explanations.G67_final5: Calibration supports the identified measurement claim, not every connected function.
explanations.G67_final6: Test purpose determines the evidence needed and the limits of its conclusion.
explanations.G67_final7: Acceptance needs a defined quantity and approved basis.
explanations.G67_final8: Desk interpretation does not confer hazardous electrical execution skills.
explanations.G67_final9: Position, isolation, verification and release are different evidence claims.
explanations.G67_final10: Category labels have no universal readiness meaning.
explanations.G67_final11: Technical equivalence requires an authorized basis, not visual similarity.
explanations.G67_final12: Original observations may reveal intermittent issues or method problems.
explanations.G67_final13: A correction should preserve the record history.
explanations.G67_final14: A bounded state tells the next role what remains undecided.
explanations.G67_final15: Use the actual equipment information and task limits; fictional course values do not establish operating limits.
explanations.G67_final16: The fictional mismatch remains unresolved until identity evidence is supplied.
explanations.G67_final17: A corrected pack is preparation evidence, not execution evidence.
explanations.G67_final18: The simulator and missing cable limit what has been demonstrated.
explanations.G67_final19: Lack of closure evidence cannot support a verified restoration claim.
explanations.G67_final20: Original scores remain recorded and practical capability and release remain separate.

lessons.title: Start here: scope and completion
lessons.body:
This course teaches the document interpretation and planning decisions needed for electrical and instrument work-pack interpretation and commissioning evidence. It is intended for the assigned roles listed in the course record. A service catalog label is a starting point for identifying a task; it is not evidence that every employee performs every specialist activity associated with that label. Work through the six lessons, six checks, two fictional worked cases and twenty final questions. The exercises use paper records only and require no equipment operation, live connection or hazardous exposure.

All twenty-six answers must be recorded. Complete every lesson and answer every question correctly, or review and explicitly acknowledge the question-specific remediation. Retain the original selections and first-attempt score alongside corrected answers and the remediation record. Completion documents this knowledge component only. It does not close any unobserved performance requirement or employer authorization.

lessons.title: 1. Translate an electrical request into a bounded assignment
lessons.body:
Electrical work must be described by its interaction with equipment, not by the worker's department. Installing an office application, replacing an enclosed peripheral, connecting an instrument to a process, opening an electrical enclosure and commissioning a protective circuit are different assignments. Write a task sentence with an action, identified asset and intended result. “Support generator G-4” is too vague. “Review the maintenance record and drawings for the proposed G-4 inspection without opening equipment” defines a desk role and makes the next permission boundary visible.

Build an interface list from the work request. Include the electrical supply, any independent control supply, battery or stored-energy connection, remote commands, process connection and equipment that depends on the circuit. This is a document review, not an instruction to locate conductors or perform isolation. Record an interface as unknown when the records do not establish it. A blank field falsely suggests that the interface does not exist; an explicit unknown creates a technical question that an accountable person can answer.

Read drawings from the title block before reading symbols. Match the equipment identifier, drawing purpose, revision, approval state and sheet references to the proposed task. A conceptual single-line drawing explains relationships but may omit the detail needed for a maintenance method. An installation diagram is not automatically an approved record of the present installation. Compare the task's asset label with the asset register and the work order. Similar names do not establish identity, especially after equipment replacement or renumbering.

Classify each proposed activity as document review, supervised learning, authorized technical execution or release decision. Then assign the role that actually owns it. A person can be qualified for one circuit or task and outside their demonstrated scope for another. The cited OSHA training provision connects training to job assignments and distinguishes additional skills for qualified persons; it does not convert an online score into those skills.

Desk exercise: a purchase order says “instrument service,” while the attached method includes opening a control panel and disconnecting a pressure impulse line. Mark both interfaces, request the appropriate electrical and process method owners, and retain the narrow desk-review task until the execution scope is settled.

lessons.title: 2. Reconcile drawings, asset records and change history
lessons.body:
A defensible electrical work pack distinguishes what the documents say from what has been confirmed about the installation. Start a discrepancy table with four columns: source and revision, stated condition, conflicting evidence, and decision owner. Do not silently change an engineering drawing to make the work request appear consistent. A marked-up review copy can identify a question while preserving the approved baseline and showing that the mark is not an installation instruction.

For an instrument loop, a loop drawing, device data sheet, input/output list and cause-and-effect description answer different questions. The loop drawing describes connections; the data sheet identifies intended device characteristics; the input/output list associates signals with the control system; the cause-and-effect record describes the intended response to conditions. A matching tag across all four supports traceability, but matching tags alone do not prove that the device, wiring or logic currently performs as intended. Missing revision alignment is a reason to seek engineering reconciliation before using the pack for technical work.

A calibration certificate can establish a bounded measurement result for an identified instrument under stated conditions. It does not prove correct installation, suitability for a hazardous location, functional operation of an entire protective loop or authority to energize equipment. Similarly, a purchase invoice for a replacement module is not evidence that the replacement has approved characteristics. Record what each evidence item actually supports and what it cannot support.

Read the change history as a chain. Identify the approved change request, affected documents, implementation evidence, testing evidence and release decision. A closed maintenance ticket with no referenced test record may establish administrative closure only. Where a field modification appears in a photograph but not in the current drawings, the reviewer should name the discrepancy and ask the designated technical owner for disposition; the reviewer should not deduce a new connection scheme from the photograph.

Desk exercise: the input/output list refers to PT-24, a certificate refers to PT-42, and the work order says “pressure transmitter.” The correct result is not a clever guess about transposed digits. Record that the certificate cannot yet be assigned to the task asset, request identity evidence and keep the verification claim open.

lessons.title: 3. Review a test plan without inventing a test method
lessons.body:
A test plan should explain the question being answered before listing instruments. Distinguish an inspection for visible condition, a measurement of a component, a functional test of a loop and commissioning of an integrated system. Each supports a different conclusion. A satisfactory component measurement cannot establish that the entire system responds correctly, and an integrated demonstration cannot supply a missing component suitability assessment.

On a desk review copy, identify the test object, approved configuration, purpose, prerequisites, responsible technical personnel, controlling procedure and acceptance source. Locate how the plan treats people and equipment outside the test boundary. Commissioning can introduce temporary supplies, simulated signals or changed operating states; those features need explicit technical review and operational coordination. This course does not teach connections, test voltages, live measurements, approach distances or switching sequences. Those belong to qualified personnel using an approved method for the actual equipment and applicable rules.

Acceptance criteria must come from an identified approved source. A spreadsheet with an unexplained green cell is not an acceptance basis. Ask whether the criterion is a manufacturer specification, engineered requirement, approved procedure or governing standard adopted for the job. Record units and the definition of the quantity being assessed. A result written as “4.2” is not interpretable until the quantity and unit are known. Do not use this lesson to calculate a hazardous operating limit.

Review measurement assurance without pretending to be the test technician. The planned instrument should have an identity and evidence appropriate to its intended use, including the relevant range or function and current condition. A calibration sticker cannot establish that every measurement function is suitable. Ask how the method handles a suspect instrument or result and who determines the consequence for previous results. The plan should retain original readings, test conditions and deviations rather than only a pass mark.

Desk exercise: a loop test form has a signature and no stated acceptance source. Write “result recorded; acceptance basis not demonstrated.” Request the approved criterion and technical review. Do not supply a customary value from memory, a different site or an internet example.

lessons.title: 4. Understand safe-state and commissioning evidence
lessons.body:
“Off,” “isolated,” “de-energized,” “tested” and “released” are distinct claims. A switch position is a position indication. An isolation record describes a controlled arrangement. Evidence that an appropriately qualified person verified the relevant condition supports a bounded safe-state claim at a time and place. Release is a decision made under the site's authority after its prerequisites are met. A desk reviewer should use precise language so that one claim is not accidentally promoted into another.

Identify which procedure governs the work and whether its scope actually includes the task. General hazardous-energy rules have exclusions and sector differences, so a familiar lockout form should not be treated as proof that one legal regime applies universally. The employer must establish the applicable electrical and energy-control arrangements. The reviewer can check whether the pack identifies the responsible people, equipment boundary, relevant energy interfaces and restoration controls without issuing an isolation or instructing a switching sequence.

Commissioning documentation should distinguish a temporary test condition from the intended normal configuration. A successful demonstration with a temporary simulator may prove the simulated part of the test while leaving the field sensor or final element unverified. Read the test boundaries and record exclusions. Temporary jumpers, disabled functions or substituted inputs are not acceptable merely because a test form is signed. Their use, control and removal require the appropriate technical and operational authority; this course does not authorize creating or removing them.

Read completion records for unresolved items. A punch-list category must have an approved meaning on that project. Do not assume that every open item is cosmetic or that an unfamiliar category permits startup. Locate the named owner and release conditions for each unresolved issue. A technical authority may approve a defined disposition, but the record must preserve its limits rather than replacing the original concern with “accepted.”

Desk exercise: a commissioning record reports a passed controller response using a simulated input, while the field device installation is incomplete. Write two separate findings: the recorded simulated response and the unverified field path. The complete loop has not been established by the available record.

lessons.title: 5. Interpret results, deviations and restoration records
lessons.body:
Technical records are useful when another authorized person can reconstruct what was tested and what remains uncertain. Review whether the result identifies the equipment, date, procedure revision, test configuration, instrument identities, relevant conditions, original observations and person performing the work. The purpose is not to add signatures for appearance. Each element connects a claim to the actual event and prevents the result being reused for a different asset or configuration.

A deviation is a departure from the approved method or expected condition. Its significance depends on the task and the technical basis. A reviewer should describe it specifically: “the specified test point was inaccessible and was not measured” is more useful than “minor issue.” If a technician substituted a method, find the recorded approval and the limits of the substitute evidence. Do not assume equivalent results because both methods produce a number with the same unit.

Separate data correction from result alteration. A demonstrated transcription mistake can be corrected through the controlled record process with the original entry, reason, author and date retained. A surprising reading cannot be deleted because the next reading looks better. The technical reviewer decides whether repeated measurements, equipment condition or method validity affect acceptance. Original evidence protects learning as well as accountability; it allows an apparently intermittent problem to be recognized later.

Restoration needs its own evidence. The pack should identify what was temporarily disconnected, inhibited, substituted or removed during the approved work and how the responsible personnel verified the intended final configuration. This is a record-review requirement, not permission to reconnect or energize anything. A clean work area and closed ticket do not establish functional readiness. Operating release remains with the authority assigned by the employer and site.

Desk exercise: a completed test sheet says “all restored,” but the change log lists a temporary alarm suppression with no closure record. Carry that exact conflict into the handover. Ask the authorized owner to verify disposition against the approved configuration and operating conditions. Do not change the log yourself or infer closure from the absence of an alarm.

lessons.title: 6. Build a task-specific competence and handover pack
lessons.body:
A competence pack connects a person to a defined task and evidence of capability. Start with the proposed duties and equipment rather than a folder of certificates. For each duty, identify necessary technical knowledge, supervised experience, observed practical performance and any applicable legal or contractual credential. Record who assessed the person, the assessor's relevant scope, conditions of assessment, performance criteria, outcome and limitations. An electrical trade credential, an instrument manufacturer course and an employer designation answer different questions and should not be collapsed into one badge.

Design a safe desk assessment for the reviewer role. Give the learner fictional drawings, a data sheet, a test plan and a result form containing a traceability conflict. Ask them to identify the conflict, describe the unsupported claim and route the question to the correct technical owner. Assess the quality of their reasoning and record interpretation. Do not mark the learner qualified for exposed electrical work because they completed this paper exercise.

The assessor determines how the person demonstrates the necessary skills without uncontrolled exposure. The scope may include equipment identification, correct use of approved methods, interpretation of results, management of unexpected conditions and controlled restoration. This course does not prescribe an assessment involving live parts, and a supervisor should not create one merely to make training realistic.

A handover should give the incoming team a usable state. State the asset, work completed, configuration covered by the evidence, limitations, unresolved deviations, temporary arrangements and release authority. Reference exact documents rather than attaching an unexplained pile of files. An incoming person should be able to distinguish “test complete awaiting review” from “accepted for the defined purpose” and from “authorized for operation.”

Desk exercise: an instrument technician has demonstrated calibration of one transmitter family but is assigned protective-loop commissioning on another platform. Record the existing evidence as relevant background, identify the new loop and platform skills, and arrange task-specific assessment and authorization. Preserve what is known without manufacturing either a blanket qualification or a blanket rejection.

lessons.title: Worked fictional case 1: the replacement transmitter package
lessons.body:
Fictional facts: Cedar Yard requests replacement of pressure transmitter PT-17 during a planned maintenance window. The planner receives a work order naming PT-17, loop drawing revision C, a data sheet revision E, a calibration certificate naming PT-71 and a proposed functional test based on revision C. No worker is being asked to open equipment as part of this exercise. The records are deliberately inconsistent.

First, the reviewer creates an evidence table. The work order establishes the requested asset identity. The drawing describes a loop at revision C, while the data sheet describes device requirements at revision E. The certificate currently supports an identified PT-71 result, not PT-17. The reviewer records all three conflicts without deciding that the certificate has a typographical error. This preserves the actual evidence and avoids attaching a plausible but unsupported certificate to the replacement.

Second, the reviewer separates device service from electrical and process interfaces. Replacing a transmitter may involve wiring, a pressure connection and effects on the monitored process. The work pack must identify the approved methods and competent roles for the interfaces actually included. The planner does not infer that an instrument-service vendor is authorized for every electrical or pressure activity. The requested work window also needs coordination with the operating owner because a measurement or protective function may be unavailable.

Third, the reviewer examines the proposed test's conclusion. The test form demonstrates an intended controller response but does not state whether it includes the installed field device. The reviewer requests a clear boundary and acceptance source. If the method uses a simulated input, its evidence must be described as simulated response evidence; the untested portion cannot disappear from the final claim.

The fictional technical owner later supplies the correct asset record, an approved revision reconciliation and a controlled correction confirming which certificate belongs to PT-17. The approved test plan identifies its scope and responsible qualified personnel. The reviewer can now mark the document conflicts resolved with references. This does not mean the physical work has happened. Execution, original results, restoration verification and operating release remain separate future records.

Final worked decision: the initial package is not ready to support an execution or full-loop acceptance claim. The useful deliverable is a specific discrepancy list and a corrected, traceable pack. The residuals are the actual personnel's qualifications, approved isolation/process method, observed task performance, completed test evidence and authorized release. The paper exercise closes none of those residuals.

lessons.title: Worked fictional case 2: a passed cabinet test and an open suppression
lessons.body:
Fictional facts: West Bend's commissioning summary says “panel complete, all tests passed.” A detailed sheet shows controller response tested using a simulator. The field sensor cable is listed as incomplete. A separate log records temporary alarm suppression, but the closure column is blank. A supervisor asks the document reviewer to change the summary to “ready for operation” because the display looks normal.

The reviewer starts with the conclusion being requested. Readiness for operation is broader than a passed controller test. The simulator record supports only the response within its stated test boundary. It does not verify the incomplete cable or installed sensor path. A normal display is an observation at one time, not evidence of the full protective function. The reviewer writes these distinctions in the review note and retains the original test report unchanged.

Next, the reviewer reconciles the suppression log. A blank closure field does not prove the suppression remains active, but it also does not prove it has been removed. The correct finding is “disposition not established from the available record.” The designated technical and operating owners must determine actual state using their approved process. The reviewer neither accesses the controller nor tries to restore a setting. Document access does not confer configuration authority.

The reviewer then reads the project's punch-list rules. The cable item has no approved release disposition, and no responsible person has accepted its limitation for the proposed use. The summary therefore cannot honestly support an unrestricted readiness statement. If an authority later approves a defined restricted use, that decision must specify scope and conditions; the reviewer must not describe it as a completed test of the missing field path.

For handover, the reviewer records the controller test reference, simulator boundary, incomplete field installation, unresolved suppression disposition and named decision owners. The team schedules qualified completion and verification under the established commissioning plan. No hazardous demonstration is performed to satisfy the desk exercise.

Final worked decision: preserve the passed test as bounded valid evidence, reject the unsupported expansion of its conclusion, and keep operating release pending its actual prerequisites. This approach protects useful evidence while preventing administrative optimism from becoming a false electrical safety claim.

lessons.title: Start here: scope and completion
lessons.body:
This course teaches the document interpretation and planning decisions needed for hvac and refrigerant service principles, scope and acceptance. It is intended for the assigned roles listed in the course record. A service catalog label is a starting point for identifying a task; it is not evidence that every employee performs every specialist activity associated with that label. Work through the six lessons, six checks, two fictional worked cases and twenty final questions. The exercises use paper records only and require no equipment operation, live connection or hazardous exposure.

All twenty-six answers must be recorded. Complete every lesson and answer every question correctly, or review and explicitly acknowledge the question-specific remediation. Retain the original selections and first-attempt score alongside corrected answers and the remediation record. Completion documents this knowledge component only. It does not close any unobserved performance requirement or employer authorization.

lessons.title: 1. Identify the actual HVAC task and refrigerant boundary
lessons.body:
An HVAC service request can describe many different jobs: reviewing comfort complaints, inspecting an accessible filter, servicing an electrical drive, assessing airflow, opening a refrigerant circuit or disposing of equipment. Begin with the exact activity and appliance. A desk designer does not become a refrigerant technician merely because the drawing includes a chiller; a worker who connects gauges may cross a refrigerant-service boundary even if the purchase order calls the task inspection.

Create a task inventory with the appliance identifier, manufacturer/model, installed location, stated refrigerant, service purpose and proposed actions. Mark information from a nameplate or approved asset record separately from information inferred from an old invoice. Refrigerants and equipment can change during approved modifications; the reviewer should not choose a gas by appearance, hose color or a remembered model family. A contradictory record is a technical query, not an invitation to sample or connect equipment during training.

The EPA Section 608 page is a United States example of function-specific certification. It distinguishes equipment-related certification categories and identifies certain refrigerant activities. Read it to understand why HVAC trained is not enough to establish scope, while avoiding a blanket claim that every HVAC worker needs the same credential. Motor vehicle air conditioning and other regimes require their own applicability review. Credentials also do not establish electrical qualification, pressure-system competence or permission to disturb an occupied building's ventilation.

Write the desk role clearly. Review asset AC-12's service pack and identify unresolved scope questions permits document interpretation. It does not authorize attaching gauges, breaking a joint, testing a live circuit, changing a controller or deciding a charge quantity. Each proposed activity needs its actual method, personnel and approvals. In a paper exercise, a general building-maintenance certificate accompanies refrigerant removal work. Request equipment-appropriate credential evidence where applicable and separate observed service skills. A generic badge cannot establish this duty.

lessons.title: 2. Read appliance and refrigerant information as a linked set
lessons.body:
An appliance file should connect identity, design information, service history and current condition. Start with the identifier and model, then match manufacturer instructions, approved modifications, refrigerant records and service reports. Do not treat a manual for a similar model as a substitute without appropriate technical determination. Some instructions cover multiple variants; identify which configuration is actually present before applying a table or requirement.

Read a safety data sheet for what it is: substance hazard and handling information for the identified product. It is not an appliance service manual, an engineering determination that a refrigerant is suitable, or a recovery-machine compatibility approval. Record the exact product identity and whether it agrees with the asset file. If a cylinder label and service record disagree, the issue is unresolved identity. Preserve both observations and ask the responsible specialist for controlled disposition; this course does not teach identification by experimental mixing or release.

Build a compatibility question list. It may include the appliance's approved refrigerant, service-equipment suitability, cylinder identification, lubricant/material compatibility and treatment of uncertain or contaminated material. Qualified technical personnel use actual manufacturer information and applicable requirements to answer it. The reviewer checks that answers have sources and owners rather than supplying chemistry or pressure limits from memory.

Service history can reveal unresolved work. Repeated additions without a clear diagnosis may be relevant to technical review, but the planner should not diagnose a leak solely from invoices. Distinguish an observation, a technician's interpretation and a confirmed repair. A line saying system topped up does not explain cause, amount validity or final condition. Record what the evidence actually says and request missing details.

Paper exercise: the register names one refrigerant, the compressor replacement record names another and the current report says gas added. The file does not establish a coherent current configuration. Create a discrepancy entry with all three sources and ask the responsible HVAC authority to reconcile the approved configuration before method selection.

lessons.title: 3. Review service planning without prescribing a circuit procedure
lessons.body:
A service plan should identify the result sought: diagnosis, repair, recovery, replacement, commissioning or disposal. These purposes are not interchangeable. A diagnostic observation can support a maintenance recommendation without establishing a repaired circuit. A recovery record can document material handling without proving an appliance ready for operation. Read the planned conclusion before checking whether the listed evidence supports it.

At desk level, review the work boundary, manufacturer method, responsible personnel, equipment identity, environmental handling arrangements and building operational interface. Ask who owns electrical isolation, pressure control, ventilation changes and occupant communication where those interfaces apply. Do not assume the HVAC technician holds every associated qualification. Do not add irrelevant requirements to a purely documentary assignment either. Connect each real interface with an accountable competent role.

The plan should explain how refrigerant identity and destination remain traceable. Review whether proposed equipment and containers are identified and supported by relevant suitability evidence. This is not instruction to select cylinder fill levels, connect recovery hoses, evacuate circuits, charge appliances or set pressures. No universal sequence in this course is suitable for every refrigerant and appliance combination.

Look for abnormal-condition decisions. A useful plan identifies who decides what happens when asset identity is uncertain, a component differs from the manual, material is suspect or planned verification cannot be completed. The reviewer should see a disposition route, preservation of evidence and a clear limitation on the result. Technician to use judgment does not supply a technical basis for an unreviewed substitution.

Paper exercise: a method lists recover, repair, recharge and commission with no appliance-specific reference or acceptance source. Identify the four intended outcomes and request referenced methods and evidence for each. Do not fill the gap with an internet recipe or guessed charge amount. The appropriate technical authority must approve the actual service arrangements before execution evidence can exist.

lessons.title: 4. Interpret measurements and material records
lessons.body:
An HVAC report contains observations taken under particular conditions. Read the asset, configuration, date, operating state and measurement basis before interpreting numbers. A temperature reading from one location cannot establish the condition of an entire building, just as a pressure observation cannot establish every aspect of appliance safety. The report must say what was measured, where, with what instrument and for what decision. Units and context belong with the result.

Distinguish test results from acceptance. A manufacturer requirement, approved commissioning specification or adopted project criterion supplies the basis for a technical conclusion. The technician's measurement is evidence considered against that basis. A green tick without the criterion source is an unsupported acceptance claim. The reviewer may identify that omission; they should not invent a criterion by comparing unrelated equipment or selecting a familiar value from memory.

Measurement assurance has scope. A thermometer's calibration evidence should match its intended function and range; a sticker alone cannot establish suitability for every purpose. An instrument outside its demonstrated use or in suspect condition needs competent disposition. Ask how affected results will be evaluated, rather than simply replacing the instrument and declaring previous measurements valid.

For material records, check whether quantities and units can be reconciled within the approved process. A discrepancy such as incompatible units or an unidentified container needs explanation by responsible personnel. Do not infer an acceptable mass balance or allowable loss from this course. Reporting and material accounting depend on actual equipment, substances, activities and jurisdiction. Original records should remain available when corrections are made.

Paper exercise: a report says within specification but gives no model-specific reference and no operating conditions. Write that a measurement may have been recorded while acceptance has not been demonstrated in the file. Request the technical basis and conditions. This is more accurate than calling the appliance defective or compliant without evidence. The document reviewer identifies the unsupported conclusion; the assigned technical authority interprets the full result.

A refrigeration-cycle diagram helps technicians avoid one-cause assumptions. The evaporator absorbs heat from the cooled space; the compressor provides the pressure difference needed for circulation; the condenser rejects heat; the metering device regulates the transition toward the evaporator. Reduced cooling can arise from airflow, heat exchange, controls or refrigerant-circuit conditions. On paper, trace air and heat paths separately from refrigerant flow. If a fictional report says a filter is obstructed and the room is warm, the obstruction is evidence of an airflow issue, not proof of a refrigerant shortage. Label the supported observation and competing hypotheses, then identify which approved diagnostic evidence a qualified technician would need. Do not add refrigerant as a substitute for diagnosis.

lessons.title: 5. Plan maintenance interfaces and return to service
lessons.body:
HVAC work can affect people away from the appliance. An occupied control room may depend on cooling or ventilation; a storage area may contain temperature-sensitive contents; a food or care facility may have hygiene requirements. Identify the actual consequence of taking the system out of service. Do not assume all comfort equipment is safety critical, but do not dismiss a critical dependency because the equipment resembles an ordinary air conditioner.

A planning record identifies affected users, the operating owner, permitted service conditions, temporary arrangements and who communicates changes. Temporary fans, portable cooling or altered ventilation can introduce electrical, air-quality and access issues. Their approval requires appropriate technical and site review. This lesson teaches identification of dependencies and evidence routes, not design of emergency ventilation or selection of substitute equipment.

Return to service is a distinct decision. Review physical completion, controlled material handling, final configuration, relevant verification and unresolved defects. An invoice marked paid establishes a commercial event, not technical readiness. A service technician may hold authority for a defined technical conclusion while the building or process owner controls use. Record those roles rather than assuming one signature covers both.

Disposal and replacement need traceability. Removing an appliance from the register should connect to the actual disposition record, including material handling where required. A missing appliance is not proof that refrigerant was appropriately managed. The paperwork reviewer requests service/disposal evidence without opening a retired appliance to investigate.

Paper exercise: a chiller is repaired, but agreed post-repair verification is deferred because an area is inaccessible. Work may be physically complete while technical acceptance remains limited. Record the deferred verification and named decision owner. Any approved interim use retains its scope and conditions; it cannot be rewritten as unrestricted completed commissioning. The next shift needs to know the specific unverified area and the agreed owner of that remaining decision, rather than receiving a reassuring but unsupported all-good message.

lessons.title: 6. Match vendor evidence and practical assessments to duties
lessons.body:
Evaluate vendor capability against the actual service offered. Identify the person performing regulated or specialist activities, not only the company logo. Where a credential is required, verify its equipment/task category and acceptable issuing evidence. A credential is one capability element, not proof of proficiency on every appliance, refrigerant or service method.

Review manufacturer or method-specific instruction and relevant experience. Ask what appliance family, refrigerant type, recovery equipment, diagnostic method and commissioning task were included. A person skilled at one type may need additional instruction and assessment for another. The gap statement should describe the new requirement specifically. Needs HVAC training is too vague to select an assessor or judge evidence.

It should address assigned service skills, equipment identification, approved documentation, material control, result interpretation and handover. This course supplies no hazardous demonstration recipe.

For the desk planner, use a fictional document set. Ask the learner to detect a refrigerant identity conflict, identify missing acceptance evidence and distinguish a credential from observed method capability. Score reasoning and source traceability. This assesses a useful planning skill while preserving the boundary between paper review and service execution.

Preserve unresolved configuration, operational and jurisdiction questions. Completion can satisfy this knowledge lesson after correct responses or recorded remediation. It cannot supply missing appliance-specific observation, technical approval or building release. Keep each residual attached to a named owner so that a general course completion cannot accidentally close it.

lessons.title: Worked fictional case 1: a contradictory chiller file
lessons.body:
Fictional facts: Meadow Services investigates poor cooling on CH-8. The purchase order says routine HVAC check. The method includes attaching gauges and removing refrigerant. The register lists refrigerant R-A, while a replacement invoice mentions R-B. The vendor submits a general mechanical-safety course and service brochure. No learner connects equipment in this exercise.

The planner identifies actual proposed activities: diagnostic review, refrigerant-circuit service and relevant electrical/operational interfaces. Routine does not remove those activities. The refrigerant identity is recorded as unresolved, citing both records. The planner does not choose R-A because it is in the register or R-B because the invoice is newer. The responsible HVAC authority must reconcile the approved configuration.

The safety course supports only the knowledge taught. It is not an equipment-appropriate refrigerant credential where required; the brochure is not observed service competence. The planner requests the proposed technician's applicable credential, appliance/method instruction and practical evidence. Electrical or pressure duties are separately matched to qualified roles.

The method proposes service without the actual manufacturer reference, equipment suitability evidence or acceptance basis. The planner requests those sources rather than adding generic pressures or charge quantities. Material identity and destination remain part of the pack. The building owner is identified because CH-8 serves an occupied records room with an agreed cooling requirement.

In the fictional resolution, an approved modification record establishes configuration. The vendor supplies personnel evidence and a method for the actual model and equipment. Planned verification has a defined acceptance source, and the building owner approves maintenance conditions. The pack supports the next controlled step; it does not show service has occurred.

Final decision: initially the proposal cannot support execution readiness or finished repair. The desk deliverable is reconciled scope and traceable evidence. Residuals remain actual practical service, original readings, material records, technical acceptance and operating handover. Obtain them from real work under the approved arrangement. A corrected document must never be substituted for an observed field result.

lessons.title: Worked fictional case 2: an invoice with incomplete verification
lessons.body:
Fictional facts: North Archive replaces an HVAC component. The invoice says repair complete; a sheet says temperatures normal with no measurement locations, conditions or acceptance source. A technician notes that verification of one occupied zone was deferred. The owner asks the planner to mark the entire system commissioned.

The planner separates three claims. The invoice supports commercial completion. The sheet reports some observations. Full commissioning is not established because context is missing and verification was explicitly deferred. The planner preserves these distinctions rather than claiming either nothing happened or everything passed.

The planner requests the approved commissioning basis and original observations. The question is not whether a temperature sounds normal; it is what the measurement was intended to prove under actual conditions. The missing zone remains unverified. The planner does not invent a criterion from a comfort article or conduct an improvised measurement to close paperwork.

The operating owner considers any defined interim arrangement through the site's authority. If approved, its conditions must be separate from outstanding commissioning evidence. Limited use does not convert an unmeasured zone into a passed test. The planner carries the distinction into the maintenance register and incoming handover.

The fictional vendor later supplies original readings and the manufacturer/project basis for assessed zones. The deferred zone is scheduled for competent verification. The planner links evidence to the asset and retains the initial limitation until missing results and technical disposition arrive. The original entry is not deleted for a cleaner report.

Final decision: record completed component work and bounded verified results, with the deferred zone and acceptance review open. Exact residuals are zone verification, competent technical acceptance and final operating conditions. A paper-course pass, paid invoice and normal display cannot satisfy them. The handoff identifies the zone and responsible owner so that an incoming planner can continue without guessing what the initial service report excluded.
